(704)   Network effects of network carriers
(705)   Evidence in the file suggests that network carriers such as the Parties, and other large
          airlines that operate hubs in the EEA (e.g., Air France-KLM, IAG etc.) benefit from
        network  effects  at  their hub  airports, which  facilitate  entering on  routes and
        expanding on certain routes, while providing disincentives to enter or expand on
         others.
(706)   Although the Parties contest that network effects and/or economies of scope can act
        as a barrier to entry, they concede that network carriers do not have incentives to fly
       on routes not connected to their hubs.860 Moreover, evidence in the Commission’s
           file suggests that these network effects affect the airlines’ choice of airport of
        operation and could result in network carriers choosing to fly from more expensive
         airports to benefit from these network effects. In particular, a report submitted by
        Lufthansa regarding competition between Brussels International (Zaventem) and
        Brussels Charleroi airports reads: […].861 However, […] which shows the relevance
        of the network and the way the airport choice  is focused on ensuring network
          benefits.862
(707)   In this context, network effects also constitute a barrier to entry on the overlapping
         routes for network carriers that do not operate a hub at either end of the route,
        because such an entry would not be consistent with the latter’s business strategy.
        This has been confirmed by market participants in the course of the Commission’s
        market investigation, such as Air France-KLM which “does not anticipate entering
       on any  direct  routes  between  Italy and Germany,  Belgium,  Austria  and/or
        Switzerland since those are not relevant for its strategic network planning. In this
         context, AFKLM is more interested on routes between Italy and its hubs in France
       and the Netherlands”;863 and Air Europa which explains that the “company  is
        focussed in [its] hub in MAD, so not interested in new routes between Italy and
       Germany, Austria, Belgium and Switzerland”.864
(708)   Contrary to the Parties arguments in the Response to the SO, even if these barriers
         are related to the “outset of a company’s strategy”, e.g. Air France-KLM not having
       hubs or bases in Rome or Milan, they still indicate that the lack of an established
         position by Air France KLM in Rome or Milan is a barrier which results in very low
         likelihood of entry.865

9.1.4.5. Lack of entry on routes
(710)  As explained in paragraph (3) above Lufthansa has acquired a number of airlines,
        including three large formerly national network carriers in the past. Notably, SWISS
         in 2005, and Brussels Airlines and Austrian Airlines in 2009. In addition, Lufthansa
         also acquired the German airline Eurowings in 2005.866
(711)   The Commission considers that the barriers to entry and expansion which prevailed
        following these acquisitions on routes within the DACHB area and specifically
       between the origin and destination pairs which were the focus of these transactions
      may be indicative, at least to some extent, of the competitive dynamics likely to
         prevail post-Transaction. The Commission’s analysis indicates that following the
         acquisition of a national carrier by Lufthansa, barriers to entry and expansion on
         routes between the core countries of Lufthansa and the country where the acquired
         entity has a significant presence appear to increase to a significant extent, which has
          led, in turn, to a deterioration of competition.
(712)    First, the Commission has analysed market shares and has identified entry and exit
        events by competitors of Lufthansa (including network and LCC/ULCC carriers) in
        order to understand to what extent the presence of Lufthansa and in particular the
         acquisition of these carriers was generally followed by entry of its competitors.867
(713)  As a result of  this analysis, the Commission has observed that Lufthansa has
         consistently maintained high market shares on all these routes. In fact, the only route
       where a competitor of Lufthansa is currently present is the Brussels-Vienna route,
       where Ryanair competes with Lufthansa from the secondary / regional airport CRL
         in the Brussels end of the route and flew to VIE on the Vienna route. The reason for
          this presence is likely the strong presence of Ryanair on both ends of the route. On
           all other routes analysed by the Commission, currently there are no competitors
         present.
(714)   In addition, entry events between the relevant origins and destinations are scarce and
         in the vast majority of the cases short-lived. While some entry events have occurred
       on the routes in the past, all the entrants were LCC (easyJet) or ULCC (Ryanair or
       Wizz Air) carriers which usually compete from secondary  / regional airports. In
         addition, the average length of these entries is between 3 and 4 IATA Seasons.868
(715)   Second, the Commission has analysed aggregate annual market shares for all direct
          flights between country pairs in the DACHB region, as set out in Figure 63 to
        Figure 68. This analysis shows that Lufthansa play a very strong, if not dominant

(722)   Contrary to the Parties’ arguments, the Commission is taking all relevant elements

        following the acquisitions of SWISS, Brussels Airways, Austrian Airways and
       Eurowings  to be  at  least informative of the post-Transaction scenario (where
        Lufthansa will expand its hubs to Rome (FCO) and gain a significant presence in
       Milan (LIN), rather than a clear and highly likely blueprint of the effects of the
         Transaction. Moreover, the Commission does not solely rely on Lufthansa’s market
         position in DACHB to justify its concerns on the effects of the Transaction, instead it
        conducted its analysis based on several facts that are specific to this Transaction
            (i.e., market  investigation,  regression  analysis and  in-depth  internal document
        review) and considers that the current competitive dynamics in DACHB at least
       show that the past-acquisitions of Lufthansa do not contradict  its analyses and
        conclusions on the effects of the Transaction.

        context of internal documents do not change the assessment of the Commission. As
       an example, the fact that flights which are highly profitable for Lufthansa may be

        Lufthansa’s operations within the DACHB region and  in  particular on routes
       between its hubs are [Details on financials], indicating that it faces lower competition
        than on other operations.875
9.1.5.   Evidence on actual entry and expansion
(724)   Based on the framework for the assessment of entry and expansion described in
         section 7.1.3, the Commission’s assessment of actual entry and expansion in the
         current case is presented in the following paragraphs.
(725)   The market investigation did not identify new entry or expansion on any of the
        overlap routes by existing carriers that could be considered as likely, timely and
         sufficient to restrain any potential anti-competitive effects of the Transaction.876
(726)   Nevertheless, in their response to the SO the Parties argue that there are no barriers
         to entry on the routes of concern, and submit evidence of past entry and expansion
        (which are discussed in the route-by-route sections below, i.e., sections 9.2 and 9.3
         below).877 In this context, the Commission does not conclude that the barriers to
         entry on the routes of concern are entirely prohibitive of entry and expansion. The
         entries and or expansion, however, need to be put into perspective.
(727)   More specifically, the Parties only refer to entry and/or expansion by Ryanair and
       Wizz Air. These two carriers, due to their ULCC model, follow a dynamic approach
         to their network planning that is characterised by a high-switching behaviour,878
        suggesting that they can exit a route or reduce capacity anytime (contrary to network

(728)   In addition, Ryanair and Wizz Air, operate from secondary airports, therefore their
         offering is different (for more information, see section 9.1.2.2 above). Consequently,
         entry and expansion of ULCCs from secondary airports, cannot lead directly to the

(729)   Notably, there has not been a single example of entry or capacity increase by a
        network carrier competitor. The only example of entry in a primary airport was by
       Wizz  Air,  at  a  relatively  low  capacity  namely,  on  route Rome-Hamburg

         Parties do not support the conclusion that barriers to entry are insignificant.880 In any
         event, the Commission has taken note of the capacity increases by competitors and
        has naturally taken them into account, where relevant, in the assessment of particular
         routes (see sections 9.2 and 9.3 below).

        Neos, expressed their willingness to start operating on certain of the overlapping
         short-haul routes to/from Milan. Such entry is conditional, however, on obtaining
          slots   at  Milan  Linate,  an  airport   that   is  severely   slot  congested  (see
         section 9.1.4.1).881 These operators have confirmed that they currently do not have
         sufficient slots at Milan Linate to be able to enter on any of the overlapping routes.882
        Thus, the likelihood of Wizz Air and/or Neos entering any of the overlapping routes
           is not, at this stage, considered by the Commission as timely, likely or sufficient
         potential entry.
(731)   Additionally, Air France-KLM indicated that  it is considering entry on the routes
        Rome-Brussels and Milan-Brussels,883 as Rome and Milan are popular destinations
      among Transavia’s Dutch  leisure-oriented  target passengers.  884 Together with
        Transavia’s strong presence in Brussels, Air France-KLM considers that the routes
        Rome-Brussels and Milan-Brussels are within Transavia’s scope of operations, and
         that they are particularly attractive routes for leisure travellers given that they present
        a “year-round strategic potential”.885 However, as Air France-KLM does not have a
         foreseeable entry plan for Transavia on the above-mentioned routes in the near
         future, its entry is not, at this stage, considered by the Commission as timely, likely
        or sufficient potential entry either.

9.1.6.   Other considerations related to general arguments in the Parties’ Response to the
      SO
(733)   The Commission takes note of the fact that in their Response to the SO, the Parties
        include  general  arguments  regarding  the  framework  of  the  Commission’s
        assessment. In particular, the Parties argue that:887
          (a)  The Commission relies heavily on market share data (including passenger
            numbers and capacity data) and/or information such as the number of carriers
               active on each route that are not always a good proxy for establishing market
             power.
         (b)  The intra-European O&Ds are generally concentrated. In particular, the Parties
             argue that out of the total of 8 332 non-stop routes operated within the EEA,
             only 37% are served by more than one carrier flying directly, and only 14% are
              served by more than two carriers flying directly. According to the Parties, the
             high consolidation on these O&Ds allows new entrants to quickly capture large
             market shares.
          (c)  The Commission’s competitive assessment  contradicts  various precedents
            where 3-to-2 mergers or mergers to monopoly when disregarding a catchment
               area, including in situations where the combined market share was above 50%
            and  the increment brought by  the  transaction was above 5%, were not
              considered as problematic due to the presence of a competitor with a large
             market share.888
(734)   The Commission notes the following regarding these arguments:
(735)   In its assessment, the Commission has taken into consideration numerous data such
          as, but not limited to, market shares to underpin its conclusions. Contrary to the
         Parties’ allegations, the Commission has among others, conducted a detailed market
         investigation, an in-depth internal document review and conducted its own economic
         analysis that justify the conclusions reached in this Decision.889


886      Horizontal Merger Guidelines, paragraph 68.
887     Response to the SO, paragraphs 4-11.
888     The Parties refer to certain routes in Cases M.7541 – IAG/Aer Lingus, paragraphs 312 – 334; M.9287 –
        Connect  Airways/Flybe,  paragraphs.  334-342  and  361-370; M.5364  –  Iberia/Vueling/Clickair,
        paragraphs 234-236 and 288-290; M.5335 – Lufthansa/SN Airholding, paragraphs 202-225; and
       M.6447 – IAG/BMI, paragraphs 257-275.
889     See Section 9.


                                    177

[PÁGINA PDF 180]
(736)   Moreover, the Commission considers that the Parties’ argument as regards the levels
        of concentration on intra-European O&Ds only proves the need to react to further
         consolidation that harms the market and results in higher prices and less frequencies
         for the consumers.
(737)   Furthermore, the Commission acknowledges that ITA managed to reach relatively
        high market shares upon entry on all the routes identified in section 9.2, and such a
         disruptive competitor is of great value in promoting market competition. In effect,
         the Commission takes the view that evidence on entry which could quickly disrupt
        concentrated markets should play a role in its assessment repeats that it has not been
        able to obtain evidence on timely, likely, and sufficient entry (plans) by any of the
         Parties’ competitors (see section 9.1.5 above).
(738)   Furthermore, the Parties seek to substantiate their arguments by reference to routes
        assessed in those decisions, none of which are subject to the present case. However,
          this contradicts the Parties own view, namely that, individual data points are not
        always deterministic of whether competition issues arise on a route or not. The
       Commission identified the routes of concern in this Decision on the basis of an
         investigation encompassing a multitude of factors. In any event, the Parties invoke
         specific conclusions picked by them from previous Commission decisions, but do not
       show how any of these conclusions would apply to the particular facts of the present
        case entirely. Instead, the Parties rely on contrasting market share levels (a data point
         the Parties themselves argue to be inconsequential by itself) in an attempt to question
         the Commission’s assessment. Importantly, the Parties also omit to highlight that
         there are examples in the very same decisions for the opposite, i.e., the Commission
         raising  concerns  over  routes  with  similar  market  shares  as  in  its  present
         assessment.890
(739)  As a result, the Commission takes the view that the arguments of the Parties do not
        impact its assessment or conclusions.

(744)   However, the assessment below would remain applicable even in case the market
       would be defined more narrowly, encompassing fewer airports (i.e., only LIN and
     MXP on the Milan end of the route and/or only BRU on the Brussels end of the
         route).
(745)   The Commission notes that if only BGY were to be considered on the Milan end of
         the route, there would be no need to assess any of the overlaps under any plausible
        market definition on the Brussels end of the route because there would be no overlap
         arising due to the activities of the Parties (as neither operates from BGY). Therefore,
       and due to the lack of overlapping activities at BGY and CRL, the (narrowest
         possible) alternative market definition concerns the catchment area including LIN
       and MXP on the Milan end of the route and BRU on the Brussels end of the route.
       Wider possible alternative markets concern (i) LIN, MXP and BGY on the Milan end
        of the route and BRU on the Brussels end of the route; and (ii) LIN and MXP on the
       Milan end of the route, and BRU and CLR on the Brussels end of the route.
(746)   All three alternative possible market definitions (i.e., the narrowest possible and the
         other wider possible market definitions), would result in the same outcome: either the
        removal of Ryanair from the competitive landscape (in light of Ryanair’s recent exit
       from MXP-BRU and its absence in LIN) or no horizontal overlaps between the
          activities of the Parties (as neither Lufthansa or ITA operate from BGY and/or CLR.
        Consequently, the concerns outlined in the Commission’s assessment below, which
        focuses on the widest plausible market definition (which includes Ryanair) would not
        only continue to be relevant under any plausible alternative market definition where
         the Transaction gives rise to horizontal overlaps, but would be amplified due to the
        removal of Ryanair from the competitive landscape (i.e., the Transaction would be a
        merger-to-monopoly), the increased market shares of Lufthansa and ITA and the
       same or increased barriers to entry and expansion.
(747)   Table 27 below, sets out the Parties and their competitor’s market shares under the
        narrowest alternative possible market definition.

9.2.1.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(748)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that the main airlines serving the route Milan-Brussels
        based on Summer 2023 data are Lufthansa (through Brussels Airlines), ITA and
         Ryanair.893 Moreover, according to Lufthansa and MEF, post-Transaction  (i) the
         Parties will be better placed to compete with Ryanair, who, pre-Transaction is the
         either strongest competitor on the market or in any event holds a stronger market
         position than ITA;894 and, (ii) will be constrained by the potential additional entry
       and expansion of other carriers, such as easyJet (that was active on the route Milan-
        Brussels between 2013 and 2017), Vueling, Transavia and TUI Fly Belgium, that are
         present and active at both Milan and Brussels’ airports.895 In addition, the Parties
         point out to the fact that over Summer IATA 2024, Ryanair increased its capacity on
          this route by 27 flights overall for the entire season.896 Consequently, Lufthansa and
     MEF submit that there are no barriers to entry and/or expansion on the route Milan-
        Brussels either as a result of the Parties’ combined slot holdings in the Milan and
         Brussels’ airports or as a result of the average congestion rates in the Milan and
         Brussels’ airports.897 Furthermore, the Parties contest that they hold a frequency
        advantage over Ryanair, and point out that on Milan – Brussels, certain market
         investigation participants consider Ryanair to be Lufthansa’s closest competitor,
       namely IAG, Luxair and TUI Group, whereas Wizz Air considers Ryanair to be both
        Lufthansa and ITA’s closest competitor.898
9.2.1.3. The Commission’s assessment
(749)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes, that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Milan –
         Brussels.
(750)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 25 above, the Parties’ combined share (by
     PAX number) between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season
       2023/2024 was between 40-62% and equal or above 50% in the last three IATA
        Seasons. For the same time period, the Parties equally held an even higher share
        based on the number of frequencies they operated on the route during each IATA
        Season, namely between 51% and 67%, and 67% over Summer IATA 2024 as set
        out in Table 26. These market shares are themselves evidence of a dominant position
        held by the Parties after the Transaction.
(751)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      15% to 20% in the last five IATA seasons (by PAX number; see Table 25). This
        corresponds to a high increase in the HHI of between 768 and 1 421, in line with the
       Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines.899

(752)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
       be higher than 5 000 in each of the last five IATA seasons (with an increment of at
          least 768) based on PAX number. The high combined market share of the Parties, the
         large increment brought by the transaction, the high change in HHI and high HHI
        post-Transaction indicate that the Transaction would create or strengthen a dominant
         position.
(753)   Fourth, even when looking into the widest possible market definition (i.e., one which
        includes LIN, MXP and BGY on the Milan end of the route, and BRU and CRL on
         the  Brussels  end),  the  Transaction  constitutes  a  3-to-2 merger  for  non-stop
          flights.900In addition to the Parties, only Ryanair operates the Milan-Brussels city
         pair (but from BRU-CLR), and held a market share of 44% in the Winter IATA
       Season 2023/2024 and 43% in the Summer IATA Season 2023 based on the number
        of passengers. Ryanair’s market share is lower based on capacity, at 33% between
      Summer IATA Season 2023 and Summer 2024 (see Table 25 and Table 26). Ryanair
        operated the Milan-Brussels city pair both from BGY to CRL and from MXP to
     BRU in the past.901 However, as of Summer IATA Season 2023, Ryanair ceased
        operating on the route from BRU and MXP and closed its BRU base, and as of then,
        only operated the route BGY-CRL. Ryanair’s Milan-Brussels city pair market share
        reduction in terms of passengers in Summer IATA Season 2023 appears be the result
        of its exit from the MXP-BRU route, as explained in section 6.5.3.2 above. Under all
         alternative possible market definitions where the activities of the Parties would still
        overlap on the route Milan – Brussels, the competitive assessment would either
        remain the same, or Ryanair would be removed from the competitive landscape and
         therefore the Transaction would result to a monopoly.
(754)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operator on the Milan-Brussels city pair, holding a significant market
        share on both IATA Seasons, in terms of passengers and capacity operated, with
        Ryanair being the only other carrier operating in the Milan-Brussels city pair.
(755)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair is unlikely to be sufficient
         to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(756)   In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair operates on the market. Notably, Ryanair’s market share has been declining
         since Ryanair’s exit from BRU-MXP in Summer IATA Season 2023 and ranged
       between 43-44% over the last two completed IATA Seasons, compared to its higher
        market share between Winter IATA 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 which was in any
        event declining over this time period as well.
(757)   In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture 20% of the market in less than three years of operation and has competed

(758)   In the third place, the Parties would hold a frequency advantage over the only other
         direct competitor on the route, Ryanair. Based on the information of Table 23, the
         Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 45 weekly frequencies as compared to the
       17 weekly frequencies of Ryanair (based on 2023 figures). Moreover, even with

(759)    Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
        not  only compete  closely on  this  route  but,  they  are  each  other’s  closest
         competitor.902
(760)   In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa (Brussels Airlines) are both network carriers
        operating similar business models and attracting similar types of customers (with a
        higher willingness to pay), whereas Ryanair is an ULCC, operating a P2P business
       model and focused on price-sensitive leisure travel. (See section 9.1.2.1 above for
       more information).
(761)   In the second place,  airlines operating a  city pair from secondary  airports of
        proximity do not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same
        primary  airports. (see section  9.1.2.2). The Commission’s market investigation
        supports the view that “there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly
        from  their local  airport”.903 Specifically regarding competition on the Milan –
        Brussels city pair, ITA and Lufthansa (Brussels Airlines) operate the Milan-Brussels
         city pair from the same primary airport(s) (partially) in Milan (i.e., Brussels Airlines
        operates from both LIN and MXP and ITA operates from LIN) and Brussels (both
        operate  from BRU)  whereas  Ryanair  operates  the  Milan-Brussels  city  pair
         exclusively through secondary  airports  of  proximity, namely BGY and CLR
         respectively. (See section 9.1.2.2 above for more information).
(762)   In  this  context, the  vast majority of customers  that expressed a view  in the
       Commission’s market investigation believe that the closest alternative of Lufthansa’s
         offering on the Milan-Brussels route is ITA’s offering, and not that of Ryanair.904
(763)   Moreover, competitors  that expressed a view during the Commission’s market
         investigation confirm that the Parties compete closely on the route based on a
       number of criteria (e.g., prices, frequencies, on-board services, time of departure and
          arrival, use of loyalty programs etc.) and in general.905 Moreover, a number of
        competitors consider Lufthansa and ITA to be each other’s closest competitors on the
          route.906 Specifically with regards to closeness of competition between BRU, where
        Lufthansa and ITA operate from and CLR, where Ryanair operates from, “Ryanair

(772)  On the Brussels end, the  fact  that BRU  is not generally congested has been
        confirmed by market participants such as Ryanair.915 However, “Transavia notes
          that, although the airport is not congested at all its operational hours, slots are not
        widely available during peak hours (i.e., early morning and late evening hours).
        According  to  Transavia,  it  is important  for  low-cost-carriers  to ensure high
          utilization and maximisation of the use of an aircraft. Ideally, this would mean
        scheduling flights with early morning departure, quick turnarounds and evening
         arrivals. However, this is not easy to achieve in BRU’.916
(773)  On the Milan end, the results of the Commission’s market investigation strongly
        support the airlines’ preference for LIN and indicate that barriers to entry at the
         airport are significantly high due to slot congestion at the specific airport. Despite the
         fact that the Milan catchment area is served by several airports (i.e., MXP and likely
       BGY), based on the results of the Commission’s market investigation, competitors
        consider that slots at LIN give a strong competitive advantage to those who operate
        them, due to its strategic location and proximity to the city centre compared to MXP
         (see section 6.5.3.6 above, section 11 below, and paragraph (655) et seq.). Therefore,
         the inability of competitors to obtain slots at LIN is considered a significant barrier to
         entry, despite the availability of slots at MXP. (See section 9.1.4.1 above for more
         information).
(774)   In the second place, the Parties’ combined market share on the route and combined
          slot holding in LIN and in BRU will be significantly high, indicative of market
       power and will act as a barrier to entry and expansion. Despite the fact that both the
       Milan and Brussels catchment areas are served by several airports, the results of the

        Section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).
(785)   In the third place, the finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is

         increases, including […] (see Section 7.7.1).
9.2.1.4. Conclusion
(786)   In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion,
         the lack of prospect of likely, timely and sufficient entry on the route and the specific
        evidence on the likely negative effects of the Transaction, the Commission concludes
         that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on the route

(789)  On the Milan-Düsseldorf city pair the following plausible alternative geographic
        market definitions exist based on the catchment areas:
          (a)  On the Milan end of the route LIN and MXP may belong to one catchment area
              together with BGY or, alternatively, LIN and MXP may be separate from BGY
             (See Section 6.5.3.6 above).
         (b)  On the Düsseldorf end of the route, DUS and CGN may belong to one
             catchment area together with DTM and NRN, or DTM and NRN may be
              considered  as  separate from  the DUS and CGN  catchment  area  (See
              Section 6.5.3.3 above).
(790)   The  Commission’s  assessment  below  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, which includes LIN, MXP and BGY on the one hand, and DUS and CGN
         together with DTM and NRN on the other hand. The market shares and concerns
         outlined below reflect this plausible definition.
(791)   However, the assessment below would remain applicable if the market would be
        defined more narrowly, encompassing fewer airports where the Transaction would
        give rise to horizontal overlaps.



                                    189

[PÁGINA PDF 192]
(792)   The Commission notes that if on the Milan end of the route:
          (a)   only LIN and MXP were to be considered, the concerns outlined below would
              not only continue  to be  relevant under any  plausible  alternative market
               definitions on the Düsseldorf end of the route, but would be amplified due the
             removal of Ryanair from the competitive landscape as Ryanair only operates
            from BGY (i.e., the Transaction would be a merger-to-monopoly under any
               plausible alternative market definitions on the Düsseldorf end of the route). In
                this context, under the narrowest possible market definition, the activities of
              the Parties would overlap on LIN and MXP on the Milan end of the route, and
         DUS and CGN on the Düsseldorf end of the route.
         (b)    if only BGY were to be considered on the Milan end of the route, there would
             be no need to assess any of the overlaps under any plausible market definition
            on the Düsseldorf end of the route because there would be no overlap arising
            due to the activities of the Parties (as neither operates from BGY). In any case,
              since the activities of the Parties do not overlap in any market that only
              includes BGY on the Milan end of the route, the Commission considers that it
                  is not a plausible relevant market for the purposes of this Decision.
(793)   The Commission also notes that if on the Düsseldorf end of the route:
          (a)   Only DUS and CGN were to be considered, the narrowest possible market
               definition would be that where LIN and MXP are considered on the Milan end
              of the route. In this scenario, the concerns outlined below would not only
              continue to be relevant but would be amplified due to the removal of Ryanair
            from the competitive landscape (as the latter only operates from BGY). If LIN,
        MXP and BGY were considered on the Milan end of the route, the concerns
            would also be amplified, as Ryanair’s presence in BGY-NRN would not be
              considered, and thus, Ryanair’s presence on the route would be limited to its
         BGY-CGN  activities, whereas the  activities of the  Parties would remain
               unaltered.
         (b)  Only DUS, CGN and DTM were to be considered, the assessment would be
               identical to the one in point (a) above, as no carrier currently operates from
        DTM to Milan.
          (c)   Only DUS, CGN and NRN were to be considered, the assessment would
             remain identical to that of the widest possible market definition (see paragraph
              (786) et seq. above), as no carrier currently operates from DTM to Milan.
         (d)  Only NRN and/or DTM were to be considered, there would be no need to
              assess any of the overlaps under any plausible market definition on the Milan
            end of the route because there would be no overlap arising due to the activities
              of the Parties (as neither operates from neither NRN Nor DTM). In any case,
              the activities of the Parties do not overlap in these markets, therefore, the
            Commission considers that these are not plausible relevant markets for the
             purposes of this Decision.
(794)   Based on the above, the concerns outlined below would not only continue to be
         relevant under any  relevant  plausible  alternative market  definition where  the
          activities of the Parties overlap but would be amplified due the removal of Ryanair
       from  the  competitive landscape  (i.e.,  the  Transaction would be a  merger-to-
        monopoly), the increased market shares of Lufthansa and ITA and the increased
         barriers to entry and expansion.

9.2.2.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s View
(796)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that the main airlines serving the route Milan-Düsseldorf
        based on based on Winter 2022/2023 and Summer 2023 data are Lufthansa (through
       Eurowings and Lufthansa Passenger Airlines), ITA and Ryanair.929 Lufthansa and
     MEF consider ITA’s market share  to be moderate.930 Moreover, according  to
        Lufthansa and MEF, post-Transaction the Parties will continue to face (i) strong
         actual competition from Ryanair, which holds a significant market share and has the
          ability to expand its activities on the route; (ii) actual competition from Neos, which
         started operating the connection MXP – CGN in Summer 2020; and (iii) potential
        competition from easyJet, that operates bases in at least one end of the route.931
        Furthermore, Lufthansa and MEF identify Wizz Air as a new entrant on the route932
       and submit that there are no barriers to entry and/or expansion on the route Milan-
        Düsseldorf because the airports are not congested at either end of the city pair.933
         Finally, the Parties point out that on Milan – Dusseldorf, certain market investigation
         participants consider Ryanair to be the closest competitor of at least one of the
          Parties, namely France-KLM, IAG, Luxair, TUI Group and Wizz Air.934
9.2.2.3. The Commission’s assessment
(797)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes, that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
         of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Milan -
        Düsseldorf.



928     At the time of writing this Decision, passenger data for the Winter 2023/2024 season was only available
         for November 2023, December 2023 and January 2024. This table therefore does not include 2 months
         of passenger data for Winter 2023/2024 (namely February 2024 and March 2024).

(798)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 28 above, the Parties’ combined share (by
     PAX number) between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season
       2023/2024 was between 40-59% and above 50% in the last four IATA Seasons. For
         the same time period, the Parties equally held an even higher share based on the
       number of frequencies they operated on the route during each IATA Season, namely
       between 52% and 73%, as set out in Table 29 above. These market shares could
        themselves be evidence that the Parties would hold a dominant position after the
         Transaction.
(799)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      10% to 20% in the last five IATA seasons based on PAX numbers. This corresponds
         to a high increase  in the HHI of between 764 and 1 739,  in  line with the
       Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines.935.
(800)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be between 4 959 – 5 399 during each of the last five IATA seasons (with an
        increment of at least more than 764) based on PAX numbers. The high combined
        market share of the Parties, the large increment brought by the transaction, the high
       change in HHI and high HHI post-Transaction indicate that the Transaction would
         create or strengthen a dominant position.
(801)   Fourth, in addition to the Parties, only Ryanair operates the Milan - Düsseldorf city
          pair, and held a market share of 41% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and
      47% in the Summer IATA Season 2023 based on the number of passengers.
        Ryanair’s market share is lower based on capacity, ranging between 19% and 29%
       between Summer IATA Season 2023 and Summer Season 2024. Furthermore, the
       Commission’s pre-notification market investigation indicates that Neos is neither
         active on nor does it plan to enter the route.936 Thus, even when looking into the
        widest possible market definition, the Transaction constitutes a 3-to-2 merger for
        non-stop flights.937
(802)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operator on the Milan - Düsseldorf city pair, holding a significant market
        share on both IATA Seasons, in terms of passengers and capacity operated, with
        Ryanair being the Parties’ only active competitor.
(803)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair is unlikely to be sufficient
         to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(804)   In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair operates on the market with market shares between 35% and 52% for the


935      According to paragraph 20 of its Horizontal Merger Guidelines, “The Commission is also unlikely to

       and a delta below 250, or a merger with a post-merger HHI above 2000 and a delta below 150, except
       where special circumstances” arise.

          latest five seasons (a market share that has remained below 50% over the last four
        completed IATA seasons and was closer to 40% over three of these IATA seasons).
(805)   In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture 20% of the market with less than 3 years of operation and has competed
         closely  with  Lufthansa on  the  route  in  the  past.  See  in  this  respect  also
        paragraph (804) et seq. below.
(806)   In the third place, the Parties would hold a frequency advantage over the only other
         direct competitor on the route, Ryanair. According to a Parties’ submission and
        based on Summer IATA 2024 data, for the summer seasons, the Parties would, post-
         Transaction,  operate 37 weekly  frequencies  (26  operated by Eurowings and
       11 operated by ITA) as compared to the 13 weekly frequencies of Ryanair. Similarly
        based on Winter IATA 2023/2024 data, for the winter seasons, the Parties would,
         post-Transaction, operate 31 weekly frequencies (19 operated by Eurowings and
       12 operated by ITA) as compared to the 11 weekly frequencies of Ryanair.938
(807)    Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
       compete closely on this route.939
(808)   In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa are both network carriers operating similar
        business models and attracting similar types of customers (with a higher willingness
         to pay), whereas Ryanair is an ULCC, operating a P2P business model and focused
       on price-sensitive leisure travel. (See section 9.1.2.1 above for more information).
(809)   Specifically on this route, even though Lufthansa operates on the Milan-Düsseldorf
         city pair through Eurowings (Lufthansa group’s LCC), generally the business model
       and marketing strategy of LCCs’ belonging to large airline groups differs from that
        of ULCCs such as Ryanair. (See section 9.1.2.1 above for more information and in
         particular paragraphs (586)-(587)).
(810)   In the second place,  airlines operating a  city pair from secondary  airports of
        proximity do not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same
        primary airports. The Commission’s market investigation supports the view that
        “there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their local
         airport”940 (see section 9.1.2.2). Specifically, regarding competition on the Milan –
        Düsseldorf city pair, ITA and Lufthansa operate from the same airports (partially)
            (i.e., Lufthansa operates on MXP-DUS, MXP-CGN and BGY-DUS, whereas ITA
        operates LIN-DUS). It is true that Ryanair, which operates exclusively from BGY to
     CGN and to NRN, could be said to operate from some of the same airports as
        Lufthansa. That being said, although both Eurowings and Ryanair operate the route
       Milan – Düsseldorf from the airport BGY, only Eurowings and ITA operate from the
       main airport at Düsseldorf. (See section 9.1.2.2 above for more information).

(811)   In  particular,  the  vast  majority  of  customers  that  expressed  a view  in  the
       Commission’s market investigation believe that the closest alternative of Lufthansa’s
         offering on the Milan - Düsseldorf route is ITA’s offering, and not one that of
         Ryanair.941
(812)   Lastly, the Commission notes that the overall travel times submitted by the Parties
        (considering the travel time from city centre to city centre on both ends of the route)
         also show that airlines operating a city pair from secondary airports of proximity do
        not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same primary
          airports. Notably, the overall travel time:942
          (a)   considering LIN and DUS (ITA present) is around 1 hour 48 minutes;
         (b)   considering BGY and DUS (Lufthansa present) is around 2 hours 16 minutes;
          (c)   considering MXP and DUS (Lufthansa present) is around 2 hours 26 minutes;
         (d)   considering MXP and CGN (Lufthansa present) is around 2 hours 45 minutes;
          (e)   considering BGY and CGN (Ryanair present)  is, similarly to MXP-CGN,
             around 2 hours 45 minutes; and
           (f)   considering BGY and NRN (Ryanair present) is around 3 hours 10 minutes.
(813)   This shows that ITA competes closely with Lufthansa on this route, considering the
         shorter travel times, and comparatively less closely with Ryanair.
(814)   In the third place, The Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive
        pressure exerted by existing carriers on the route was corroborated by the responses
         to the Commission’s market investigation. In particular, despite the fact that several
        market participants such as Air France-KLM, IAG, Luxair, TUI Group and Wizz Air
        consider Ryanair to be the closes competitor of at least one of the Parties, as
         correctly pointed out by the Parties,943 the majority of competitors that expressed a
       view consider that Lufthansa and ITA are closer competitors of each other on the
        Milan-Düsseldorf city pair compared to Ryanair,944 and that, in any event, the Parties
       compete closely on the route based on a number of criteria (e.g., prices, frequencies,
        on-board services, time of departure and arrival etc.) and in general.945
(815)   Seventh, as further explained in section 9.1.4, there are several barriers to entry and
        expansion on the route.
(816)   In  the  first  place,  the  relevant  airports  are  to an  extent  congested. This  is
        demonstrated by the fact that, from the Milan end, all LIN, MXP and BGY are
        Level 3 Coordinated  Airports  (i.e., demand  significantly exceeds  the  airports’
         capability), whereas from  the  Düsseldorf  end, DUS and CGN  are  Level 3
        Coordinated Airport  (i.e., demand significantly exceeds the airports’ capability),
        whereas NRN is Level 1 Non-Coordinated Airport.946

(820)   The above figures indicate that LIN is significantly slot constrained (including during
         the time of operation of the Parties) whereas MXP and DUS have some  slot
         constraints  at peak times but have some spare capacity for new entrants and
        incumbents to grow.
(821)  On the Milan end, the results of the Commission’s market investigation strongly
        support the airlines’ preference for LIN and indicate that barriers to entry at the
         airport are significantly high due to slot congestion at the specific airport. (See
         section  9.1.4.1 above  for more  information). Despite  the  fact  that  the Milan
        catchment area is served by several airports (i.e., MXP and likely BGY), based on
         the results of the Commission’s market investigation, competitors consider that slots
          at LIN give a strong competitive advantage to those who operate them, due to its
         strategic  location and  proximity  to  the  city  centre compared  to MXP  (see
         section 6.5.3.6 above, section 11 below, and paragraph (655) et seq.). Therefore, the
          inability of competitors to obtain slots at LIN is considered a significant barrier to
         entry, despite the availability of slots at MXP. (See section 9.1.4.1 above for more
         information).
(822)   In the second place, the Parties’ combined market share on the route and combined
          slot holding in LIN and in DUS will be significantly high, indicative of market power
       and will act as a barrier to entry and expansion. Despite the fact that both the Milan
       and Düsseldorf catchment areas are served by several airports, the results of the
       Commission’s market investigation and internal documents of the Parties support
         that (i)“there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their
         local airport”950 and thus entering a secondary airport would not allow competitors
         to compete closely with the Parties (see section 9.1.2.2 above for more information);
       and that (ii) Lufthansa uses its strong market position in primary airports to eliminate
        competition on both primary and secondary airports of the same catchment area. (See

(823)   Eighth, no further, likely, timely and sufficient entry or expansion of competitors is
        expected on the Milan-Düsseldorf city pair. The Commission has analysed the entry
        plans of all relevant potential competitors which, taken individually and as a whole,
       do not support that the concentration on the route would be offset by future market
         entry, or indeed that any market entry would occur at all.
(824)   In the first place, TUI Fly confirms that it does not plan on entering the route MIL-
      DUS. 951
(825)   In the second place, as indicated by the Parties, Wizz Air operated eight frequencies
         in  total  for  the connection MXP-DTM  for  the whole Summer  2024.952 The
       Commission notes that eight frequencies overall, throughout the entire Summer
      IATA 2024 season cannot be seen as a continuous service (which is consistent with
         the Commission’s assessment of Eurowings’ activities on routes such as Brindisi-
          Stuttgart, Brindisi-Düsseldorf and Cagliari-Munich over the Winter IATA Season in
         section 9.4.6below) and therefore Wizz Air cannot be considered as a new entrant
         that will constrain the Parties activities. Moreover, the Commission notes that based
       on Wizz Air’s online booking platform (website),953 the latter will offer 4 frequencies
       on MXP-DTM over June 2024, and no other flights are planned to be operated until
       December 2025. Therefore, even if Wizz Air were to be considered as a new entrant
       on the route, it would in any event have exited in June 2024. Moreover, Wizz Air
        confirmed  that  it would consider an entry (continuous operations) conditional
        ‘[p]ending access to LIN’, for which ‘Wizz Air clarifies that it applied for slots (…)
        under the normal seasonal procedure as it does every season, however, it has not
       been able to change the times it already has or to obtain new slots, so such an entry
       would be conditional on obtaining the necessary slots’.954 Therefore, it appears that
       Wizz Air would only consider entry with continuous operations if  it would gain
        access to suitable slots in LIN, which it currently cannot do. On this basis Wizz Air’s
       8 frequencies over Summer IATA 2024 (last four of which to be operated in mid-
        June) and subsequent exit over the same season, as well as its submission as to a
         likely entry with continuous operations is not considered as indicative of a timely,
         likely or sufficient potential entry.
(826)   In the third place, other potential entry and/or expansion plans are subject to the
       outcome of the Transaction, and thus are not considered as indicative of a timely,
         likely or sufficient entry.955 In other words, the results of the Commission’s market
         investigation are that potential entrants are only considering potential actions on this
         route.  In  particular,  the Commission did not  find  that  potential  entrants had
        developed specific plans or adopted preparatory steps to enter these routes, and the

        generic planning that it did find lacked detail and was typically subject to numerous
        caveats and conditions.956 (See section 9.1.5 above for more information.)
(827)   Ninth, there is specific evidence showing that the Transaction is likely to result in
        negative effects.
(828)   In the first place, while a sizeable share of the respondents indicated that they did not
       know, the vast majority of competitors active on short-haul routes and expressing an
        opinion considered the impact of the Transaction on the route to be negative.957
       While the views of customers on the impact of the Transaction on this route are
         overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion of responding customers
        consider the impact to be negative.958 In addition, several market participants have
         identified negative effects stemming from Lufthansa’s past acquisitions of short-haul
         carriers in the EEA (see Section 7.7.4 for more detailed results).
(829)   In the second place, a finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is in line with the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a short-haul route as well as the
         elimination of competition by ITA is associated with significantly higher prices (see
        Section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).
(830)   In the third place, the finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is also in line with the internal documents of Lufthansa predicting price
         increases, including […] (see Section 7.7.1).
9.2.2.4. Conclusion
(831)   In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion,
         the lack of prospect of likely, timely and sufficient entry on the route and the specific
        evidence on the likely negative effects of the Transaction, the Commission concludes
         that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on the route
       Milan - Düsseldorf by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in both the
        Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition.

(834)  On the Milan - Frankfurt city pair the following plausible alternative geographic
        market definitions exist in line with the market definition findings on the catchment
         areas:
          (a)  On the Milan end of the route LIN and MXP may belong to one catchment area
              together with BGY or, alternatively, LIN and MXP may be separate from BGY
             (See section 6.5.3.6 above).
         (b)  On the Frankfurt end of the route FRA and HHN may belong to one catchment
              area  or,  alternatively, they may belong to separate catchment areas (See
               section 6.5.3.4 above).
(835)   The  Commission’s  assessment  below  considers  the  widest  possible  market
         definition, which includes LIN, MXP and BGY on the Milan end of the route and
     FRA and HHN on the Frankfurt end of the route.
(836)   However, the assessment above would remain applicable even in case the market
       would  be  defined more  narrowly,  encompassing  fewer  airports  (where  the
        Transaction would still give rise to horizontal overlaps).
(837)   The Commission notes that if on the Milan end of the route:
          (a)   only LIN and MXP were to be considered, the concerns outlined below would
              not only continue  to be  relevant under any  plausible  alternative market
               definitions on the Frankfurt end of the route, but would be amplified due the
             removal of Ryanair from the competitive landscape as Ryanair only operates
            from BGY (i.e., the Transaction would be a merger-to-monopoly under any
               plausible alternative market definitions on the Frankfurt end of the route). In
                this context, under the narrowest possible market definition, the activities of
              the Parties would overlap on LIN and MXP on the Milan end of the route, and
         FRA on the Frankfurt end of the route.
         (b)     if only BGY were to be considered on the Milan end of the route, there would
             be no need to assess any of the overlaps under any plausible market definition
            on the Frankfurt end of the route because there would be no overlap arising due
               to the activities of the Parties (as neither operates from BGY).
(838)   The Commission also notes that if on the Frankfurt end of the route:
          (a)   Only FRA were to be considered, the concerns outlined below would not only
              continue to be relevant but would be amplified due to the removal of Ryanair
            from the competitive landscape (as the latter only operates from HHN), under
                  all  plausible  market  definitions on  the Milan end  of  the  route. More
                specifically, if only FRA were to be considered, the Transaction would result in
             a monopoly.
         (b)   Only HHN were to be considered, there would be no need to assess any of the
              overlaps under any plausible market definition on the Milan end of the route
             because there would be no overlap arising due to the activities of the Parties (as
               neither operates from HHN).
(839)   The Parties' market share would increase under all the plausible narrower market
         definitions where the Transaction gives rise to horizontal overlaps (i.e., with less
         airports considered) since Ryanair is not active in those narrower markets.

9.2.3.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(841)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that the main airlines serving the route Milan-Frankfurt
        based on Winter 2022/2023 and Summer 2023 IATA seasons are Lufthansa (through
        Lufthansa  Passenger  Airlines  and  Air  Dolomiti), ITA and  Ryanair.961  Post-
         Transaction, according to Lufthansa and MEF, the merged entity will (i) continue to
        face strong competition from Ryanair a long-standing competitor with a similar
        market share to that of ITA having increased capacity in Summer IATA 2024,962
            (ii) be constrained by the potential entries of Wizz Air and easyJet, both of which
        already operate on both legs of the city pair963 and Neos.964 Lufthansa and MEF
        argue that Lufthansa competes closely with low-cost carriers, especially Ryanair,
       which is also reflected by the internal documents.965 According to Lufthansa and
      MEF, the combined entity would also face out-of-market competitive constraints
       from train operators, namely Deutsche Bahn and Trenitalia, as the former of which
         offering daily direct connections of approximately 7h 24min.966 Finally, Lufthansa
       and MEF submit that there are no barriers to entry and/or expansion on the route
        Milan-Frankfurt because the airports are not congested, at either end of the city
          pair.967 Finally, Lufthansa and MEF note that 47% of all respondents stated that they
       do not know whether the Transaction will have an impact on competition on this
         route, further to 7% who did not respond at all.968
9.2.3.3. The Commission’s assessment
(842)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Milan –
         Frankfurt.

(843)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 31 above, the Parties’ combined share (by
     PAX number) between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season
       2023/2024 was between 52-88%. For the same time period, the Parties equally held
       an even higher share based on the number of frequencies they operated on the route
        during each IATA Season, namely between 85% and 97%, as set out in Table 32
        above. These market shares may be evidence in themselves of a dominant position
          after the Transaction.
(844)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      12% to 20% in the last five IATA seasons. This corresponds to a high increase in the
      HHI  of between 940 and 2 553 based on PAX numbers,  in  line with  the
       Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines.969
(845)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be between 5 011 and 7 854 in each of the last five completed IATA seasons (with an
        increment of at least 940) based on PAX numbers. The high combined market share
        of the Parties, the large increment brought by the transaction, the high change in HHI
       and high HHI post-Transaction  indicate  that  the Transaction would  create or
        strengthen a dominant position.
(846)   Fourth, when looking into the widest possible market definition, the Transaction
         constitutes a 3-to-2 merger for non-stop flights.970 In addition to the Parties, only
        Ryanair operates the Milan - Frankfurt city pair (but from BGY-HHN) and held a
        market share of 13% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and 12% in the Summer
      IATA Season 2023 based on the number of passengers. Ryanair’s market share is
        lower based on capacity, ranging between 3% and 4% between Summer IATA
       Season 2023 and Summer IATA Season 2024. Under all alternative possible market
         definitions where the activities of the Parties would still overlap on the route Milan –
         Frankfurt, the competitive assessment would either remain the same, or Ryanair
       would be removed from the competitive landscape and therefore the Transaction
       would result to a monopoly.
(847)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operator on the Milan - Frankfurt city pair, holding a significant market
        share on both IATA Seasons, in terms of passengers and capacity operated, with
        Ryanair being the Parties’ only active competitor.
(848)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair is unlikely to be sufficient
         to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(849)   In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair operates on the market with market shares between 12% and 48% for the
          latest five seasons, and with a market share below 20% over the last four seasons.


969      According to paragraph 20 of its Horizontal Merger Guidelines, “The Commission is also unlikely to
          identify horizontal competition concerns in a merger with a post-merger HHI between 1000 and 2000
       and a delta below 250, or a merger with a post-merger HHI above 2000 and a delta below 150, except
       where special circumstances” arise.
970     As indicated in section 9.2.1.1, under all alternative possible market definitions where the activities of
         the Parties would still overlap on the route Milan – Frankfurt, Ryanair would be removed from the
        competitive landscape and therefore the Transaction would result to a monopoly.

        Notably, Ryanair’s market share has been declining since Ryanair’s exit from BGY-
     FRA in Summer IATA Season 2022.
(850)   In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture 20% of the market with less than three years of operation and has competed
         closely  with  Lufthansa on  the  route  in  the  past.  See  in  this  respect  also
        paragraph (849) below.
(851)   In the third place, the Parties would hold a frequency advantage over the only other
         direct competitor on the route, Ryanair. Based on the information of Table 23 above,
         the Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 89 weekly frequencies, a significantly
        higher number as compared to the two to three weekly frequencies of Ryanair (based
       on 2023 figures).
(852)    Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
       compete closely on this route.971
(853)   In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa are both network carriers operating similar
        business models and attracting similar types of passengers, whereas Ryanair is an
     ULCC  operating a P2P  business model and  focused on  leisure  travel.  (See
         section 9.1.2.1 above for more information).
(854)   The Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive pressure exerted by
         existing carriers on the route was corroborated by the responses to the Commission’s
        market investigation, where the majority of competitors that expressed a view
        consider that Lufthansa and ITA are closer competitors of each other on the Milan-
        Frankfurt city pair compared to Ryanair.972 Air France-KLM explains that “Frankfurt
      Hahn  is closer to Luxembourg than Frankfurt (situated 1h35 min by car from
        [F]rankfurt center). It has no facility to operate large traffic flows. It has around
       2.5m pax per year for the moment in comparison to close to 70m for FRA. Only Wizz
       and Ryanair are operating from HHN on a very low frequency basis and to leisure
         destinations only. Hahn is only reachable by Bus in 2hours from Frankfurt city.
        Frankfurt airport  is located close to the  city and also reachable easily from
       Mainz/Wiesbaden and Darmstadt which are the four main  cities to contribute
          locally. HAHN cannot play that role. FRA [M]ain airport operates a state of the art
         train station with hundreds of high-speed and regional train per day connecting FRA
         [A]irport to rest of Germany, It is one of the main station for Deutsche Bahn.(…)”.973
         Similarly, in the case of Milan, Wizz Air considers that MXP and BGY are not close
         substitutes to.974
(855)   In the second place,  airlines operating a  city pair from secondary  airports of
        proximity do not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same
        primary airports. The Commission’s market investigation supports the view that

        “there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their local

        operate the Milan - Frankfurt city pair from the same primary airport(s) (partially) in
       Milan (i.e., Lufthansa operates from both LIN and MXP and ITA operates from LIN)
       and Frankfurt (both operate from FRA) whereas Ryanair operates the Milan  -
        Frankfurt city pair exclusively through secondary airports of proximity, namely BGY
       and HHN respectively. The Commission notes that Ryanair’s market share on the
         route is declining. More specifically, Ryanair operated the Milan-Frankfurt city pair
       from BGY to FRA until Winter IATA Season 2021/2022. However, as of Summer
      IATA Season 2023, Ryanair ceased its operations from FRA, and as of then, only
        operated the route BGY-HHN. The declining market share of Ryanair on the route
       Milan - Frankfurt in terms of passengers in Summer IATA Season 2023 appears be
         the result of its exit from the FRA. In this context, Ryanair explains that “In IATA
      Summer 2019 we [Ryanair] carried 81.0k passengers between Frankfurt Main and
        Milan. In IATA Summer 2023, after we halted operation to Frankfurt Main, we
        carried 22.8k passengers between Frankfurt Hahn and Milan. (…) In IATA Summer
       2019 we operated daily flights between Frankfurt Main and Milan. In IATA Summer
        2023, we operated biweekly flights between Frankfurt Hahn and Milan. (…) Our
        load factor dropped (…) following the switch from Main to Hahn between IATA
      Summer 2019 and IATA Summer 2023”.976
(856)   Moreover, the vast majority of customers that expressed a view in the Commission’s
        market investigation believe that the closest alternative of Lufthansa’s offering on the
       Milan - Frankfurt route is ITA’s offering, and not that of Ryanair.977 Moreover, the
        majority of competitor respondents that expressed a view consider that the Parties
       compete closely on the route based on a number of criteria (e.g., prices, frequencies,
        on-board services, time of departure and arrival etc.) and in general.978
(857)   Lastly, the Commission notes that the overall travel times submitted by the Parties
        (considering the travel time from city centre to city centre on both ends of the route)
         also show that airlines operating a city pair from secondary airports of proximity do
        not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same primary
          airports. Notably, the overall  travel time considering LIN and FRA (ITA and
        Lufthansa present) is around 1 hour 40 minutes. The overall travel time increases to
        approx. 2 hours 10 minutes when considering MXP and FRA (Lufthansa present). In
         contrast the overall travel time is approx. 3 hours 10 minutes when considering BGY
       and HHN (Ryanair present).979 This shows that Lufthansa and ITA compete closely
        with each other considering the shorter travel times than they do with Ryanair.
(858)   Seventh, as further explained in section 9.1.4, there are several barriers to entry and
        expansion on the route.
(859)   In  the  first  place,  the  relevant  airports  are  to an  extent  congested. This  is
        demonstrated by the fact that, from the Milan end, all LIN, MXP and BGY are

        of the Parties, but has some spare capacity for new entrants and incumbents to grow.

         the airlines’ preference for LIN and indicate that barriers to entry at the airport are
         significantly high due to slot congestion at this specific airport. (See section 9.1.4.1
       above for more information).
(864)  On the Frankfurt end of the route however, competitors such as Ryanair explain that
     FRA  is congested over peak  hours.984 On  the Milan end,  the  results  of  the
       Commission’s market investigation, strongly support the airline’s preference for LIN
       and indicate that barriers to entry at the airport are significantly high. Despite the fact
         that the Milan catchment area is served by several airports (i.e., LIN, MXP and likely
       BGY), based on the results of the Commission’s market investigation, competitors
        consider that slots at LIN give a strong competitive advantage to those who operate
        them, due to its strategic location and proximity to the city centre compared to MXP
         (see section 6.5.3.6 above, section 11 below, and paragraph (655) et seq.). Therefore,
         the inability of competitors to obtain slots at LIN is considered a significant barrier to
         entry, despite the availability of slots at MXP. (See section 9.1.4.1 above for more
         information).

(874)   Ninth, there is specific evidence showing that the Transaction is likely to result in
        negative effects.
(875)   In the first place, while a sizeable share of the respondents indicated that they did not
       know, the vast majority of competitors active on short-haul routes and expressing an
        opinion considered the impact of the Transaction on the route to be negative.998
       While the views of customers on the impact of the Transaction on this route are
         overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion of responding customers
        consider the impact to be negative.999 In addition, several market participants have
         identified negative effects stemming from Lufthansa’s past acquisitions of short-haul
         carriers in the EEA (see Section 7.7.4 for more detailed results).
(876)   In the second place, a finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is in line with the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a short-haul route as well as the
         elimination of competition by ITA is associated with significantly higher prices (see
        Section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).
(877)   In the third place, the finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is also in line with the internal documents of Lufthansa predicting price
         increases, including […] (see Section 7.7.1).
9.2.3.4. Conclusion
(878)   In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion,
         the lack of prospect of likely, timely and sufficient entry on the route, the negligible
        out-of-market constraints that the Parties will face by train operators, and the specific
        evidence on the likely negative effects of the Transaction, the Commission concludes
         that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on the route,
       Milan - Frankfurt by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in both the
        Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition.

(881)   Considering  the Milan-Hamburg  city  pair  the  following  plausible  alternative
        geographic market definitions exist based on the catchment areas:
          (a)  On the Milan end of the route LIN and MXP may belong to one catchment area
              together with BGY or, alternatively, LIN and MXP may be separate from BGY
             (See section 6.5.3.6 above).
         (b)  On the Hamburg end of the route HAM and LBC may belong to one catchment
              area or may be considered as separate markets (See section 6.5.3.5 above).
(882)   The  Commission’s  assessment  below  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, whereby LIN, MXP and BGY on the one hand, and HAM and LBC on the
         other hand would belong to the same catchment areas. The market shares and
        concerns outlined above reflect this widest plausible market definition.
(883)   However, the assessment below would remain applicable even in case the market
       would be defined more narrowly, encompassing fewer airports (and where the
        Transaction would still give rise to horizontal overlaps).
(884)   The Commission notes that if on the Milan end of the route:
          (a)   only LIN and MXP were to be considered, the concerns outlined below would
              not only continue  to be  relevant under any  plausible  alternative market
               definitions on the Hamburg end of the route (where the Transaction would give
                rise to horizontal overlaps), but would be amplified due the removal of Ryanair
            from the competitive landscape as Ryanair only operates from BGY (i.e., the
              Transaction would be a merger-to-monopoly under any plausible alternative
             market definitions on the Hamburg end of the route where the Transaction
            would give rise to horizontal overlaps). In this context, under the narrowest
              possible market definition, the activities of the Parties would overlap on LIN
            and MXP on the Milan end of the route.
         (b)     if only BGY were to be considered on the Milan end of the route, there would
             be no need to assess any of the overlaps under any plausible market definition
            on the Hamburg end of the route because there would be no overlap arising due
               to the activities of the Parties (as neither operates from BGY).
