9.2.4.3. The Commission’s assessment
(889)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Milan –
       Hamburg over the summer IATA seasons.
(890)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route over the summer IATA seasons.1008 As set out in Table 36 above,
         the Parties’ combined share (by PAX number) between Summer IATA Season 2022
       and Summer IATA Season 2023 was between 60-66%. For the three Summer IATA
        Seasons from 2022-2024, the Parties equally held a high share based on the number
        of frequencies they operated on the route during each Summer IATA Season, namely
       between 64% and 71%, as set out in Table 35 above. These market shares may be
        evidence in themselves of a dominant position after the Transaction.
(891)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      19% to 25% in the last two summer IATA seasons. This corresponds to a high
         increase in the HHI of between 1 563 and 2 051 based on PAX numbers, in line with
         the Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines.1009
(892)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be between 4 575 and 5 022 in each of the last two summer IATA seasons (with an
        increment of at least 1 563) based on PAX number. The high combined market share
        of the Parties, the large increment brought by the Transaction, the high change in
      HHI and high HHI post-Transaction indicate that the Transaction would create or
        strengthen a dominant position over the summer IATA season.
(893)   Fourth, even when looking into the widest possible market definition (i.e., one which
        includes LIN, MXP and BGY on the Milan end of the route, and HAM and LBC on
         the Hamburg end), and which includes not only direct flights but also indirect flights)
         the Transaction constitutes a 3-to-2 merger in the market that includes both direct
       and indirect flights, as the share of indirect flights exceeds 10%.1010 (For more
        information on short-haul markets that direct and indirect flights, see section 9.4
        below). Under all alternative possible market definitions where the activities of the

         Parties would  still  overlap on  the  route Milan – Hamburg,  the  competitive
        assessment would either remain the same, or Ryanair would be removed from the

(894)   In addition to the Parties, over the Summer IATA season, only Ryanair operates
         direct flights on the Milan - Hamburg city pair (but from BGY-HAM) and held a
        market share of 29% in the Summer IATA Season 2023 and 28% in the Summer
      IATA Season 2022 based on the number of passengers. Ryanair’s market share based
       on capacity, ranges between 22% and 28% between Summer IATA Season 2022 and
      Summer IATA Season 2024.
(895)   According to the Parties submissions, Neos is also active on a seasonal basis on the
         route (i.e., Summer IATA only). However, in response to the Commission’s market
         investigation Neos explains that its operations on MXP-HAM are chartered flights
        operated on behalf of a cruise companies.1011 Neos clarifies its operations on the
         route Milan – Hamburg “are exceptionally closed flights, which are not available for
         direct purchase by customers. In other words, only customers of Costa Cruise and
     MSC Cruise can purchase seats, these flights are not available through NEOS’
        website or any distribution channel, and the operations are limited to the needs of
         the two Cruise companies (e.g., all luggage is collectively transported to the port,
       and passengers receive them on the cruise boat)”.1012
(896)  As passengers are unable to purchase dry-seats from typical distribution channels on
       Neos’ flights on the route Milan – Hamburg, the Commission considers that the latter
        does not compete with the  Parties on the  route, as  there  is no demand-side
          substitutability between the activities of the Parties and Ryanair on the one hand, and
       Neos on the other.
(897)   Furthermore, the other competitor offering indirect flights on the Milan – Hamburg
         city pair is Air France – KLM, with a negligible presence and very low market share
        of <1% on both Summer IATA seasons 2022 and 2023.
(898)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operator on the Milan  - Hamburg city pair over the summer IATA
         seasons, holding a significant market share both in terms of passengers and capacity
         operated, with Ryanair being the Parties’ only active competitor.
(899)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair (offering direct flights) and
        Air France – KLM (offering indirect flights) is unlikely to be sufficient to constrain
         the Parties post-Transaction.
(900)   In the first place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair and to a very minor extent from Air France -KLM (due to its negligible
        market share) post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture 25% of the summer season market within its three years of operation and has
       competed closely with Lufthansa on the route in the past. See in this respect also
        paragraph (899) et seq. below.

(901)   In the second place, the Parties would hold a frequency advantage over the only other
         direct competitor on the route, Ryanair. According to a Parties’ submission and
        based on Summer IATA 2023 and Summer IATA 2024 data, for the summer
         seasons,  the  Parties would,  post-Transaction, operate  triple  the frequencies  of

       Eurowings and 7 operated by ITA over Summer IATA 2023), and, approximately
         three times more compared to the 5 weekly frequencies of Ryanair.1013
(902)    Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
       compete closely on this route.1014
(903)   In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa are both network carriers operating similar
        business models and attracting similar types of customers (with a higher willingness
         to pay), whereas Ryanair is an ULCC, operating a P2P business model and focused
       on price-sensitive leisure travel. (See section 9.1.2.1 above for more information).
(904)   Even though Lufthansa  operates on  the Milan  - Hamburg  city  pair through
       Eurowings  (Lufthansa  group’s  LCC),  generally LCCs’  business  model  and
        marketing differs from that of ULCCs such as Ryanair. (See section 9.1.2.1 above for
       more information and in particular paragraphs (586)-(590)).
(905)   In the second place,  airlines operating a  city pair from secondary  airports of
        proximity, like on the present route where Ryanair operates from BGY, do not
       compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same primary airports.
       The Commission’s market investigation supports the view that “there is a general
         preference of the majority of passengers to  fly from their local airport”.1015 (See
         section 9.1.2.2 above for more information).
(906)   In  particular,  the  vast  majority  of  customers  that  expressed  a view  in  the
       Commission’s market investigation believe that the closest alternative of Lufthansa’s
         offering on the Milan  - Hamburg route  is ITA’s offering, and not one that of
         Ryanair.1016
(907)   In the third place, the Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive
        pressure exerted by existing carriers on the route was corroborated by the responses
         to the Commission’s market investigation, where the majority of competitors that
        expressed a view consider that Lufthansa and ITA are closer competitors of each
         other on the Milan-Hamburg city pair compared to Ryanair.1017 Moreover, the
        majority of competitor respondents that expressed a view consider that the Parties
       compete closely on the route based on a number of criteria (e.g., prices, frequencies,
        on-board services, time of departure and arrival etc.) and in general.1018

        Telecoms, judgment of 13 July 2023,  the Commission is not required to establish that the Parties are

         particularly close competitors in a concentrated market can result in a significant impediment to

(908)   Seventh, as further explained in section 9.1.4, there are several barriers to entry and
        expansion on the route.
(909)   In  the  first  place,  the  relevant  airports  are  to an  extent  congested. This  is
        demonstrated by  the  fact  that,  all LIN, MXP, BGY and HAM  are Level 3
        Coordinated Airports.1019
(910)   Moreover, the average congestion rate per hour band data for Summer IATA Season
       2023 at LIN ranges between 73% and 98% between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm, whereas
          at MXP, it ranges between 40% and 85%.1020
(911)   The average congestion level per hour band for the scheduled weekly flights of
        Lufthansa on the Milan-Hamburg city pair are as follows: from MXP ranging
       between 52-72% and from HAM between 0-40% during Summer IATA Season
        2023. During Winter IATA Season 2022/2023, average congestion levels from MXP
        ranged between 38-72% and from HAM between 0-30%.1021
(912)   Similarly, the average congestion level per hour band for the scheduled weekly
          flights of ITA on the Milan-Hamburg city pair are as follows: from LIN ranging
       between 74-82% and from HAM between 27-53% during Summer IATA Season
         2023.1022
(913)   The above figures indicate that LIN is significantly slot constrained (including during
         the time of operation of the Parties), MXP has some slot constraints at peak times,
        whereas both the latter and HAM have some spare capacity for new entrants and
        incumbents to grow.
(914)  On the Milan end, the results of the Commission’s market investigation, strongly
        support the airlines’ preference for LIN and indicate that barriers to entry at the
         airport are significantly high due to the slot congestion at the specific airport. Despite
         the fact that the Milan catchment area is served by several airports (i.e., MXP and
         likely BGY), based on the  results of  the Commission’s market  investigation,
        competitors consider that slots at LIN give a strong competitive advantage to those
      who operate them, due to  its strategic location and proximity to the city centre
       compared to MXP (see section 6.5.3.6 above, section 11 below, and paragraph (655)
          et seq.). Therefore, the inability of competitors to obtain slots at LIN is considered a
         significant  barrier  to  entry,  despite  the  availability  of  slots  at MXP.  (See
         section 9.1.4.1 and 9.1.4.2above for more information). In the second place, the
         Parties’ combined slot holding will be significantly high in LIN and high in HAM. In
          particular,  in LIN,  the  Parties’ combined  slot  holding  in 2022 amounted  to
        62.4-65.4%1023 whereas  in HAM,  the  Parties’ combined  slot holding  in 2022
       amounted to 51%.1024 In both airports, the Parties’ combined slot holdings may in
           itself be evidence of dominance and therefore could act as a barrier to entry and
        expansion in the Milan-Frankfurt city. Despite the fact that both the Milan and
       Hamburg catchment  areas  are  served by  several  airports,  the  results  of  the

       Commission’s market investigation and internal documents of the Parties support
         that (i)“there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their
         local airport”1025 and thus entering a secondary airport would not allow competitors
         to compete closely with the Parties (see section 9.1.2.2 above for more information);
       and that (ii) Lufthansa uses its strong market position in primary airports to eliminate
        competition on both primary and secondary airports of the same catchment area. (See
         section 9.1.4.2 above for more information and in particular Figure 54).
(915)   In the third place, the Parties’ high combined market share on the route Milan-
       Hamburg city pair is indicative of dominance over the summer seasons and therefore
        could act as a barrier to entry and expansion in the Milan-Hamburg city pair. (See
         section 9.1.4.2 above for more information).
(916)   Eighth, no further, likely, timely and sufficient entry or expansion of competitors is
        expected on this route. The Commission has analysed the entry plans of all relevant
         potential competitors which, taken individually and as a whole, do not support that
         the concentration on the route would be offset by future market entry, or indeed that
       any market entry would occur at all.
(917)   In the first place, TUI Fly confirms that it does not plan on entering the route MIL-
     HAM. 1026
(918)   In the second place, Wizz Air’s potential entry is conditional ‘[p]ending access to
        LIN’, for which ‘Wizz Air clarifies that it applied for slots (…) under the normal
        seasonal procedure as it does every season, however, it has not been able to change
         the times it already has or to obtain new slots, so such an entry would be conditional
       on obtaining the necessary slots’.1027 Therefore, it appears that Wizz Air would only
        consider entry if  it would gain access to suitable slots in LIN, which  it currently
        cannot do. On this basis Wizz Air’s submission is not considered as indicative of a
         timely, likely or sufficient potential entry.
(919)   In the third place, other potential entry and/or expansion plans are subject to the
       outcome of the Transaction, and thus are not considered as indicative of a timely,
         likely or sufficient entry.1028 In other words, the results of the Commission’s market
         investigation are that potential entrants are only considering potential actions on this
         route.  In  particular,  the Commission did not  find  that  potential  entrants had
        developed specific plans or adopted preparatory steps to enter these routes, and the
        generic planning that it did find lacked detail and was typically subject to numerous
        caveats and conditions.1029 (See section 9.1.5 above for more information.) Ninth,
         there is specific evidence showing that the Transaction is likely to result in negative
          effects.

(920)   In the first place, while a sizeable share of the respondents indicated that they did not
       know, the vast majority of competitors active on short-haul routes and expressing an
        opinion considered the impact of the Transaction on the route to be negative.1030
       While the views of customers on the impact of the Transaction on this route are
         overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion of responding customers
        consider the impact to be negative.1031 In addition, several market participants have
         identified negative effects stemming from Lufthansa’s past acquisitions of short-haul
         carriers in the EEA (see Section 7.7.4 for more detailed results).
(921)   In the second place, a finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is in line with the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a short-haul route as well as the
         elimination of competition by ITA is associated with significantly higher prices (see
        Section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).
(922)   In the third place, the finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is also in line with the internal documents of Lufthansa predicting price
         increases, including […] (see Section 7.7.1).
9.2.4.4. Conclusion
(923)   In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion,
         the lack of prospect of likely, timely and sufficient entry on the route and the specific
        evidence on the likely negative effects of the Transaction, the Commission concludes
         that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on the route
       Milan - Hamburg by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in the summer
      IATA season, under any plausible market definition.

9.2.5.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(933)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that the only airlines serving the route Milan-Stuttgart
        based on Summer 2023 data are Lufthansa (through Eurowings), ITA and Ryanair, in
          light of a number of exits from the market in previous years, namely by easyJet,
       Laudamotion and Air Berlin.1034 According to Lufthansa and MEF, Ryanair, is a
        strong competitor in the market, as it managed to gain a significant market share
       from the beginning of  its operations.1035 Moreover, the Parties also submit that
        Ryanair expanded its capacity on the route, from 120 overall in Summer IATA 2023
         to 154 overall frequencies in Summer IATA 2024.1036 Furthermore, the Parties
        consider that they also compete with the indirect daily train connection offered by
         Trenitalia and Deutsche Bahn, of average travel time 7h31min,1037 and that the
         attractiveness of this train connection is evident from the eight daily frequencies
         offered.1038 In addition, Lufthansa and MEF submit that there are no barriers to entry
        and/or expansion on the route Milan-Stuttgart either as a result of the Parties’
       combined slot holdings or average congestion rates in the Milan and Stuttgart
          airports.

        Transaction will have an impact on competition or that the Transaction would have a
         neutral impact on the Milan – Stuttgart route.1043

(946)   The Commission notes that in case CRL on the Brussels end of the route would be
        considered a separate geographic market, there would be no need to assess the CRL-
      Rome routes separately, as there would be no overlap arising because of the activities
        of  the  Parties.  Therefore,  the only  alternative  plausible  overlap concerns  the
        catchment area including only BRU on the Brussels end of the route, which would be
         the narrowest plausible market definition.
(947)   All alternative market definitions (including the narrowest possible one as identified
         in the previous paragraph) would result in the same outcome: a decrease in Ryanair’s
        presence. Consequently, the concerns outlined in the Commission’s assessment
       below would not only continue  to be  relevant under  the narrowest  plausible
         alternative market definition which  limits the relevant market to BRU on the
        Brussels end of the route, but would be amplified due to the decrease in Ryanair’s
        presence in the competitive landscape, the increased market shares of Lufthansa and
      ITA and the same or increased barriers to entry and expansion.
(948)   The Table below, sets out the Parties and their competitors’ market shares under the
        narrowest alternative possible market definition.

9.2.6.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(949)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that the main airlines serving the route Rome-Brussels
        based on Summer 2023 data are Lufthansa (through Brussels Airlines), ITA and
        Ryanair. According to the Parties, Ryanair is the market leader on the route, holding
        market shares above 50% in the last two IATA seasons. Lufthansa and MEF further
         elaborate that Ryanair has bases in FCO, CIA and CRL and although it closed its
        base in BRU due to a regulatory fee’s increase, it continues to serve this airport with
          aircrafts based outside Belgium. Moreover, the Parties submit that the merged entity
         will be constrained by potential entrants such as Vueling, who would not face any
          slot restriction at either side of the route that could prevent them from entering.1050
        Lufthansa and MEF  further emphasize  that Ryanair exerts a high competitive
         constraint on Lufthansa and ITA on this route, while Vueling, Transavia and Wizz
        Air may enter the route. The Parties also highlight that barriers to entry on this route
         are limited in terms of slot congestion in BRU and airport charges in BRU.1051 In
          their Response to the SO, the Parties further argue that the Commission fails to take
         into account the competitive dynamics, in particular the competitive pressure exerted
       by Ryanair. The Parties consider that their market shares are “moderately high” and
         refer to Ryanair as a leading player, and the closest competitor of the Parties. The
         Parties also note that in their view any alleged frequency advantage over Ryanair
        cannot be a concern on this route. The Parties also note that the Commission’s
        concerns are not in line with its previous case practice. The Parties also argue that the
       Commission should consider potential future entries on this route and a different
         interpretation of the results of the market investigations (one that takes “I do not
       know” or lack of responses into account). The Parties also argue that in the market
         investigation two responses regarding the Rome-Brussels route have been redacted
        without providing a sufficient non-confidential description of the content.1052

9.2.6.3. The Commission’s assessment
(950)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes, that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome –
        Brussels and, in any event as a result of the elimination of important competitive
         constraints that ITA had exerted on Lufthansa on the route Rome-Brussels.
(951)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very large combined
        market share on the route. As set out in Table 40, the Parties’ combined market share
       by number of passengers travelled is very large or at least large and ranges from
       40-56% between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024.
         Overall, these market shares indicate that the Parties would have notable market
       power after the Transaction.1053 The increment brought by the Transaction is also
         large, at 16-20%.
(952)   Moreover, based on the market share data in Table 41 the Parties’ combined market
        share by capacity (number of seats) is higher, and ranges from 45 to 62% between
      Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024. The increment
        brought  by  the  Transaction   is  also  large  or  particularly  large,  ranging
       between 22-34%.
(953)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      16% to 20% (by passenger) in the last five IATA seasons. This corresponds to a high
         increase in the HHI of between 811 and 1 417, in line with the Commission’s
        Horizontal Merger Guidelines.1054
(954)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be higher than 5 000 in each of the last five IATA seasons (with an increment of at
          least 811) based on PAX number. The high combined market share of the Parties, the
         large increment brought by the transaction, the high change in HHI and high HHI
        post-Transaction indicate that the Transaction would create or strengthen a dominant
         position.
(955)   Fourth,  even when  looking  into  the  widest  possible  market  definition,  the
        Transaction constitutes a 3-to-2 merger for non-stop  flights. In addition to the
          Parties, only Ryanair operates the Rome-Brussels city pair, and held a market share
        of 44% in the Summer IATA Season 2023 and 57% in the Winter IATA Season
       2023/2024 based on the number of passengers. Ryanair’s market share is similar or
        lower (depending on the IATA Season) based on capacity, ranging between 47%
       and 37% between Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and Summer IATA Season 2024.
        Ryanair operated the Rome-Brussels city pair from CIA to CRL and FCO to BRU.
(956)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
       on both IATA Seasons the largest operator on the Rome-Brussels city pair in terms
        of capacity operated and, holding a significant market share on both IATA Seasons,
         in terms of passengers, with Ryanair being the Parties’ only active competitor.

       and a delta below 250, or a merger with a post-merger HHI above 2000 and a delta below 150, except
       where special circumstances” arise.

(957)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route (i.e. Ryanair) is
         likely  to be  insufficient  to  eliminate  the  significant impediment  to  effective
        competition caused by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair is
         unlikely to be sufficient to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(958)   In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair operates on the market with market shares between 44% and 60% for the
          latest five seasons.
(959)   In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture approximately 20% of the market with less than 3 years of operation and has
       competed closely with Lufthansa on the route in the past. The Commission notes,
         that contrary to the Parties Response to the SO, while Ryanair is relevant for the
        assessment of the competitive dynamics on the Rome-Brussels route, ITA remains an
        important  competitive  constraint  of  Lufthansa  on  this  route  based  on  the
       Commission’s assessment.1055
(960)   Notably, LCC/ULCC carriers such as Ryanair tend to operate lower frequencies
       compared to network carriers such as Lufthansa or ITA, which in turn means that
        Ryanair is present on the market with lower capacities (fewer planes flying fewer
          trips) and  less choice for customers (fewer planes flying fewer times a day).
        According to a Parties’ submission and based on Summer IATA 2024 data, for the
       summer seasons, the Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 32 weekly frequencies
        (18 operated by Lufthansa and 14 operated by ITA) as compared to the 17 weekly
        frequencies of Ryanair.1056 Similarly based on Winter IATA 2023/2024 data, for the
        winter seasons, the Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 30 weekly frequencies
        (15 operated by Lufthansa and 15 operated by ITA) as compared to the 24 weekly
        frequencies of Ryanair.1057 The Commission takes the view that contrary to the
         Parties argument, which considers  that  this frequency advantage cannot be a
        “meaningful concern”, the additional frequencies operated by the Parties render it
       more likely that customers find a flight-time which  fits  their travel plans and
        purposes, which gives Lufthansa and ITA a clear advantage over Ryanair.1058
(961)    Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
        not  only compete  closely on  this  route  but,  they  are  each  other’s  closest
         competitor.1059
(962)   In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa (Brussels Airlines) are both network carriers
        operating similar business models and attracting similar types of passengers, whereas
        Ryanair is an ULCC, operating a P2P business model and focused on leisure travel.
       The Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive pressure exerted by

(974)   Eighth,  at  this stage of the investigation, based on the available evidence, the
       Commission  is not able to conclude that Lufthansa’s and MEF’s allegations as
        regards potential competitive constraints (potential entrants such as Vueling – as
        noted by the Parties)1077 would be sufficient to counter the likely negative effects of

       Commission to conclude that there is timely, likely or sufficient potential entry or
        expansion in the Rome-Brussels city pair, post-Transaction.1078 In other words, the

        considering potential actions on this route. In particular, the Commission did not find

        opinion considered the impact of the Transaction on the route to be negative.1080
       While the views of customers on the impact of the Transaction on this route are
         overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion of responding customers
        consider the impact to be negative.1081 In addition, several market participants have
         identified negative effects stemming from Lufthansa’s past acquisitions of short-haul
         carriers in the EEA (see Section 7.7.3 for more detailed results).

        negative is in line with the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a short-haul route as well as the
         elimination of competition by ITA is associated with significantly higher prices (see
        Section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).

9.2.6.4. Conclusion
(979)   In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very large or at
          least large combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction,
         the overall concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by
         competitors, the fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to
         entry and the lack of prospect of likely, timely and sufficient entry on the route, the
       Commission concludes that the Transaction would significantly impede effective
        competition as a result of the creation or strengthening of a dominant position in both
         the Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition on the
         route Rome-Brussels by removing the competition exerted by ITA on the market. In
       any  event, and  for  these same  reasons,  the Commission  concludes  that  the
        Transaction would significantly impede effective competition as a result of the
         elimination of important competitive constraints that ITA had exerted on Lufthansa
       on the route Rome-Brussels.

(982)  On the Rome-Frankfurt city pair the following plausible alternative geographic
        market definitions exist based on the catchment areas:
          (a)  On the Rome end of the route FCO and CIA belong to one catchment area (See
               section 6.5.3.9 above).
         (b)  On the Frankfurt end of the route FRA and HHN may belong to one catchment
              area or HHN may be considered as a separate market from FRA (See
               section 6.5.3.4 above).
(983)   The  Commission’s  assessment  below  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, which includes FRA and HHN on the Frankfurt end of the route and FCO
       and CIA on the Rome end of the route.
(984)   However, the assessment below would remain applicable even in case the market
       would be defined more narrowly, encompassing fewer airports (i.e. only FRA or
     HHN on the Frankfurt end of the route).
(985)   The Commission notes that in case HHN on the Frankfurt end of the route would be
        considered a separate geographic market, there would be no need to assess the HHN-
      Rome route separately, as there would be no overlap arising because of the activities
        of  the  Parties.  Therefore,  the only  alternative  plausible  overlap concerns  the
        catchment area including only FRA on the Frankfurt end of the route.
(986)   This alternative possible market definition (which would be the narrowest plausible
        market definition), would result in the removal of Ryanair from the competitive
        landscape. Consequently, the concerns outlined in the Commission’s assessment
       below would not only continue to be relevant under any plausible alternative market
         definition which limits the relevant market to FRA on the Frankfurt end of the route,
        but would be amplified due  to the removal of Ryanair from the competitive
        landscape  (i.e., the Transaction would be a merger-to-monopoly), the increased
        market shares of Lufthansa and ITA and the same or increased barriers to entry and
        expansion.

9.2.7.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(989)   Lufthansa and MEF submit that Ryanair, ITA and Lufthansa (under the Lufthansa
        brand) were the main airlines operating the route Rome-Frankfurt in Summer and
        Winter 2022 IATA seasons. According to the Parties, the merged entity will face
        strong competition from Ryanair which has the ability and the incentive to further
       expand even though it did not operate the route Rome-Frankfurt in Summer 2023
         (but will resume its operations in the Winter 2023 IATA season) and decided to close
           its base at FRA due to charges’ increase. They further elaborate that the merged
         entity will be constrained by potential entry of airlines such as Wizz Air, Vueling or
         easyJet, which would not face slot restrictions that could prevent them from entering
         the route.1084 The Parties further highlight that ITA’s increment on this route is low,
        while Ryanair is active on the route and constrains Lufthansa and ITA significantly.
       The Parties also emphasize that new entrants may enter the route and that new
         constructions at FRA may alleviate barriers to entry.1085 In the Response to the SO,
         the  Parties highlighted  that Ryanair must be considered as a well-established,
        constant and relevant competitor on this route as  it has restarted  its operations
        following  the “pause”  of  the Summer IATA Season 2023. The  Parties  also
        emphasize that Ryanair’s market share on this route is above ITA’s and that during
         the market investigation several competitors have indicated that Ryanair is one of the
         closest competitors of Lufthansa and ITA on this route. The Parties also refer to the
         fact that Ryanair has increased its capacities on the route, moreover, they claim that
         the route is attractive for airlines such as Wizz Air and Vueling, which have a base in
      FCO. The Parties also explain that barriers to entry are limited in light of the
         construction of a new terminal in FRA. The Parties also argue that the Commission

9.2.7.3. The Commission’s assessment
(990)   For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome –
         Frankfurt.
(991)    First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 43 below, the Parties’ combined market share
       by number of passengers travelled is very high and ranges from 66-100% between
        Winter IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024. The increment
        brought by the Transaction is also sizeable or large, reaching up to 19%. These
        market shares indicate that the Parties would hold a dominant position after the
         Transaction.
(992)   Moreover, based on the market share data in Table 44, the Parties’ combined market
        share by capacity (number of seats operated) is even higher, ranging between 86%
       and 100% in Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024. The
        increment brought by the Transaction is sizeable or large in most years and also the
          last two seasons, reaching up to15% starting with Summer IATA Season 2023. The
       Commission highlights that with the exception of Summer IATA Season 2022 and
        Winter IATA Season 2022/03, the market share increment was significant and
         generally show a growth tendency, therefore the Commission cannot conclude that
         the market share increment appears to be limited.
(993)   Under both indications, the Parties’ combined market shares could be indicative of a
       dominant position.
(994)   Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
     2% to 19% (by passenger) in the last five IATA seasons. This corresponds to a high
         increase in the HHI of up to 3 067 in line with the Commission’s Horizontal Merger
         Guidelines.1087
(995)   Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be higher than 5 000 in each of the last five IATA seasons (with an increment of at
          least 257) based on PAX number. Furthermore, even when looking into the widest
         possible market definition, the Transaction constitutes a 3-to-2 merger for non-stop
          flights. The high combined market share of the Parties, the large increment brought
       by the transaction, the high change in HHI and high HHI post-Transaction indicate
         that the Transaction would create or strengthen a dominant position.
(996)   Fourth, even when looking into the widest possible market definition (i.e., one which
        includes FCO and CIA on the Rome end of the route, and FRA and HHN on the

(997)   In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction, the Parties will become
       by far the largest operator on the Rome-Frankfurt route, holding a very large market
        share in terms of both passengers and capacity operated, with Ryanair being the
         Parties’ only currently active competitor. While Ryanair is a competitor relevant for
         the Commission’s competitive assessment, its capacity is very limited compared to
         that of the Parties, and moreover, it has a history of suspending operations on this
         route as explained above in paragraph (993).1089
(998)   The Commission notes that even if Ryanair’s activities would remain stable or show
        a growth tendency (which the Commission could not confirm during  its market
         investigation), the competitive constraint exerted by Ryanair would remain limited,
       due to the relatively low market shares, the  fact  that Ryanair  is a  less close
        competitor of the Parties than they are to each other (see section 9.1.2), and the
         particularly high distance and limited connectivity between Frankfurt and HHN
       compared to Frankfurt and FRA (see more details in sections 9.1.2 and 6.5 above).
(999)    Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair is unlikely to be sufficient
         to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(1000)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair operates on the market with market shares between <1% and 32% for the
          latest five seasons.
(1001)  In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture approximately 15-20% of the market with less than 3 years of operation and
        has competed closely with Lufthansa on the route in the past.
(1002)  In the third place, the Parties would hold a significant frequency advantage over the
        only  other  direct  competitor on  the  route,  Ryanair. According  to  a  Parties’
        submission and based on Summer IATA 2024 data, for the summer seasons, the
         Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 46 weekly frequencies (34 operated by
        Lufthansa and 12 operated by ITA) as compared to the 2 weekly frequencies of
        Ryanair. Similarly based on Winter IATA 2023/2024 data, for the winter seasons, the
         Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 35 weekly frequencies (28 operated by

(1003)  Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
        not  only compete  closely on  this  route  but,  they  are  each  other’s  closest
         competitor.1091
(1004)  In the  first place, ITA and Lufthansa (Lufthansa Passenger Airlines) are both
        network carriers operating similar business models and attracting similar types of
        passengers, whereas Ryanair is an ULCC operating a P2P business model focused on
         leisure travel. The Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive pressure
        exerted by existing carriers on the route was corroborated by the responses to the
       Commission’s market investigation, where, while some competitors noted Ryanair as
         the closest competitor, the majority of competitors that expressed a view consider
         that Lufthansa and ITA are closer competitors to each other on the Rome-Frankfurt
         city pair compared to Ryanair.1092 (See section 9.1.2.1 above for more information).
(1005)  In the second place, ITA and Lufthansa operate the Rome-Frankfurt route from the
       same airports in Rome (FCO) and Frankfurt (FRA), whereas Ryanair operates this
         route on the Frankfurt side exclusively at HHN (until Summer 2022 IATA Season,
        Ryanair operated the route CIA-HHN, and moved its operations to FCO-HHN in
        both Winter 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 IATA  Seasons).  In  this  context,  the
       Commission’s market investigation supports the view that airlines operating a city
         pair from neighbouring airports do not compete as closely with airlines operating the
       same city pair from the same airports.
(1006)  For  example,  Air France-KLM  explains  that  “Frankfurt Hahn  is  closer  to
       Luxembourg than Frankfurt (situated 1h35 min by car from [F]rankfurt center). It
        has no facility to operate large traffic flows. It has around 2.5m pax per year for the
       moment in comparison to close to 70m for FRA. Only Wizz and Ryanair are
        operating from HHN on a very low frequency basis and to leisure destinations only.
      Hahn is only reachable by Bus in 2hours from Frankfurt city. Frankfurt airport is
        located close to the city and also reachable easily from Mainz/Wiesbaden and
       Darmstadt which are the four main cities to contribute locally. HAHN cannot play
         that role. FRA [M]ain airport operates a state of the art train station with hundreds
         of high-speed and regional train per day connecting FRA [A]irport to rest of
       Germany, It is one of the main station for Deutsche Bahn.(…)”.1093 While in the case
        of Rome the difference between FCO and CIA is less clear cut, nevertheless easyJet
        explained that FCO may be more attractive for airlines compared to CIA (See
        paragraph (962) above).1094

(1007)  Lastly, the Commission notes that the overall travel times submitted by the Parties
        (considering the travel time from city centre to city centre on both ends of the route)
         also show that airlines operating a city pair from secondary airports of proximity do
        not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same primary
          airports. Notably, the overall travel time considering FCO and FRA (ITA and
        Lufthansa present) is around 2 hours. 31-41 minutes. In contrast the overall travel
        time is approx. 3 hours and 41 minutes when considering FCO and HHN (Ryanair
         present). This shows that Lufthansa and ITA compete closely with each other
        considering the shorter travel times than they do with Ryanair.1095
(1008)  Seventh, as further explained in section 9.1.4, there are several barriers to entry and
        expansion on the route.

        Airport and HHN is a Level 1 Non-Coordinated Airport.1096

       2023 at FCO ranges between 1% and 74% between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm, at CIA

       and 79%, 54% and 102%, and 54% and 102%.1097

        Winter IATA Season 2022/2023, the average congestion level per hour band for the
        scheduled weekly  flights of Lufthansa on the Rome-Frankfurt city pair are as
         follows: from FCO ranging between 36-44%, and from BRU between 41-55%.1098
(1012)  Similarly, the average congestion level per hour band for the scheduled weekly
          flights of ITA on the Rome-Frankfurt city pair are as follows: from FCO during
      Summer IATA Season 2023 ranging between 53-68% and from FRA between
       87-102%. ITA did not provide the relevant information for Winter IATA Season
        2022/2023.1099

        confirms that “FRA is generally not slot congested (apart from some peak hours1
       where it is slightly congested) (See section 9.1.4 above for more information).

       would consider that all barriers (including charges, the behaviour of other airlines
          etc.) would be necessarily alleviated or fully negated by the expansion of the
        capacity of FRA, or that  (iii) any of the considerations outlined above by the
       Commission would be significantly affected as a result of this construction project.
        Therefore, the Commission could not confirm the Parties’ statements that new
         entrants may enter the route due to the new constructions at FRA and in general that
      new constructions at FRA may alleviate barriers to entry.

9.2.7.4. Conclusion
(1024)  In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and the lack of
        prospect  of  likely, timely and  sufficient  entry on  the  route,  the Commission
        concludes that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on
         the route Rome – Frankfurt by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in both
         the Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition.

(1027) On the Rome-Munich city pair the following plausible alternative geographic market
         definitions exist based on the catchment areas:
          (a)  On the Rome end of the route FCO and CIA belong to one catchment area (See
               section 6.5.3.9 6.5.3.9 above).
         (b)  On the Munich end of the route MUC and FMM may belong to one catchment
              area or FMM may be considered as a separate market from MUC (See
               section 6.5.3.7 above).
(1028)  The  Commission’s  assessment  below  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, which includes MUC and FMM on the Munich end of the route, and FCO
       and CIA on the Rome end of the route.
(1029)  However, the assessment below would remain applicable even in case the market
       would be defined more narrowly, encompassing fewer airports (e.g. potentially only
     MUC or FMM on the Munich end of the route). The Commission notes that in case
     FMM would be considered a separate geographic market, there would be no need to
         assess the FMM-Rome route separately, as there would be no overlap arising because
         of the activities of the Parties. Therefore, the only alternative plausible overlap
        concerns the catchment area including only MUC on the Munich end of the route.
(1030)  The alternative market definition (which would be the narrowest plausible market
         definition), would result in the following outcome: the removal of Ryanair and Wizz
        Air from the competitive landscape. Consequently, the concerns outlined in the
       Commission’s assessment below would not only continue to be relevant under
        narrower alternative market definition which limits the relevant market to MUC on
         the Munich end of the route, but would be amplified due to the removal of Ryanair
       and Wizz Air from the competitive landscape  (i.e., the Transaction would be a
        merger-to-monopoly), the increased market shares of Lufthansa and ITA and the
       same or increased barriers to entry and expansion.

9.2.8.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(1032)  Lufthansa’s and MEF’s view Lufthansa and MEF submit that ITA and Lufthansa
        (under the Lufthansa brand) were the only airlines operating the route Rome-Munich
         in Winter 2022, while Wizz Air and Ryanair entered the route in Summer 2023.
        According to the Parties, the merged entity will increasingly be constrained by these
       two competitors which are likely to grow, and by potential new entrants such as
        Vueling or easyJet which already operated  this route and would not face  slot
          restrictions at either side of the route. The Parties finally argue that the direct night
          train connection between Munich and Rome operated by ÖBB and Trenitalia could
         offer a viable alternative for costs and ecological sensitive travellers.1112 The Parties
         further emphasize the limited increment on this route, refer to the competitive
         constraint exerted by the relatively new entrant ULCCs and consider that the barriers
         to entry and expansion are limited.1113 The Parties also submit that Ryanair has
        almost doubled its capacity for the Summer 2024 IATA Season compared to that of
         the Summer 2023 IATA Season.1114 In the Response to the SO, the Parties argue that
         the Commission fails to capture the fierce competition with Ryanair and Wizz Air as
      new entrants on this route, which continue to constrain Lufthansa and ITA going
        forward, despite of their high combined market share. The Parties also highlight that
         the market shares of Lufthansa and ITA have been declining and that with Ryanair
       and Wizz Air present, the Transaction would lead to a 4-to-3 situation. The Parties
        explain that the Ryanair and Wizz Air increased their frequencies over Summer
      IATA 2024 and have a are higher market share than the increment ITA represents,
       and that therefore their presence will very likely be sufficient to constrain Lufthansa
       and ITA post-Transaction. The Parties also refer to the fact that both Ryanair and
       Wizz Air have been expanding on this route. In addition, the Parties argue that the
         travel time difference between MUC and FMM does not lead to LCC’s being less
         close competitors of Lufthansa and ITA. Instead, Ryanair and Wizz Air are also
         targeting business customers and flying at business friendly hours. The Parties also
        argue that the Commission should consider a different interpretation of the results of
         the market investigations (one that takes “I do not know” or lack of responses into
         account).1115
9.2.8.3. The Commission’s assessment
(1033)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome –
       Munich.
(1034)  First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in in Table 46, the Parties’ combined market share by
       number of passengers travelled is very high and ranges from 74-100% between
      Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024. These market
        shares indicate that the Parties would hold a dominant position after the Transaction.
(1035)  Moreover, based on the market share data in Table 47 the Parties’ combined market
        share by capacity (number of frequencies) is also very high, and ranges from 88
         to 100% between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024.

       The increment brought by  the Transaction  is  also  sizeable  or  large, ranging

(1036)  Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      18% to 22% (by passenger) in the last five IATA seasons. While the increment
       somewhat decreased in the latest IATA Season for which data is available, it remains
         significant at 14% (pax) and 20% (capacity), therefore the Commission cannot
        conclude that the increment is limited. This corresponds to a high increase in the HHI
        of between 1 640 and 3 545, in line with the Commission’s Horizontal Merger
         Guidelines.1116
(1037)  Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be higher than 5 000 during each of the last five IATA seasons (with an increment of
          at least 1 640) based on PAX number. The high combined market share of the
          Parties, the large increment brought by the transaction, the high change in HHI and
        high HHI post-Transaction indicate that the Transaction would create or strengthen a
       dominant position.
(1038)  Fourth, even when looking into the widest possible market definition (i.e., one which
        includes FCO and CIA on the Rome end of the route, and MUC and FMM on the
        Brussels end), the Transaction constitutes a 4-to-3 merger for non-stop flights. in
         addition to the Parties, only Ryanair and Wizz Air operate between the Rome-
       Munich city pair.1117 The competitive constraint of Ryanair and Wizz Air would
        remain  limited  post-Transaction  for  the  reasons  explained  in  the  following
         paragraphs.1118
(1039)  Ryanair held a market share of 12% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and 9%
         in the Summer IATA Season 2023. In terms of capacity (number of seats), Ryanair’s
        market share is significantly lower, as it held 6% in Winter 2023/2024 IATA Season
       and will hold a market share of 7% in the Summer IATA Season 2024.
(1040)  Wizz Air held a market share of 14% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and 4%
         in the Summer IATA Season 2023. In terms of capacity (number of seats), Wizz
         Air’s market share is significantly lower, as it held 6% in Winter 2023/2024 IATA
       Season and will hold a market share of 8% in the Summer IATA Season 2024.
(1041)  In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operator on the Rome-Munich city pair, holding a very significant market
        share on both IATA Seasons, in terms of passengers and capacity operated, with
        Ryanair and Wizz Air being the Parties’ only active competitors. The Commission
         also notes, that while the Parties’ market shares have been declining in the recent
        years due to the entry of Ryanair and Wizz Air, they continue to hold very high
       combined market shares. In addition, it is unlikely that the growth of Ryanair and
       Wizz Air on this route would result in further significant decline in the market shares
        of the Parties (combined market shares below 40-50%) considering among others the
         capacities / frequencies flown by these low cost competitors, which together amount

(1042)  Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of Ryanair and Wizz Air is unlikely to
        be sufficient to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(1043)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
        Ryanair and Wizz Air operate on the market with market shares between 1% and
      12% for Ryanair and 4% and 14% for Wizz Air for the latest five seasons.
(1044)  In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
        Ryanair post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination of an
        important competitive constraint, in the form of ITA, an airline that managed to
        capture approximately 15-20% of the market with less than 3 years of operation and
        has competed closely with Lufthansa on the route in the past.
(1045)  In the third place, the Parties would hold a frequency advantage over the other direct
        competitors on the route, namely Ryanair and Wizz Air. According to a Parties’
        submission and based on Summer IATA 2024 data, for the summer seasons, the
         Parties would, post-Transaction, operate 44 weekly frequencies (32 operated by
        Lufthansa and 12 operated by ITA) as compared to the 3 weekly frequencies of
        Ryanair and 3 weekly frequencies of Wizz Air. Similarly based on Winter IATA
       2023/2024 data, for the winter seasons, the Parties would, post-Transaction, operate
       40 weekly frequencies (33 operated by Lufthansa and 7 operated by ITA) as
       compared to the 2 weekly frequencies of Ryanair and 2 weekly frequencies of Wizz
          Air.1120
(1046)  Sixth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
        not  only compete  closely on  this  route  but,  they  are  each  other’s  closest
         competitor.1121
(1047)  In the first place, ITA and Lufthansa are both network carriers operating similar
        business models and attracting similar types of passengers, whereas Ryanair and
       Wizz Air are ULCCs, operating a P2P business model and focused on leisure travel.
       The Commission’s assessment with respect to the competitive pressure exerted by
         existing carriers on the route was corroborated by the responses to the Commission’s
        market investigation, where the majority of competitors that expressed a view
        consider that Lufthansa and ITA are closer competitors of each other on the Rome-

        operating a city pair from neighbouring airports do not compete as closely with
          airlines operating the same city pair from the same airports. For instance, specifically
        with regards to MUC and FMM, Ryanair noted that there is only “very limited

       Commission’s market investigation believe that the closest alternative of Lufthansa’s

       Wizz Air.1126 (See section 9.1.5 above for more information.)
(1051)  Lastly, the Commission notes that the overall travel times submitted by the Parties
        (considering the travel time from city centre to city centre on both ends of the route)
         also show that airlines operating a city pair from secondary airports of proximity do
        not compete as closely with airlines operating a route from the same primary
          airports. Notably, the overall travel time considering FCO and MUC (ITA and
        Lufthansa present) is around 2 hours and 31 minutes. In contrast the overall travel
        time is approx. 3 hours 6-11 minutes when considering FCO and FMM (Ryanair and
       Wizz Air present). This shows that Lufthansa and ITA compete closely with each
         other considering the shorter travel times than they do with Ryanair and Wizz
          Air.1127

       and ITA on the Rome – Munich routes to some extent, and some customers,

(1053)  Seventh, as further explained in section 9.1.4, there are several barriers to entry and

         follows: from FCO ranging between 43-63%, and from MUC between 31-62%.1131
(1057)  Similarly, the average congestion level per hour band for the scheduled weekly
          flights of ITA on the Rome-Munich city pair are as follows: from FCO during

       where it is difficult to expand operations. As an example, AF-KLM notes that MUC
           is a highly constrained airport as it is one of Lufthansa’s hubs.1134

(1060)  In the second place, the Parties’ combined market share on the route and combined
          slot holding in FCO and in MUC will be significantly high, indicative of market
       power and will act as a barrier to entry and expansion. Despite the fact that the
       Munich catchment area  is potentially served by two airports, the results of the
       Commission’s market investigation and internal documents of the Parties support
         that (i) “there is a general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their
         local airport”1135 and thus entering a secondary airport would not allow competitors
         to compete closely with the Parties (see section 9.1.2.2 above for more information);
       and that (ii) Lufthansa uses its strong market position in primary airports to eliminate
        competition on both primary and secondary airports of the same catchment area. (See
         section 9.1.4.2 above for more information and in particular Figure 54).
(1061)  Eighth, the available train connection on the Rome Munich route is a night train,
       which – according to the Parties – takes approx. 13 hours of travel time.1136 As
        explained in more detail in Section 6.8 above, neither Lufthansa or ITA, nor train
         operators would consider  that night  trains with such  travel times would exert
         significant competitive pressure on direct flights. In addition, within the framework
        of  the Commission’s market  investigation,  all  competitors  expressing a view
        considered that very few passengers (<10%) consider air and train services as close
         substitutes on the Rome-Munich route even considering a potential permanent price
         increase of 5-10%, and, moreover, the majority of those customers expressing a view
        submitted the same response.1137 Therefore, the Commission’s market investigation
        suggests that night trains do not exert sufficient competitive constraint on the Rome-
       Munich route and, therefore, they do not affect the above assessment.
(1062)  Ninth, while Ryanair appears to have expanded its capacities from Summer IATA
       Season 2023 to Summer IATA Season 2024 on this route, it is unclear whether such
         increase in capacity  is a lasting one, which will continue throughout both the
      Summer and Winter IATA Seasons, especially considering Ryanair’s submission
         highlighting that “[f]uture growth [on this route]  is entirely contingent on the
        Transaction and any remedies put in place.”1138 Even if Ryanair would continue to
         increase capacity, Lufthansa and ITA would still likely hold very high market shares
       on this route. Moreover, even if Ryanair would continue increasing capacities on this
         route, it would remain a less close competitor of Lufthansa compared to ITA, first
       and foremost due to the fact that  it operates from a secondary  / regional airport,
         rather than the same airport as Lufthansa. Therefore, the Commission considers that
         the assessment above applies even considering potential increases in Ryanair’s
         capacity.

       Commission  is not able to conclude that Lufthansa’s and MEF’s allegations as
        regards potential competitive constraints (potential entrants such as Vueling and
         easyJet – as noted by the Parties)1139 would be sufficient to counter the likely
        negative effects of the Transaction on the Rome-Munich city pair. This is because,
         the Commission’s market investigation did not confirm or introduce evidence that

9.2.8.4. Conclusion
(1068)  In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and the lack of
        prospect  of  likely, timely and  sufficient  entry on  the  route,  the Commission
        concludes that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on
         the route Rome - Munich by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in both
         the Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition.

9.2.9.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(1076)  Lufthansa and MEF submit that Lufthansa (through SWISS), ITA, Wizz Air and
         easyJet are the main airlines operating the route Rome-Zurich. According to the
          Parties, the merged entity will face strong competition from easyJet (that increased
           its capacity in Summer IATA 2024) and Wizz Air (that entered in Winter IATA
        2022/2023) which hold, respectively, 25% and 12% of market shares in Summer
       2023 IATA Season. Lufthansa and MEF further elaborate that the merged entity
        could be disciplined by potential entry or expansion, for example by airlines such as
        Vueling or Ryanair which both have bases in Rome and would not face  slot
          restrictions that could prevent them from entering the route Rome-Zurich. Finally,
         the Parties note that SBB offers a 6h 37min indirect high-speed train connection
       between Rome and Zurich that could constitute a viable offer for costs and ecological

(1077)  In the Response to the SO the Parties argue that the Commission fails to adequately
        capture the competitive dynamics on this route. Notably, the Parties characterise the

       on this route. The Parties also consider that NEOS, Vueling and Ryanair are all
         potential entrants on this route together with other potential entrants.
(1078)  The Parties also highlight that the market investigation confirms that easyJet and

         the market  investigation). In  addition, the  Parties note  that the Commission’s

       between the airports and Zurich and omit the assessment of other factors, such as

        about the Transaction’s impact.1146
9.2.9.3. The Commission’s assessment
(1079)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
        of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome –
        Zurich.
(1080)  First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 49, the Parties’ combined market share by
       number of passengers travelled is very high and ranges between 46-81% between
      Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024. These market
        shares indicate that the Parties would hold a dominant position after the Transaction.
       The increment brought by the Transaction is also large, at 15-28%.
(1081)  Moreover, based on the market share data in Table 50 the Parties’ combined market
        share by capacity (number of frequencies) is significantly higher, and ranges from 70
         to 86% between Summer IATA Season 2021 and Winter IATA Season 2023/2024.
       The increment brought by the Transaction is also particularly large or large, ranging
       between 18-30%.
(1082)  Thus, under both indications, the Parties’ combined market shares are indicative of a
       dominant position. Moreover, as shown in the paragraphs (1080) to (1114) below,
        while the competitive constraint exerted by Wizz Air and easyJet on this route
        remain relevant, it will not be sufficient to constraint the combined entity on this
         route. Even considering the “significant decline” in market shares referenced by the

         Parties in their Response to the SO, the market shares of Lufthansa and ITA will

(1083)  Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be large at
      15% to 22% (by passenger) in the last five IATA seasons. This corresponds to a high
         increase in the HHI of between 918 and 2 121 in line with the Commission’s
        Horizontal Merger Guidelines.1148
(1084)  Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be between 3 962 – 5 811 during each of the last five IATA seasons (with an
        increment at or more than 918 and up to 2 121).
(1085)  The high combined market share of the Parties, the large increment brought by the
         transaction, the high change in HHI and high HHI post-Transaction indicate that the
        Transaction would create or strengthen a dominant position.
(1086)  Fourth, even when looking into the widest possible market definition (i.e., one which
        includes FCO and CIA on the Rome end of the route, and ZRH and BSL on the
        Zurich end), the Transaction constitutes a 4-to-3 merger for non-stop flights.1149 In
         addition to the Parties, only easyJet and Wizz Air operate the Rome-Zurich city pair.
(1087)  easyJet held a market share of 41% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and 26%
         in the Summer IATA Season 2023. In terms of capacity (number of seats), easyJet’s
        market share is significantly lower, as  it held 21% in Winter 2023/2024 IATA
       Season and will hold a market share of 18% in the Summer IATA Season 2024.
(1088)  Wizz Air held a market share of 13% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024
       and 12% in the Summer IATA Season 2023. In terms of capacity (number of seats),
       Wizz Air’s market share is significantly lower, as it held 9% in Winter 2023/2024
      IATA Season and will hold a market share of 8% in the Summer IATA Season 2024.
(1089)  Both easyJet and Wizz Air operated the Rome-Zurich city pair from FCO to BSL.
(1090)  In this context, the Commission notes that, post-Transaction the Parties will become
         the largest operators on the Rome-Zurich city pair, holding a significant market share
       on both IATA Seasons, in terms of passengers and capacity operated, with easyJet
       and Wizz Air being the Parties’ only active competitors.
(1091)  Fifth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction. In particular, the presence of easyJet and Wizz Air is unlikely to
        be sufficient to constrain the Parties post-Transaction.
(1092)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to Lufthansa and ITA, only
       Wizz Air and easyJet operate on the market with market shares between 26%
       and 41% for easyJet and <1% and 13% for Wizz Air for the latest five seasons.
(1093)  In the second place, even though the Parties would continue to face competition from
         easyJet and Wizz Air post-Transaction, the Transaction would lead to the elimination

         section 9.1.2.1 above for more information).
(1097)  In the second place, ITA and Lufthansa operate the Rome-Zurich city pair from the

        (both operate from ZRH) whereas easyJet and Wizz Air operate the Rome-Munich
         city pair exclusively through the FCO-BSL route.

       from Zurich and is not necessarily seen by customers and airlines as substitutable to
        Zurich Airport”.1153 Wizz Air explained that it while BSL and ZRH compete to some

(1111)  In the second place, the Parties’ combined market share on both the route and the
       combined  slot holding  in FCO and  in ZRH  will be  significantly high, being
         indicative of market power susceptible of acting as a barrier to entry and expansion.
        (See section 9.1.4.2 above for more information). Despite the fact that the Zurich
        catchment area is potentially served by two airports, the results of the Commission’s
        market investigation and internal documents of the Parties support that (i) “there is a
        general preference of the majority of passengers to fly from their local airport”1168
       and thus entering a secondary airport would not allow competitors to compete
         closely with the Parties (see section 9.1.2.2 above for more information); and that (ii)
        Lufthansa uses its strong market position in primary airports to eliminate competition
       on  both  primary and  secondary  airports  of  the same  catchment  area.  (See
         section 9.1.4.2 above for more information and in particular Figure 54).
(1112)  Eighth, the Commission notes that the vast majority of customers who expressed a
       view within the framework of the Commission’s market investigation consider that
          train services are not close substitutes for short-haul flights with regard to Rome-
        Zurich specifically.1169 Similarly, a majority of customers who expressed a view
        considered that even in case of a 5-10% price increase, only very few passengers
       (<10%) would consider air and train-transport services substitutable on the Rome-
        Zurich route specifically.1170 Similarly, a majority of competitors expressing a view
        consider that very few passengers (<10%) would consider air and train services as
         close substitutes on the Rome-Zurich route, even in case of a permanent increase of
       5-10% in the prices of air transport services.1171 While SBB considers that train and
         air-transport services are substitutable on the Rome-Zurich route, it also notes that
          train travel times are “rather long” and consider that the train services on this route
         exert only some competitive pressure on airlines.1172 Based on the above, while train
         services might exert some out of market competitive constraint on short-haul flights
       on the Rome-Zurich route, the Commission’s market investigation suggests any such
         constraints are likely to be week and, considering the Parties’ market shares on this
         route, would not affect the above assessment.
(1113)  The Commission notes that, as a result of  its market investigation,  it does not
        consider train connections between Rome and Zurich competing with the passenger
          air transport services of Lufthansa and ITA. As an out of market constraint the
       Commission’s investigation has indicated  that the  train connection exerts very
         limited competitive pressure, if any, on the Rome-Zurich route. For more details see
         sections 6.8 and (273) et seq above.

        regards potential competitive constraints (potential entrants such as Ryanair or
        Vueling – as noted by the Parties)1173 would be sufficient to counter the likely
        negative effects of the Transaction on the Rome-Zurich city pair. This is because, the

        allow the Commission to conclude that there is timely, likely or sufficient potential

         acquisitions of short-haul carriers in the EEA (see section 7.7.4 for more detailed
          results).

        negative is in line with the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a short-haul route as well as the
         elimination of competition by ITA is associated with significantly higher prices (see
         section 7.7.2 for more detailed results).
(1117)  In the third place, the finding that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is also in line with the internal documents of Lufthansa predicting price
         increases, including […] (see section 7.7.1).
9.2.9.4. Conclusion
(1118)  In light of the common considerations on short-haul routes explained in section 9.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market shares and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the limited constraint imposed by competitors, the
         fact that the Parties compete closely, the existence of barriers to entry and the lack of
        prospect  of  likely, timely and  sufficient  entry on  the  route,  the Commission
        concludes that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition on
         the route Zurich – Rome by creating or strengthening a dominant position, in both
         the Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any plausible market definition.
9.2.10.  Conclusion
(1119)  In  light of the above, the Commission concludes  that  the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition on the routes Milan – Brussels, Milan –
        Düsseldorf, Milan – Frankfurt, Milan – Hamburg, Rome – Brussels, Rome –
         Frankfurt, Rome – Munich and Rome - Zurich.
