(1522)  In the present case, the Commission’s market investigation overall confirmed that the
        strong competitive position of the Parties on long-haul routes would constitute a
         barrier to entry or expansion post-Transaction. As explained in section 10.1.5.1, the
       merged entity would operate on a hub-to-hub basis on each of the three problematic
        long-haul routes discussed in this Decision, and as shown in sections 10.2 and 10.3,
             it would hold large market shares and capacity shares on each of the routes. The
        majority of the competitors that expressed an opinion during the Commission’s
         investigation clearly indicated that the Parties (including their JV partners) hold a
        strong competitive position on the long-haul routes listed in sections 10.2 and
          10.3,1485 and that the strong position of the merged entity (to whom, contrary to the
         Parties’ claim in their Response to the SO,1486 the respondents referred, without
        including the airlines belonging to the A++ JV), would constitute a barrier to entry
       and expansion on long-haul  routes.1487 As a way of example, Virgin Atlantic
       commented that “market consolidation would increase, impacting specially FCO-
        CAI, FCO-SFO and FCO-WAS, where Star Alliance carriers will hold 100% of the
        capacity share. [The Lufthansa] Group together with  its partners would gain a
         significant presence in those specific long haul routes, which would create further
        challenges for rival airlines to enter or compete effectively on those routes”.1488
         Similarly, according to one of the Parties’ main competitors, “the merged entity
       would make it even more difficult for [Air France-KLM] to consider opening one of
         th[ese] routes because the main competitor would be even stronger. Beyond opening
        routes from Italy, the merged entity would even threaten [Air France-KLM]’s feeding
       from Italy to long-haul destinations”.1489
(1523)  Furthermore, as further explained in section 10.1.5.3, the Parties’ high slot portfolio
          at both origin and destination on most of the overlapping long-hauls routes included
         in this Decision - which the Commission, contrary to the Parties’ argument,1490
        always calculated having regard to all relevant airports at least potentially falling
        within the same catchment areas and not at the level of a single airport, except for
         airports that are not used for long-haul operations - allows them to respond more
        dynamically to competitive changes. This factor makes  it harder for airlines with
        smaller slot portfolios at these airports to compete vis-à-vis the merged entity.
10.1.5.6. Availability of aircrafts and crews
(1524)  The results of the market investigation, which are not contradicted by the vague
        arguments brought by the Parties in their Response to the SO,1491 show that the
         availability of aircrafts and crews is crucial for the ability of airlines to enter or
       expand on the overlap routes and therefore serves as a barrier to entry. The aircraft
        has to be suitable for flying the long-haul overlap routes and the crew has to be
         trained to operate the specific aircraft used on the route.1492 In this regard, there are
        widespread reports that airlines are currently facing significant delays in aircraft
         deliveries due to production bottlenecks,1493 as well as significant crew shortages.1494

10.2.   Route-by-route assessment of direct overlaps (current)
(1525)  The Commission considers that the Transaction would significantly impede effective
        competition on the following three routes in which both Lufthansa’s A++ JV partner
        United Airlines and ITA have a current direct connection: Rome-Washington and
       Rome-San Francisco.
(1526)  These two routes are characterised, in addition to the fact that the Parties have direct
        connections, by the following common features:
          (a)   High combined market shares: On each route, the Parties’ combined market
              share is above 50% in the last two seasons (and up to 71%). As outlined in
             paragraph 17 of the Horizontal Merger Guidelines, very large market shares
          may in themselves be evidence of the existence of a dominant market position.
              In addition, according to paragraph 27 of the Horizontal Merger Guidelines,
              the larger the market share, the more likely a firm is to possess market power.
         (b)  No non-stop competition: On each route, there is no other direct competitor
               active at any point of the year. As outlined in section 10.1.4, this means that the
               Parties are close competitors on these routes. As outlined in paragraph 28 of
              the Horizontal Merger Guidelines, the higher the degree of substitutability
            between the merging firms’ products  (i.e., the  closer the merging firms
            compete with one another), the more likely it is that the merging firms will
                raise prices significantly.
          (c)   Significant increment: ITA’s market share on these routes is already significant
            and expected to grow further in the coming years. As outlined in paragraph 27
              of the Horizontal Merger Guidelines, the larger the addition of market share,
              the more likely it is that the merger will lead to a significant increase in market
             power.
(1527)  Each route is discussed in more detail below.

10.2.1.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(1534)  Lufthansa and MEF submit  that  the main  airlines  serving  the  route Rome-
       Washington based on Summer 2023 data are ITA, Lufthansa’s A++ JV partners
        United Airlines and Air Canada, IAG (together with  its JV partner American
         Airlines) and Delta (together with its JV partner Air France-KLM). In their response
         to the 6(1)(c) decision, Lufthansa and MEF further argue that the increment brought
        about by the Transaction from ITA is rather limited, as it only reached a low two-
          digits numbers in Summer 2023. Moreover, according to Lufthansa and MEF, post-
        Transaction  the  Parties  will be  constrained by  potential  additional  entry and
        expansion of other carriers. Finally, Lufthansa and MEF submit that no relevant slot
          restrictions exist on either side of the route Rome-Washington for new entrants.1500
        In their response to the 6(1)(c) decision, Lufthansa and MEF further submit that i)
         the competitive constraint from indirect connections on this route is significant, ii)
         the increment brought about by the Transaction is not large, and iii) the results of the
        market investigation as reported in the 6(1)(c) decision are not conclusive.1501
(1535)  In the Response to the SO, Lufthansa and MEF further submit that a) indirect flights,
        including from competitors such as TAP Air Portugal, Turkish Airlines, Icelandair,
       and others, constitute an important competitive constraint on this route, as evidenced
       by the significant share of passengers flying on indirect connections on this route,
       and b) the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV are relevant competitors on this route
        with market shares of around 10%.1502
10.2.1.3. The Commission’s assessment
(1536)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
         of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome-
       Washington during both IATA Winter and Summer season.
(1537)  First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high or at least high
       combined market share on the route. As set out in Table 66, the Parties’ combined

        share over the last six IATA seasons was between 49% and 71% since Summer 2022
         (the season that United Airlines entered this route with a direct connection), with
      ITA only entering this route with a direct service in Summer 2023, where the
       combined share of the Parties was equal to 71% (and with partial market shares for
        Winter 2023/24 equal to 70%). In addition, both United Airlines and ITA are
        planning to increase their current capacity on this route in the next two seasons (from
         close to zero capacity in Winter 2022/23 to 9 average weekly connections in Winter
        2023/24 and from 11 average weekly connections in Summer 2023 to 18 average
       weekly connections in Summer 2024). These capacity increases are likely to further
         increase the Parties’ strong position on this route (around 70% market share in
        seasons where both United Airlines and ITA had a direct connection). According to
         the Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines, very large market shares (50% or
        above) may in themselves be evidence of a dominant market position.1503
(1538)  Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA is large at 17% to
      20% in the first two seasons (Summer 2023 and Winter 2023/24) that ITA has started
         offering a direct connection on this route. This corresponds to a substantial increase
         in the HHI of between 1 867 and 1 991.1504 In addition, ITA plans to [information on
       ITA’s expansion plans] average weekly frequencies in Summer 2023 to [information
       on ITA’s expansion plans]weekly frequencies [information on ITA’s expansion
         plans] (corresponding to almost [information on ITA’s expansion plans] available
          seats, or almost [information on ITA’s expansion plans] of total O&D demand on
          this route based on Summer 2023).1505 In this regard, the low increments cited by
        Lufthansa and MEF in relation to this route are misleading since they relate to
        seasons where ITA had not yet entered this route with a direct connection.1506
         Overall, the very high level and the large increment in the Parties’ joint market
         position is an indicator that the Transaction could lead to a significant increase in
        market power and create or strengthen a dominant position on this route.
(1539)  Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be at between 5 293 and 5 154 based on the first two seasons in which ITA has
        entered this route with a direct connection. Furthermore, the Transaction constitutes a
         2-to-1 merger for direct flights during both the summer and winter season.
(1540)  Fourth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction.
(1541)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, no competitor other than ITA and the A++
      JV has achieved a market share above 10% since ITA started direct operations on
          this route in Summer 2023. Compared to the Parties’ joint market share of over 70%
        during these seasons, these competitors are unlikely to exert a sufficient competitive
         constraint on  the  Parties  to  eliminate  the  significant impediment  to  effective
        competition caused by the Transaction.

(1542)  In the second place, access to feeder traffic at Rome-FCO constitutes a significant
        advantage on the route Rome-Washington. Indeed, about 53% of ITA’s passengers
         travelling on the route in Summer 2023 transferred onto other services at FCO,
        whereas this percentage was significantly lower (less than 5%) for United Airlines,
       which  is  without  access  to  its own  feeder  network  at FCO  prior  to  the
         Transaction.1507 The Parties would be the only competitor operating the route with
        access to their own feeder traffic at FCO. Furthermore, as Washington-IAD is an
         airport hub of Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines, the Transaction
       combines two carriers which are particularly competitive on the route as they both
        have access to their own feeder network. Furthermore, following the Transaction, the
         Parties would also be the only competitor operating the route with access to their
      own (or that of a joint venture partner’s) feeder traffic at both ends of the route after
         the Transaction. Therefore, as explained in section 10.1.5.1, the Parties would face
        fewer barriers to expansion than their rivals, given that they can attract a higher
       volume of connecting passengers on both ends of the routes (both in Rome and in
        Washington) compared to their rivals. The profits that the Parties would derive from
          their passengers connecting at both ends of the route would not be affected by price
        competition on the trunk route  (i.e., the direct Rome-Washington route) and the
         Parties would have a stable base of profits in the form of these connecting passengers
         that would give them a competitive advantage on the trunk route, resulting in making
         the route less attractive for their rivals.
(1543)  In the third place, the competitive constraints imposed on the Parties from indirect
          flights appear to be limited on this route. Contrary to the Parties’ argument according
         to which  the Commission  is  “focussing on  direct  competitors  only”,1508  the
       Commission acknowledges that indirect flights generally compete with direct flights
         for long-haul travel, but notes that they represent a different value proposition, and
       would only be an alternative to a subset of passengers, as further explained in
         section 10.1.4. This is also in line with the limited market share that each competitor
        with indirect connections has been able to achieve on this route since ITA’s entry
        with a direct flight in Summer 2023 (below 10% for each competitor on the route,
        including the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV).1509 With regards to the indirect
        connections referenced by Lufthansa and MEF that are offered by TAP Air Portugal,
        Turkish Airlines, Icelandair on this route,1510 each of these competitors transported
         less than 5% of the total passengers flying on this route over the last two seasons
         since ITA offered a direct connection and in total, these airlines accounted for less
        than 7% of the overall market.1511 Therefore, the competitive constraints imposed on
         the Parties from these indirect competitors appears to be limited on this route.
(1544)  Fifth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
       compete closely on this route.
(1545)  In the  first place, long-haul competitors of the Parties consider that Lufthansa
         (including its JV partners) and ITA are the most competitive airlines on this route
         with, on average, each receiving 4.7 out of 5 stars (with 1 star indicating a very weak

        each other’s closest competitor on this route (i.e., all respondents consider ITA as
        Lufthansa’s closest competitor, and vice versa).1513
(1547)  In the third place, ITA and Lufthansa’s JV partner United Airlines both operate
         direct services on the route. As outlined in section 10.1.4, carriers that provide direct
        scheduled flights compete more closely with each other than they do with carriers
        providing indirect connections. The Parties are therefore closer competitors with
        each other than they are with carriers that offer indirect services on the route. This is
         particularly relevant for the route Rome-Washington, where indirect operations only
        provide a limited competitive constraint on the Parties.
(1548)  In the fourth place, the Parties are close competitors when considering the airport
         pairs served by the airlines belonging to the A++ JV and ITA compared to their
         competitors. As shown in Table 69 above, the Parties’ combined market share is
        even higher (at 77% in Summer 2023 and 79% in partial Winter 2023/24) when
        considering the airport pair FCO-IAD only. Therefore, this implies that the Parties
       compete even more closely with each other for passengers with a preference for IAD
        over other airports in the Washington catchment area.
(1549)  In the fifth place, [information about ITA’s monitoring activity of rivals on this
          route]., whereas [information about Lufthansa’s monitoring activity of rivals on this
          route].1514 In addition to the various other evidence presented in this section, this
       shows that the Parties consider each other close competitors on this route.
(1550)  In the sixth place, as explained in section 10.1.5.3, ITA holds a significant slot
         portfolio at Rome-FCO whereas Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines
        holds a significant slot portfolio at Washington-IAD, which means that they both can
        adapt flexibly to changes in capacity and pricing and thereby exert competitive
         constraints on each other.
(1551)  In the seventh place, United Airlines (Lufthansa’s A++ JV partner) currently is the
        only airline with a hub in IAD and therefore has competitive advantages at this
         airport compared to rivals, including the ability to compete at efficient scale and to
        operate important connections, including on this route, during periods in which slots
         are in high demand.1515
(1552)  Sixth, as explained in section 10.1.5, there are several barriers to entry and expansion
       on the route.
(1553)  In the first place, the strong position of the Parties constitutes a barrier to entry for
         the reasons set out in section 10.1.5.5 above. For Rome-Washington, this is due to
         the Parties holding a significant frequency advantage on the route as compared to

(1554)  In the second place, as regards the availability of slots, IAD is a Level 2 coordinated

(1555)  In the third place, for the route Rome-Washington, access to feeder traffic at both

        Indeed, over the three seasons (S22-S23) since United Airlines entered this route

(1556)  Seventh, the Commission’s investigation does not support a finding of market entry

        competitive effects of the Transaction.1517 In particular, no competitor indicated
        during the market investigation that they were concretely planning to enter this route
        with a direct connection.
(1557)  Eighth, while  the views  of competitors and customers on  the impact  of  the
        Transaction on this route are overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion
         of responding long-haul competitors and customers consider the impact  to be
         negative. The Parties’ main competitors on this route (Delta and American Airlines)

        explaining that it is “not able to predict the effects of the Transaction as it cannot
         anticipate how the overall market will react”.1518 Further, Air France-KLM, Condor,
      LOT, Neos and Turkish Airlines consider that the impact of the Transaction on this
         route is negative, while IAG and Lufthansa’s JV partner Air Canada considers that

        impact of the Transaction on this route is positive for passengers in terms of lower
         prices and/or higher quality of services offered.1519 1520 The Commission notes that
         the views by Lufthansa’s JV partners United Airlines and Air Canada may be biased
         as they have a clear financial interest in this Transaction as ITA is likely to join the
      A++ JV following the potential approval of the Transaction and all partners will
        share their revenues generated from the long-haul routes covered by the agreements.
        In addition, two long-haul competitors (Air France-KLM, LOT) consider that the
        Transaction would increase the barriers to entry and/or expansion on this route,
        whereas Delta considers that the impact of the Transaction on barriers to entry and/or
        expansion on this route depends on “how the overall market will react”.1521 Finally,
      29% of customers that expressed an opinion consider the impact of the Transaction
       on this route to be negative, whereas the remaining 38% and 33% consider the
        impact of Transaction to be respectively neutral and positive.1522

(1558)  Ninth, based on the various factors considered above, the Commission considers that,
         despite the mixed feedback from competitors and consumers, the impact of the
        Transaction on  this route  is  likely  to be negative. This conclusion  is  further
         reinforced by the results of the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a long-haul route is associated with
         significantly higher prices and that the competitive constraint exerted by indirect
        competitors is more limited than that exerted by direct competitors (see section 7.7.2
         for more detailed results). In addition, the finding that the impact of the Transaction
       on this route is negative is also in line with the internal documents of Lufthansa
         predicting price increases, including […] (see section 7.7.1).
10.2.1.4. Assessment of potentially narrower markets
(1559)  The  Commission’s  assessment  above  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, where IAD, DCA and BWI would belong to the same catchment areas.
        Therefore, the market shares and concerns outlined above reflect this plausible
         definition. The Parties’ combined market shares are even higher for the last two
        seasons (S23 and W23/24) if only the airport pair FCO-IAD is considered, compared
         to a broader market definition. Otherwise, the Commission’s assessment on the
        presence of competitors, closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, remains
         largely the same for a narrower market considering only the airport pair FCO-IAD.
      On the airport pairs FCO-DCA and FCO-BWI the overlap between the Parties is
         immaterial. Therefore, while the Commission’s conclusion remains the same no
        matter the precise market definition, the concerns identified for a broader market
        including IAD, DCA and BWI airports are even more severe when considering only
         the airport pair FCO-IAD.
(1560)  Concerning  the  plausible  distinction  between TS  and NTS  passengers,  the
       Commission’s assessment has been carried out on the widest plausible market
         definition  (i.e., TS and NTS combined). The Commission’s assessment on the
        presence of competitors, closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, would
        remain largely the same for TS and NTS passengers. The only significant difference
           is that the Parties’ combined market shares exceed their combined share across
        passenger types (by about 10 percentage points in both Summer 2023 and Winter
        2023/24). Therefore, while the Commission’s conclusion remains the same no matter
         the precise market definition, the concerns identified for a broader market including
        both TS and NTS passengers are even more severe when considering TS passengers
         as a separate market.
(1561)  Based on the above, the concerns outlined above continue to be relevant under any
         plausible relevant alternative market definition that includes IAD airport.
10.2.1.5. Conclusion
(1562)  In light of the common considerations on long-haul routes explained in section 10.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market share and large increment brought by the Transaction, the overall
        concentration level of the market, the fact that the constraint from the remaining
        competitors on the route is likely to be insufficient, the closeness of competition
       between the Parties, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion, the absence of
          likely, timely and sufficient entry or expansion on the city pair post-Transaction as
        well as the evidence on the effects of the Transaction, the Commission concludes
         that the Transaction would significantly impede effective competition as a result of
         the creation or strengthening of a dominant position in relation to the Rome-


                                    357

[PÁGINA PDF 360]
       Washington city pair, in both the Winter and Summer IATA Seasons, under any
         plausible market definition that includes IAD airport.
10.2.2.  Rome-San Francisco
10.2.2.1. Market structure
(1563)  The market structure on the route Rome-San Francisco in terms of passengers
         transported point-to-point (direct and indirect), average weekly (direct) frequencies,
         as well as a breakdown of connections on the route by airport pair and main
        competitors is presented in Table 70 to Table 72 respectively.
(1564) On this route, Rome-Fiumicino (FCO) is the only relevant airport near Rome, as
       Rome-Ciampino (CIA) is not used for any long-haul connections (both direct and
          indirect). San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Oakland International Airport
       (OAK), Oakland Norman Y. Mineta San José International Airport (SJC) and San
        José Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (STS) are located, even though to
         different extents, near San Francisco. Therefore, the assessment in  this section
         includes the following airport pairs: FCO-SFO, FCO-OAK, FCO-SJC and FCO-STS,
         but, as explained below, the assessment will not change materially if all or some
         airport pairs other than FCO-SFO were not considered part of the same market. The
       Commission’s approach on airport substitutability is in line with Lufthansa and
      MEF’s views on airport substitutability for Rome and San Francisco, as outlined in
         section 6.5.3.13. The following figures on the market structure include both time-
         sensitive  and  non-time-sensitive  passengers,  as  well  as  direct  and  indirect
         connections.1523
(1565) On  the  route Rome-San  Francisco,  the  only  airlines  with  direct  flights  are
        United Airlines and ITA, with ITA flying a direct connection across the whole year
       and United Airlines flying a direct connection in the summer season only. All other
          airline carriers active on this route operate via indirect flights only.

10.2.2.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(1569)  Lufthansa and MEF submit  that  the main  airlines  serving  the  route Rome-

         partners United Airlines and Air Canada, Air France-KLM (together with its JV

        according to Lufthansa and MEF, post-Transaction the Parties will be constrained by

         route Rome-San Francisco for new entrants.1526 In their response to the 6(1)(c)
         decision, Lufthansa and MEF further submit that i) the competitive constraint from
         indirect connections on this route is significant, and ii) the results of the market
         investigation as reported in 6(1)(c) decision are not conclusive.1527

(1570)  In the Response to the SO, Lufthansa and MEF further submit that a) indirect flights,

10.2.2.3. The Commission’s assessment
(1571)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
         of a dominant position under any plausible market definition that includes SFO on
         the route Rome-San Francisco during both IATA Winter and Summer season.
(1572)  First, the Transaction would lead to the Parties holding a very high combined market
        share on the route. As set out in Table 70, the Parties’ combined share since ITA and
        Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines entered this route in Summer 2023
        with a direct connection was 67% in Summer 2023 and 69% in partial Winter
        2023/24. According to the Commission’s Horizontal Merger Guidelines, very large
        market shares above 50% may in themselves be evidence of a dominant market
          position.1529
(1573)  Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction from ITA would be sizeable
         to large at 14 to 29 percentage points in the first two seasons that ITA has started
         offering a direct connection on this route (Summer 2023 and Winter 2023/24). This
        corresponds to a substantial increase in the HHI of between 1 517 and 2 325.1530 In
         addition, ITA plans to [information on ITA’s expansion plans], from its current 2
       weekly  frequencies  in Summer  2023  to  [information  on  ITA’s  expansion
        plans]weekly frequencies [information on ITA’s expansion plans] (corresponding to
        almost [information on ITA’s expansion plans] overall available seats, or around
        [information on ITA’s expansion plans] of the total O&D demand on this route based
       on Summer 2023).1531 Furthermore, ITA plans to [information on ITA’s expansion
         plans] to [information on ITA’s expansion plans] average weekly frequencies in
        Winter 2026/27 (corresponding to about [information on ITA’s expansion plans]
         available seats, or over [information on ITA’s expansion plans] of the total O&D
       demand in Winter 2022/23). The very high level and the large increment in the
         Parties’ joint market position is an indicator that the Transaction could lead to a
         significant increase in market power and create or strengthen a dominant position on
          this route.
(1574)  Third, the market is highly concentrated. Following the Transaction, the HHI would
        be at least 4 774 and 5 040 based on the last two seasons since both ITA and United
         Airlines entered this route with a direct connection. Furthermore, the Transaction
         constitutes a 2-to-1 merger for direct flights during the summer seasons, whereas in
         the winter seasons ITA will be the only carrier with a direct connection. As outlined
         in section 10.1.4, this suggests that the Parties are close competitors on this route.

(1575)  Fourth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction.
(1576)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to ITA and the A++ JV, only
         the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV have achieved material shares on this route,
        with Blue Skies ranging between 11% and 25% for the last six seasons and between
     8% and 11% since ITA started direct operations, and the AA-IAG JV reaching
       between 10% and 21% for the last six seasons and between 10% and 11% since ITA
         started  direct operations. With regards  to the other competitors referenced by
        Lufthansa and MEF for this route (TAP Air Portugal and Turkish Airlines),1532 these
       two airlines each transported only 5% or less of the total passengers travelling on this
         route over the last two seasons and overall constituted only around 7% of the total
        market. Therefore, these competitors are unlikely to impose a significant competitive
         constraint on the Parties, both individually and in aggregate.
(1577)  In the second place, access to feeder traffic at Rome-FCO will constitute a significant
        advantage on the route Rome-San Francisco. Indeed, about 47% of ITA’s passengers
         travelling on the route in Summer 2023 transferred onto other services at FCO,
        whereas the same percentage for United Airlines was significantly lower (less than
     5% in Summer 2023). United Airlines  is the only other  carrier with a  direct
        connection on this route, and, prior to the Transaction, did not access to its own
         feeder network at FCO.1533 The Parties would be the only competitor operating the
         route with access to their own feeder traffic at FCO. Furthermore, Lufthansa’s joint
        venture partner United Airlines is the only air carrier on this route with an airport hub
         in San Francisco. As a result of this network aspect, about 23% of United Airlines’
        passengers on this route in Summer 2023 transferred onto other services at SFO. The
        Transaction therefore combines two carriers which are particularly competitive on
         the route as they both have access to  their own feeder network. Furthermore,
        following the Transaction, the Parties would be the only competitor operating the
         route with access to their own (or that of a joint venture partner’s) network of feeder
          traffic at both ends of the route (whereas all other competitors do not have a network
         of  feeder  traffic  at  either  end  of  the  route).  Therefore,  as  explained  in
         section 10.1.5.1, the Parties would face fewer barriers to expansion than their rivals,
        given that they can attract a higher volume of connecting passengers on both ends of
         the routes (both in Rome and in San Francisco) compared to their rivals. The profits
         that the Parties would derive from their passengers connecting at both ends of the
         route would not be affected by price competition on the trunk route (i.e., the direct
       Rome-San Francisco route) and the Parties would have a stable base of profits in the
       form of these connecting passengers that would give them a competitive advantage
       on the trunk route, resulting in making the route less attractive for their rivals.
(1578)  In  the  third  place,  the  competitive  constraints imposed on  the  Parties from
        competitors with indirect flights only appears to be limited on this route. Contrary to
         the Parties’ argument according to which the Commission is “focussing on direct
        competitors only”,1534 the Commission acknowledges that indirect flights generally
       compete with direct flights for long-haul travel, but notes that they represent a
         different value  proposition, and would only be an  alternative  to a subset of
         passengers, as further explained in section 10.1.4. This is also in line with the limited

(1579)  Fifth, the market investigation has provided further evidence that Lufthansa and ITA
       compete closely on this route.
(1580)  In the  first place, long-haul competitors of the Parties consider that Lufthansa
         (including its JV partners) and ITA are the most competitive airlines on this route
         with, on average, receiving 4.5 and 4.7 out of 5 stars, respectively. All remaining
         current and potential competitors on this route have significantly lower ratings,
        including American Airlines (3.2), Delta (3.3), Air France-KLM (2.6), IAG (3.4) and
      TAP (2).1537
(1581)  In the second place, all except one responding long-haul competitors consider that
      ITA is Lufthansa’s closest competitor on this route, whereas all responding long-haul
        competitors consider that Lufthansa is ITA’s closest competitor.1538
(1582)  In the third place, the Parties (including their JV partners) both operate direct
         services on the route. As outlined in section 10.1.4, carriers that provide direct
        scheduled flights compete more closely with each other than they do with carriers
        providing indirect connections. The Parties are therefore closer competitors with
        each other than they are with carriers that offer indirect services on the route. This is
         particularly relevant for the route Rome-San Francisco, where indirect operations
        only provide a limited competitive constraint on the Parties.
(1583)  In the fourth place, [information about ITA’s monitoring activity of rivals on this
         route] whereas [information about Lufthansa’s monitoring activity of rivals on this
          route].1539 In addition to the various other evidence presented in this section, this
       shows that the Parties consider each other close competitors on this route.
(1584)  In the fifth place, as explained in section 10.1.5.3, ITA holds a significant slot
         portfolio at Rome-FCO whereas Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines
        holds a significant slot portfolio at San Francisco-SFO, which means that they both
        can adapt flexibly to changes in capacity and pricing and thereby exert competitive
         constraints on each other.
(1585)  In the sixth place, United Airlines (Lufthansa’s A++ JV partner) currently is the only
          airline with a hub in SFO and therefore has competitive advantages at this airport

(1586)  Sixth, as explained in section 10.1.5, there are several barriers to entry and expansion
       on the route.
(1587)  In the first place, for the route Rome-San Francisco, access to feeder traffic at both
        ends of the route, including at Rome-FCO, constitutes a significant advantage.
        Indeed, in Summer 2023, around 33% of all passengers travelling on the trunk route
         transferred  onto  other  services  at  either end  of  the  route.1540 Following  the
         Transaction, the Parties (and their JV partners) would be the only carriers operating
         the route with its own network of feeder traffic at both ends of the route.
(1588)  In the second place, the strong position of the Parties constitutes a significant barrier
         to entry for the reasons set out in section 10.1.5.6 above. For Rome-San Francisco,
          this is due to the Parties holding a significant frequency advantage on the route as
       compared to other competitors and holding a significant number of slots at both ends
         of the route, allowing them to react to market entry or expansion.
(1589)  In the third place, as regards the availability of slots, SFO is a Level 2 coordinated
          airport, which may limit the ability of other competitors to compete effectively via
          this airport.
(1590)  Seventh, the Commission’s investigation does not support a finding of market entry
         that would be likely, timely and sufficient to deter or defeat any potential anti-
        competitive effects of the Transaction.1541 In particular, no competitor indicated
        during the market investigation that they were concretely planning to enter this route
        with a direct connection.
(1591)  Eighth, while  the views  of competitors and customers on  the impact  of  the
        Transaction on this route are overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion
         of responding long-haul competitors and customers consider the impact  to be
         negative. The  Parties’ main independent competitors on  this route (Delta and
       American Airlines) consider that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
         uncertain with Delta explaining that  it is “not able to predict the effects of the
        Transaction as it cannot anticipate how the overall market will react”.1542 This view
           is also shared by Egyptair. Air France-KLM, Condor, LOT, Neos and Turkish
         Airlines consider that the impact of the Transaction on this route is negative, while
      IAG and Lufthansa’s JV partner Air Canada consider that the impact is neutral. Only
        Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines considers that the impact of the
        Transaction on this route is positive for passengers in terms of lower prices and/or
        higher quality of services offered.1543 The Commission notes that the views by
        Lufthansa’s JV partners United Airlines and Air Canada may be biased as they have
        a clear financial interest in this Transaction as ITA is likely to join the A++ JV
        following the potential approval of the Transaction and all partners will share their
        revenues generated from the long-haul routes covered by the JV agreement. In
         addition, one long-haul competitor (Air France-KLM) considers that the Transaction
       would increase the barriers to entry and/or expansion on this route, whereas Delta

(1592)  Ninth, based on the various factors considered above, the Commission considers that,
         despite the mixed feedback from competitors and consumers, the impact of the

        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a long-haul route is associated with

(1593)  Tenth, contrary to the submission by Lufthansa and MEF,1546 the Commission’s

       IAG/Aer Lingus. While Lufthansa and MEF do not specify in which respect this
        conclusion is inconsistent with the IAG/Aer Lingus decision and instead only refer to
        a section at the beginning of their Response to the SO, in this section, Lufthansa and
     MEF submit that no competition concerns were found on some overlapping long-
        haul routes in the IAG/Aer Lingus decision, citing the Dublin-New York route, where
        both of the parties had a direct connection and combined market shares above 50%
       and where the market share of a remaining competitor was similar or higher to the
        increment brought by the Transaction, even with increments above 20 percentage
         points.
(1594)  The competitive situation on the Dublin-New York route in the IAG/Aer Lingus case
            is, however, factually different from the competitive situation on the route Rome-
       San Francisco route in the present case. First, as discussed above, ITA has significant
        growth plans on the route Rome-San Francisco route, whereas such growth plans
       were not part of the competitive assessment on the Dublin-New York route in the
       IAG/Aer Lingus case. Second, the increment brought about by the Transaction in the
         present case is already, even prior to these growth plans, significantly above the
        market share of the largest remaining competitor (29% vs. 12% in Winter 2023/24),
        whereas this was not so on the Dublin-New York route in the IAG/Aer Lingus case.
         Third, in the present case, ITA and Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines
         are the only competitors with a direct connection on the Rome-San Francisco route
        (with ITA flying the full year and United Airlines during the summer season only),
        whereas on the Dublin-New York route in the IAG/Aer Lingus case, there were two
         other competitors present, besides the Parties, that offered a direct connection. In any
         event, Lufthansa and MEF’s comparison of the competitive assessment in this case
        with the IAG/Aer Lingus case does not consider to what extent the various common
         considerations relevant for the present case, including those described in sections 7.7
       and 10.1, as well as the various route-specific considerations described in this section
       compare against the relevant considerations in the IAG/Aer Lingus case. In addition

         to the Commission’s prior practice not binding  it in its assessment of individual

10.2.2.4. Assessment of potentially narrower markets
(1595)  The  Commission’s  assessment  above  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, where SFO and OAK as well as the other identified airports belong to the
       same catchment areas. Therefore, the market shares and concerns outlined above
          reflect  this plausible definition. However, as airports other than SFO currently
         represent only an immaterial share of passengers on indirect connections on this
         route, the Commission’s assessment on the strength of the Parties, the presence of
         competitors, closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, remains the same,
        independently of whether airports other than SFO are considered part of the same
        catchment area as SFO.
(1596)  Concerning  the  plausible  distinction  between TS  and NTS  passengers,  the
       Commission’s assessment has been carried out on the widest plausible market
         definition  (i.e., TS and NTS combined). The Commission’s assessment on the
        presence of competitors, closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, remains
         largely the same for TS and NTS. The Parties’ combined market shares with regards
         to time-sensitive passengers are broadly in line with their combined share across
        non-time sensitive passengers. Therefore, the Commission’s conclusion remains the
       same no matter the precise market definition.
(1597)  Based on the above, the concerns outlined above continue to be relevant under any
         plausible alternative market definition that includes the airport SFO.
10.2.2.5. Conclusion
(1598)  In light of the common considerations on long-haul routes explained in section 10.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to the Parties’ very high
       combined market  shares and  the  sizeable  to  large increment brought by  the
         Transaction, the overall concentration level of the market, the fact that the constraint
       from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be insufficient, the closeness
         of competition between the Parties, the existence of barriers to entry and expansion,
         the absence of timely, likely and sufficient entry or expansion on the city pair post-
        Transaction  as  well  as  the  evidence on  the  effects  of  the  Transaction,  the
       Commission concludes that the Transaction would significantly impede effective
        competition as a result of the creation or strengthening of a dominant position in
         relation to the Rome-San Francisco city pair, in both the Winter and Summer IATA
        Seasons, under any plausible market definition that includes the airport SFO.

        competition on the route Rome-Toronto in which Lufthansa’s A++ JV partner Air
       Canada has an established direct connection, whereas ITA recently launched a direct
         service on this route in Summer 2024. The Commission’s concerns on this route are
         limited to the IATA Summer season only, [information on ITA’s entry plans]. While
       ITA’s entry is not yet reflected in the historical market shares, the Parties already

10.3.1.  Rome-Toronto
10.3.1.1. Market structure
(1600)  The market structure on the route Rome-Toronto in terms of passengers transported
         point-to-point (direct and indirect), average weekly (direct) frequencies, as well as a
       breakdown of connections on the route by airport pair and main competitors is
        presented in Table 73 to Table 75 respectively. ITA started operations on this route
       on 10 May 2024, during the course of these proceedings, and is currently actively
        operating on this route.1548 As a result of the historical nature of the IATA passenger
         data that is used to calculate market shares, ITA’s entry on this route is not yet
         reflected in the market shares presented below.
(1601) On this route, Rome-Fiumicino (FCO) is the only relevant airport near Rome, as
       Rome-Ciampino (CIA) is not used for any long-haul connections (both direct and
          indirect). Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ) and Billy Bishop Toronto
        City Airport (YTZ) are all located, even though to a different extent, near Toronto.
        Therefore, the assessment in this section includes the following airport pairs: FCO-
     YYZ and FCO-YTZ, but, as explained below, the assessment will not change
         materially if the airport pair FCO-YTZ was not considered part of the same market.
       The Commission’s approach on airport substitutability is in line with Lufthansa and
      MEF’s views on airport substitutability for Rome and Toronto, as outlined in section
         6.5.3.13. The following figures on the market structure include both time-sensitive
       and non-time-sensitive passengers, as well as direct and indirect connections.1549
(1602) On the route Rome-Toronto, the only airlines with direct flights are Air Canada, Air
        Transat and ITA (from Summer 2024). ITA and Air Transat operate on this route
        during the summer season only. All other airline carriers active on this route operate
         via indirect flights only.

10.3.1.2. Lufthansa and MEF’s view
(1606)  Lufthansa and MEF submit that the main airlines serving the route Rome-Toronto
        based on Summer 2023 data are Lufthansa’s A++ JV partners (particularly Air
       Canada) and Air Transat. Air Transat offers direct flights only in summer seasons.
        During the winter seasons, according to Lufthansa and MEF, post-Transaction the
         Parties will be constrained by additional carriers, such as Air France-KLM and IAG
        (with indirect flights only). In addition, Lufthansa and MEF consider that new
         entrants face no relevant slot restriction on either side of the Rome-Toronto route.1555
        In the 6(1)(c) decision, Lufthansa and MEF further argue that i) the Parties do not
       compete more closely for Business Class passengers as ITA only had very few
        Business Class passengers on this route, and ii) Air Transat competes more closely
        with Air Canada than ITA does.1556
(1607)  In the Response to the SO, Lufthansa and MEF further submit that a) Air Transat
         exerts a strong competitive constraint on Lufthansa’s JV partner Air Canada, and b)
         indirect  flights constitute an important competitive constraint on  this route, as
        evidenced by the significant share of passengers flying via indirect connections on
          this route as well as the prominent display of indirect connections on Google Flights
         for this route.1557
10.3.1.3. Submission by third-party carrier Air Canada
(1608) On 17 April 2024, following the adoption of the Commission’s Statement of
         Objections, Air Canada, Lufthansa’s joint venture partner in the A++ JV (together
        with United Airlines), submitted written observations on the SO, focussing on the
       Commission’s  preliminary  assessment  of  the  route  Rome-Toronto.  In  these
         observations, Air Canada argues that the Commission’s assessment of the route
       Rome-Toronto “fails to meet the legal and evidentiary standards required by law to
        demonstrate a SIEC [significant impediment to effective competition]”.1558
(1609)  More specifically, Air Canada argues that the SO a) incorrectly groups together time-
         sensitive and non-time-sensitive passengers in  its assessment which “artificially
          inflates Air Canada’s market position”, b) overstates ITA’s position, which only
         started operations on this route in May 2024, c) disregards fierce competition from
        Air Transat, d)  fails to consider that there are no substantial barriers to entry,
         e) provides no evidence on merger-specific harm to consumers and f) misrepresents
         the results of the market investigation, including by relying primarily on statements
       by biased third-parties.1559
10.3.1.4. The Commission’s assessment
(1610)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
         of a dominant position under any plausible market definition on the route Rome-
        Toronto during the IATA Summer season only.1560

(1611)  First, even prior to ITA’s entry, Lufthansa and its JV partner Air Canada hold a very
        high market share on the route. As set out in Table 73, the market share of the A++
      JV over the last two IATA Summer seasons was 55% (and 85% in Summer 2021
        although, as noted by Lufthansa and MEF,1561 this season may  still have been
         significantly affected by the COVID pandemic). According to the Commission’s
        Horizontal Merger  Guidelines,  very  large market  shares above 50% may  in
        themselves be evidence of a dominant market position.1562
(1612)  Second, while this is not yet reflected in the historical market share data, ITA’s entry
       on this route in May 2024 has the likely effect of significantly increasing the Parties’
       combined market share on  this  route. From the current Summer 2024 season
        onwards, ITA operates on this route with 5 average weekly frequencies during the
       summer season, which is expected to increase to [information on ITA’s expansion
         plans] average weekly frequencies [information on ITA’s expansion plans].1563 This
        corresponds to about [information on ITA’s expansion plans] overall seats during the
       summer seasons ([information on ITA’s expansion plans] of the total O&D demand
       on this route, based on Summer 2023).1564 The very high level of joint market shares
       and the expected large increment in the Parties’ joint market position, which will
        derive from ITA’s entry and expansion on  this route,  is an indicator that the
        Transaction is likely to lead to a significant increase in market power and create or
         strengthen a dominant position on this route.
(1613)  With regards to Air Canada’s submission that the Commission is overstating ITA’s
         position on this route, Air Canada does not actually present any evidence for this
        claim and instead only makes general statements relating to the fact that ITA is a
         recent entrant on this route and the fact that ITA may choose, absent the Transaction,
         to  exit the route due to  profitability  considerations.1565 [Information on ITA’s
        network strategy].1566 [Information on ITA’s network strategy].1567 In relation to Air
        Canada’s claim that demand on this route is not strong enough to sustain, on a long-
        term basis, more than two independent direct competitors on this route,1568 the
       Commission notes that the level of demand (as represented by the total number of
        passengers travelling on this route and the total market size in terms of revenues
        earned) in the summer season significantly exceeds the total level of demand on
         other long-haul routes that have sustained more than two competitors with direct
          flights for significant periods of time.1569
(1614)  Third, the market is highly concentrated. Even prior to ITA’s entry, the HHI on the
         route was high, namely between 4 577 and 7 292 during the last three summer
         seasons. Following ITA’s direct entry, the level of concentration is likely to further
         increase on  this route following the Transaction. Furthermore, the Transaction

         constitutes a 3-to-2 merger for direct flights during the summer season. In addition to
         the Parties, only Air Transat operates the route with direct services (in the summer
        season only). The  total market share of  all indirect connections on  this route
         represents only around 15% on this route during the last two summer seasons (in
       which both Air Canada and Air Transat had a direct connection on this route). As
        explained in section 10.1.4, the proportion of passengers travelling indirectly on this
         route is expected to further decrease following ITA’s entry on this route with a direct
        connection.
(1615)  Fourth, the constraint from the remaining competitors on the route is likely to be
         insufficient to eliminate the significant impediment to effective competition caused
       by the Transaction.
(1616)  In the first place, prior to the Transaction, in addition to the A++ JV, only Air
        Transat has consistently achieved significant market shares during the summer
        seasons (around 40% in the last two summer seasons since its direct entry), with no
         other competitor achieving more than 3% market share during the last two summer
        seasons (where both Air Canada and Air Transat had a direct connection on this
         route).
(1617)  With regards to the submission by Air Canada, according to which Air Transat “is a
        strong  competitive  alternative”  on  this  route  and  according  to  which  the
       Commission’s assessment of the route contradicts the Commission’s assessment in
         the proceeding M.9489 – Air Canada / Transat where the Commission found that Air
       Canada and Air Transat are close competitors,1570 the Commission notes that in
        highly concentrated markets, such as this one, where prior to ITA’s entry, the two
         largest competitors (Air Canada and Air Transat) accounted for over 90% of the total
        market over the last two summer seasons, it is possible and not inconsistent for the
       Commission to identify competition concerns both when considering a merger
       between these two competitors, as well as between one of these competitors and a
         recent entrant, such as ITA. In addition, as confirmed in the recent CK Telecoms
        judgement, even in oligopolistic markets, the Commission is only required to assess
        whether  the merging  parties  are  close  competitors  (rather  than  “particularly
          close”).1571 It is possible and consistent with the Commission’s present assessment
         that both Air Transat and ITA are close competitors to Lufthansa and its JV partners
       on this route.
(1618)  In the second place, access to feeder traffic at both Rome-FCO and Toronto-YYZ
         will constitute a significant advantage on the route Rome-Toronto. Following the
         Transaction, the Parties would be the only competitor operating the route with access
         to their own feeder traffic at Rome-FCO. Furthermore, Toronto-YYZ is an airport
       hub of Lufthansa’s joint venture partner Air Canada, whereas Air Transat is a point-
         to-point carrier without access to feeder  traffic in Toronto. The Parties would
         therefore be the only competitor operating the route with access to their own (or that
         of a joint venture partner’s) feeder traffic at each end of the route. Therefore, as
        explained in section 10.1.5.1, the Parties would face fewer barriers to expansion than
          their rivals, given that they can attract a higher volume of connecting passengers on
        both ends of the routes (both in Rome and in Toronto) compared to their rivals. The
         profits that the Parties would derive from their passengers connecting at both ends of
         the route would not be affected by price competition on the trunk route (i.e., the

         direct Rome-Toronto route) and the Parties would have a stable base of profits in the
       form of these connecting passengers that would give them a competitive advantage
       on the trunk route.
(1619)  In the third place, the Parties and their JV partners would hold a frequency advantage
        over the other direct competitors on the route. ITA and the A++ JV would operate
       17 weekly  frequencies during  the summer season (based on ITA’s  entry and
        expansion plans on this route) compared to the 5 weekly frequencies of Air Transat,
         the only  other competitor with  direct  flights on  this  route. As explained  in
         section 10.1.5.5, the lower number of frequencies and thus the lower capacity of Air
        Transat means that the competitive constraint it may impose on the Parties is limited.
      As explained above, it would be difficult for Air Transat (or any other competitor) to
         increase its frequencies following the Transaction to similar levels as the Parties,
         since it would not have access to connecting traffic at Rome-FCO or Toronto-YYZ.
(1620)  In the fourth place, for the summer season, the competitive constraints imposed on
         the Parties from indirect flights appear to be limited on this route. While indirect
          flights generally compete with direct flights for long-haul travel, they represent a
         different value  proposition, and would only be an  alternative  to a subset of
         passengers, as further explained in section 10.1.4. This is also in line with the limited
        market share that each competitor with indirect connections has been able to achieve
       on this route, both individually and in aggregate.
(1621)  In their Response to the SO, Lufthansa and MEF contest that indirect flights exert
        only limited competitive constraint on the Parties’ operations on the route Rome-
        Toronto. Lufthansa and MEF submit that results from Google Flights for the route
       Rome-Toronto route show that “additional travel time is often compensated by lower
        price” as Google’s algorithm classifies several indirect offers as well as Air Transat’s
         direct offer on this route for a specific date as “Best Flights” (rather than the Parties’
         direct offers).1572 However, as acknowledged by Lufthansa and MEF, the Parties’
         direct flight offers available for that date are offered at a significant price premium
       compared to the indirect flight offers classified by Google Flights as “Best Flights”
         for that date.1573 Google Flights results suggest that passengers see indirect flight as
         relevant substitutes to the Parties’ direct flights on this route only when indirect
          flights are offered  at a significant discount compared to direct  flights. This  is
         consistent with the Commission’s finding that indirect flights are likely to exert only
         limited competitive constraint on the Parties’ operations on the route Rome-Toronto
         (as competitors with direct flight appear to be able to sell tickets on this route at a
         significant price premium compared to competitors with indirect flight offers which
           is an expression of the market power that direct competitors have on this route).
(1622)  Fifth, Air Canada submits that, from a Canadian perspective, Italy is a “non-location
       bound vacation destination” and that therefore other destinations, primarily other
        Mediterranean  destinations, “impose competitive constraints” on the  Parties as
        “passengers can choose to go elsewhere”.1574 However, this claim by Air Canada is
         entirely  unsubstantiated and  can  therefore  not  factor  into  the Commission’s
        assessment of this route. While Air Canada submitted statistics according to which
        Canadians  travel to various destinations in Europe, these  statistics provide no

(1623)  Sixth,  the market  investigation  has  provided  further  evidence  that  Lufthansa
         (including its JV partners) and ITA will compete closely on this route during summer
        seasons following ITA’s entry in Summer 2024,
(1624)  In the first place, long-haul competitors of the Parties consider Lufthansa (including
           its JV partners) to be the most competitive airline on this route (4.2 stars out of 5)
       and Air  Transat  the second most  competitive  (4  stars), both  offering  direct
        connections. Other carriers, operating the route with indirect connections only, are
        considered as being less competitive, rated at most 3 stars (e.g., Air France-KLM,
      IAG and TAP with 3, 2.8 and 2.4 stars respectively).
(1625)  In the second place, 5 out of 6 responding long-haul competitors considered
        Lufthansa (and its JV partners) to be the closest competitor to ITA on this route with
         the remaining competitor considering Air Transat to be the closest.1575
(1626)  In the third place, the Parties will both operate direct services on the route from
      Summer 2024 onwards. As outlined in section 10.1.4, carriers that provide direct
        scheduled flights compete more closely with each other than they do with carriers
        providing indirect connections. The Parties are therefore closer competitors with
        each other than they are with carriers that offer indirect services on the route. This is
         particularly relevant for the route Rome-Toronto, where indirect operations only
        provide a limited competitive constraint on the Parties.
(1627)  In the fourth place, [information about ITA’s monitoring activity of rivals on this
          route].1576 In addition to the various other evidence presented, [information about
        Lufthansa’s monitoring activity of rivals on this route] (in May 2024, as explained
       above at paragraph (1596)).
(1628)  In the  fifth place, as explained in section 10.1.5.3, ITA holds a significant slot
         portfolio at Rome-FCO whereas Lufthansa’s joint venture partner Air Canada holds a
         significant slot portfolio at Toronto-YYZ, which means that they both can adapt
         flexibly to changes in capacity and pricing and thereby exert competitive constraints
       on each other.
(1629)  Seventh, as explained in section 10.1.5, there are several barriers to entry and
        expansion on the route.
(1630)  In the first place, the strong position of the Parties constitutes a significant barrier to
         entry for the reasons set out in section 10.1.5.5 above. For Rome-Toronto, this is due
         to the Parties holding a significant frequency advantage on the route as compared to
         other competitors.
(1631)  In the second place, as regards the availability of slots, YYZ, where almost all
        passengers traveling between Italy and Toronto land, is a Level 3 coordinated airport,
       meaning that this airport is congested and available slots to airlines hoping to enter or
       expand via this airport are limited.
(1632)  In the third place, for the route Rome-Toronto, access to feeder traffic at both ends of
         the route, including at Rome-FCO, constitutes a significant advantage. Indeed, over
         the last five seasons (S21-S23), between 26% and 57% of passengers travelling on

         side of the route”.1578 This contradicts the Lufthansa and MEF’s argument according
         to which point-to-point carriers, such as Air Transat, do not face any relevant barriers
         in competing head-to-head with network carriers, such as the Parties, that have
        access to feeder traffic on one or both ends of the route.1579
(1633)  In the fourth place, contrary to the submission by Lufthansa and MEF,1580 the fact
         that Air Transat increased  its capacity on this route between Summer 2022 and
      Summer 2023 does not, in  itself, provide evidence that there are no significant
         barriers to entry and expansion on this route. In this regard, Air Transat’s capacity
         increase was very modest, from 4 average weekly flights in Summer 2022 to 5
        average weekly flights in Summer 2023, whereas Lufthansa’s JV partner Air Canada
        increased its capacity over the same period from 6 to 8 average weekly flights (and,
         again, in Summer 2024 to 10 average weekly flights). In addition, Air Transat
        already operated on this route prior to Summer 2023 and therefore this small increase
         in capacity does not provide any indication on potential barriers to entry on this
         route.
(1634)  Eighth, the Commission’s investigation does not support a finding of market entry
         that would be likely, timely and sufficient to deter or defeat any potential anti-
        competitive effects of the Transaction.1581 In particular, no competitor indicated
        during the market investigation that they were concretely planning to enter this route
        with a direct connection. With regards to the potential entry claims made by Air
       Canada for this route,1582 including by airlines such as WestJet and Neos, the
       Commission notes that these entry claims remain hypothetical and unsubstantiated
       and are therefore not comparable to ITA’s entry on this route which is operating
         direct flights on this route since May 2024.
(1635)  Ninth, while  the views  of  competitors and customers on  the impact  of  the
        Transaction on this route are overall mixed and inconclusive, a significant proportion
         of responding long-haul competitors and customers consider the impact  to be
         negative. The Parties’ main competitor on this route Air Transat considers that the
        impact  of  the Transaction on  this  route  is  negative.1583  It explained  that  its
        “operations are likely to be hampered by the Transaction, as it will impact its ability
         to grow in Italy”.1584 The view that the impact of the Transaction on this route is
        negative is also shared by Air France-KLM, Condor, and LOT, while Neos, IAG and

        Transaction on  this route  is  likely  to be negative. This conclusion  is  further
         reinforced by the results of the Commission’s regression analysis which shows that a
        reduction in the number of direct competitors on a long-haul route is associated with
         significantly higher prices and that the competitive constraint exerted by indirect
        competitors is more limited than that exerted by direct competitors (see section 7.7.2
         for more  detailed  results).1588 In  addition, the finding  that  the impact of  the
        Transaction on this route is negative is also in line with the regression analysis
        performed by Lufthansa when assessing the impact of the Transaction prior to
       making a decision to invest in ITA (see section 7.7.1).
10.3.1.5. Assessment of potentially narrower markets
(1637)  The  Commission’s  assessment  above  considers  the  widest  plausible  market
         definition, where YYZ and YTZ belong to the same catchment areas, therefore the
        market shares and concerns outlined above reflect this plausible definition. However,
         as YTZ currently represents only an immaterial share of passengers on this route, the
       Commission’s assessment on the strength of the Parties, the presence of competitors,
         closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, remains the same, independently
         of whether YTZ is considered part of the same catchment area as YYZ.
(1638)  Concerning  the  plausible  distinction  between TS  and NTS  passengers,  the
       Commission’s assessment has been carried out on the widest plausible market
         definition  (i.e., TS and NTS combined). The Commission’s assessment on the
        presence of competitors, closeness, barriers to entry, and evidence of entry, remains
         largely the same for time-sensitive and non-time sensitive passengers. The only
         significant difference is that the A++ JV has significantly higher market shares when
        considering TS passengers only (with 93% market share in Summer 2023). This is
        because Air Transat  is not active as a significant competitor for time-sensitive
        passengers according to the data provided by Lufthansa and MEF. However, and

         contrary to the submission by Air Canada,1589 the Commission’s conclusion also
         applies when considering NTS passengers only. As outlined in paragraph (1601), the
         Parties’ combined market shares remain above 50% in the summer season, even
       when considering NTS passengers only.1590 In addition, the various further points
         that are relevant for the competitive assessment, as outlined by the Commission in

10.3.1.6. Conclusion
(1640)  In light of the common considerations on long-haul routes explained in section 10.1,
       and in view of the above findings related in particular to Lufthansa’s (including its
      JV partners’) current high market share, the expected future increment in the Parties’
          joint market position following ITA’s entry, the overall concentration level of the
        market, which is likely to further increase following ITA’s expected direct entry on
          this route, the closeness of competition between the Parties, the limited competitive
         constraints imposed on the Parties from indirect flights, the existence of barriers to
         entry and the uncertainty with respect to likely sufficient entry or expansion on the
         city pair post-Transaction, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
         significantly impede effective competition as a result of the creation or strengthening
         of a dominant position in relation to the Rome-Toronto city pair, in the Summer
      IATA season only, under any plausible market definition.

       make the expansion of smaller firms and potential competitors more difficult or
        otherwise restrict the ability of rival firms to compete. In such a case, competitors
      may not, either individually or in the aggregate, be in a position to constrain the
       merged entity to such a degree that it would not increase prices or take other actions
        detrimental to competition. For instance, the merged entity may have such a degree

11.4.   Milan-Linate: The Commission’s assessment
11.4.1.  Ability to foreclose
(1647)  To be able to provide passenger air transport, an air carrier needs access to airport
         infrastructure. At congested airports, an air carrier must thus hold slots to operate
         routes from or to those airports. Lack of access to slots is therefore a barrier to an air
          carrier's ability to compete for passengers between an airport and the destinations
        served from the airport. An airline's slot holding at an airport provides a measure of
           its  ability to compete on the passenger  air transport markets  to or from  that
          airport.1604 Air carriers holding a large slot portfolio may adopt practices aimed at
        preventing entry or expansion by other carriers at airports, such as predatory pricing,

         “slot hoarding”,1605 “slot babysitting”,1606 or use of their “slot shuffling power”1607 to
        engage in exclusionary conduct.1608
(1648)  For the merged entity to be able to foreclose its competitors post-Transaction, the
        following conditions must be fulfilled: (i) the slots that the merged entity would hold
        post-Transaction represent a significant share of the airport capacity, in particular at
        peak times; (ii) the Transaction has a material impact on the merged entity’s slot
        holding at the airport, in particular at peak times; and (iii) the merged entity’s slot
        holding could negatively affect the overall availability of slots as an input for the
        passenger air transport markets to or from the relevant airport.1609 Condition (iii)
         requires that (a) the airport at which the merged entity would hold a large portfolio of
          slots does not have sufficient available capacity (i.e. its level of congestion is high);
       and (b) the airports considered as substitutable by air carriers do not have sufficient
         available  capacity  either.1610 The Commission  will  support  this  analysis with
        evidence from market participants and internal documents of the Parties on the
         strength of the position of the Parties in LIN and about the ability of the merged
         entity to engage in foreclosure strategy in LIN post-Transaction.

11.4.1.2. Condition (ii): the Transaction has a material impact on the merged entity’s slot
        holding at the airport, in particular at peak times.
(1651)  The Transaction will bring together the number 1 and number 2 slot holders in LIN
        with an increment of around 6 to 7% in slot holding during operating hours and peak
         hours.  This  increment  cannot  be  considered  a  negligible  increment.  For
        completeness, the Commission observes that a similar increment was considered in
        previous case as a significant increment that raised competition concerns.1617 As a
          result of the Transaction, the competitive pressure exerted by the second largest
        competitor operating in LIN (that is, Lufthansa as an independent competitor to ITA)
         will be eliminated. In addition, the larger number of slots would provide the merged
         entity with reinforced  slot  shuffling power allowing  it more  possibilities and
          flexibility in exercising that power. In addition, hoarding and babysitting tactics
        could be applied to a larger number of slots, withholding a larger share of slots from
         competitors.
11.4.1.3. Condition (iii)(a) LIN is a highly congested airport
(1652)  Traffic at Linate airport started to be restricted in the year 2000 when the city built a
      new terminal at the old Malpensa Airport to develop  it into a big international
          airport. In order  to  facilitate the development of the new  airport, the  Italian
       Government started introducing limitations with Ministerial Decree no. 15 of 3
       March 2000, with respect to which destinations could be served from Linate,
        imposing limits on capacity and frequencies. Throughout the years those restrictions
        have been progressively modified. The current limitation can be broadly summarised
         as follows:
          (a)   18 scheduled commercial movements per hour.
         (b)  Only flights with narrow body or single aisle aircraft type are allowed.
          (c)   Only scheduled point-to-point flights in the European Union or to airports
              located within a radius of 1 500 km.
(1653)  According to Lufthansa and MEF, LIN is a highly congested airport with technical
          utilisation rates above 75% during operating hours and close to 90% during peak
         hours. However, as explained by Lufthansa and MEF, restrictions on the allocation
