11.4.1.5. Market participants raise foreclosure concerns with respect to LIN
(1659)  Market participants raised concerns with respect to the position of the merged entity
       and  its  ability  to  foreclose. Their statements lend support  to  the  findings  in
         sections 11.4.1.1 - 11.4.1.4 above that show that post-Transaction the merged entity
         will have the ability to foreclose competitors in LIN.
11.4.1.5.1.   The position of Lufthansa and ITA in LIN
(1660)  The large majority of carriers responding to the question,1628 were of the view that
        considering ITA’s  slot holding per  airport, the congestion levels LIN and the
         alternative (substitutable) airports available, ITA already holds a dominant position
         in LIN.1629 Almost half of the carriers expressing a view said that this position caused
          their company or other carriers to deprioritize or exit the airport in the past.1630
(1661)  The large majority of  carriers responding  to the question considered  that the
        Transaction would improve the market position of Lufthansa and ITA in this airport,
         resulting in the creation or strengthening of a dominant position to the detriment of
         competition.1631 One carrier explained that “Lufthansa Group will add 8.7% to the
      57% capacity share controlled by ITA on the EEA  flights from LIN  airport,
        strengthening  its dominant position. Other competitors are not allowed to add
        frequencies as the airport is totally capped. This would create unsustainable levels of
         concentration, to the detriment of competitors that will no longer be able to compete
        with  the Merged  Entity  for  traffic  to/from  this  unique and  highly  valuable
         airport.”1632 Another carrier added that “ITA are approximately 60% of capacity at
        LIN. Lufthansa Group account for a further 7%. In total this will equate to over two
         thirds of capacity at LIN. This will have a chilling affect  [sic] on competition,
         resulting in less choice and higher price on consumers.  Their dominant market
        share substantially inhibits the development of low cost competitors which impacts
         customers.”1633 This was also the position of the LIN airport manager, saying that
       “As the Transaction (Merger) will involve the consolidation and coordination of
        Capacity, Schedule, Pricing, Inventory management between the two airlines, which
         at LIN will have a dominant position in terms of slots at LIN it might effect [sic] the
        time sensitive passengers which is predominant.” [emphasis added].1634
(1662)  Almost half of respondents among short-haul competitors expressing an opinion
       were of the view  that the  joint market position of Lufthansa and ITA post-
        Transaction may cause them or other carriers to deprioritize or exit the airport.1635
        Neos, for example, stated that “in order for itself as well as other competitors to be

11.4.1.5.2.   The merged entity’s ability to foreclose
(1663)  The large majority of respondents among short-haul competitors considered that
        each of the Parties’ or their combined slot-portfolio constitutes or would constitute a
         barrier to entry and expansion for short-haul competitors post-Transaction.1637 Neos,
         for example, stated that “if Lufthansa and ITA keep the same percentage of slots in
       LIN post-Transaction, it would be more difficult for other carriers to compete on
        routes like Milan – Frankfurt, or Milan – Hamburg.”1638
(1664)  First, the holding of a significant share of slots in LIN, a highly congested airport,
          restricts  the number  of  carriers and  their  operations. The  Transaction would
        exacerbate this situation by concentrating an even larger share of slots in the hands of
         the merged entity and reducing further the number of carriers operating in the airport
        (by merging two carriers into one). As explained by S.E.A, the airport manager of
       LIN, “[Lufthansa] and ITA joint activities at LIN will restrict further the access to
          slots”.1639 The Commission considers that this will follow not only from the reduced
       number of carriers operating in LIN but also because of the increased ability of the
       merged entity to engage in foreclosure tactics as explained further below.
(1665)  Air France-KLM, for example, explained with respect to low cost carriers that “if an
        operator such as Lufthansa has a significant presence in an airport,  it would
        probably make it difficult for a low-cost carrier to operate on a point-to-point basis
       from that airport (e.g., because most likely Lufthansa will hold a significant share of
         the slots that are attractive to low-cost carriers, those being the ones during the
       morning peak hours and the late evening hours, as well as the fact that, a flag
         carrier, in order to serve  its network, use  its high slot capacity to offer many
        frequencies to its destinations, making an entry for a low-cost carrier less attractive).
        This is likely to be the case at LIN and possibly at FCO.”1640
(1666)  Second, respondents explained that the remaining slots will not allow carriers to
        operate on a sustainable  scale. One  carrier explained for example  that “Post-
        Transaction, Wizz Air estimates that the merged entity will have approx. 69% of
         Linate’s slots, and therefore, even if Wizz Air obtains a small number of slots, it will
        not be able to compete with the merged entity in routes to/from Milan meaningfully,
         risking the creation of a similar situation to that of Frankfurt and/or Munich, where
       no carrier can compete with Lufthansa due to  its strong and well established
        presence in those airports. In this context, Wizz Air explains that, even if a small
       number of slots are given to a new entrant in order for them to enter a specific route,
          this will likely not to be possible on the routes where the merged entity will be active
          at, due to the latter’s significant slot holding.1641 Wizz Air added that a large slot

          facilitate the adoption of such decision by the airport. Because of their business
        model, low-cost carriers are more sensitive to high airport charges than Lufthansa.
        Ryanair explained and the Parties did not contest, that it had to decrease activities in
       some airports due to increased airport charges. The Commission considers, therefore,
         that Lufthansa may have in fact an interest in higher airport charges if they would
          result in foreclosing low-cost carriers and decrease competition in an airport.

(1688)  The Parties also argued that the internal documents of Lufthansa relate to […] in

(1689)  This argument also cannot be accepted. The analysis above raised the concern that
        post-Transaction the merged entity will have the ability to foreclose competitors in
      LIN based on the strength of the slot holding position of the merged entity post-
        Transaction in LIN, the material impact of the Transaction on this position and the
        congestion level  at LIN. The internal documents of Lufthansa reviewed above
         reinforce these concerns showing that these are not merely theoretical concerns but
         that there are concrete examples in which Lufthansa was indeed able to use its slot
        holdings in several airports to successfully foreclosure competitors. The Commission
           is not required in addition to form a view whether those examples were “anti-
        competitive” or an abuse of Lufthansa’s dominant position in the airports concerned.
11.4.1.7. Counter-strategies
(1690)  In their Response to the SO the Parties also argued that carriers could relocate to
         other airports in the same catchment area in reaction to higher airport charges.1678
       However, as explained  in section 6.10 above, the relevant market  for  airport
         infrastructure services is LIN alone and the other Milan airports, MXP and BGY, are
        not  substitutable. Consequently, relocation  to MXP or BGY  is not a relevant
         counterstrategy.
(1691)  In more general terms, as observed by the Commission in previous cases, there are
         limited effective and timely counter-strategies that Lufthansa's competitors would be
         likely to deploy in case of foreclosure strategy by Lufthansa. There is no possibility
         for an air carrier to be less reliant on access to airport infrastructure or to sponsor the
        expansion of airport capacity or the opening of new airports.1679
11.4.1.8. Conclusions
(1692)  Based on the high combined slot holding of Lufthansa and ITA in LIN, the high
        congestion at LIN and the views of market participants, and internal documents
       showing past behaviour of the Parties, the Commission finds that the Transaction is
         likely to create or strengthen a dominant slot holding position for the merged entity
         in LIN resulting in the ability for the merged entity to foreclose its competitors.

         prejudice to the powers of public authorities to require the transfer of slots between air carriers and to
         direct how these are allocated pursuant the requirement of competition law.

11.4.2.  Incentive to foreclose
(1693) A dominant carrier at a relevant airport would in principle have a strong incentive to
        pursue a foreclosure strategy, as any new service or expansion by another carrier
       would be likely to introduce or increase competition on one of the dominant carrier's
         routes. Such a dominant carrier would have a greater incentive than any other carrier
          at the airport to keep slots out of reach of other carriers. The incentive to foreclose
       would also grow with the increased size of the slot portfolio it would control at the
          airport.1680
(1694)  Therefore, the Commission needs to analyse (i) the market shares of the merged
         entity in the relevant passenger air transport markets; and (ii) the relative capacity
         constraints faced by the merged entity and its competitors.1681
(1695)  In the specific framework of its assessment of the merged entity’s incentives to
         foreclose other air carriers’ access to airports, the Commission will take account of
           its share on the market for passenger air transport at LIN and the merged entity's fleet
        deployed in that airport.1682
(1696)  First, as can be seen in Table 116 below, in terms of market shares at LIN in number
         of passengers, ITA represented more than half of the passengers. The Transaction
         will increase this share by about 7%, represented by Lufthansa. The Commission
        considers that, those market shares may be sufficient to give an incentive to the
       merged entity to engage in a foreclose strategy.1683
Table 80: Market shares in number of passengers in LIN
                   Summer 2022          Winter 2022        Summer 2023
ITA                       55.9%                58.6%              52%
Lufthansa                  7.3%             7%                 7.2%
Combined                  63.2%                65.6%                59.2%

Source: Response to RFI-22, Table 2.
(1697)  Second, in terms of capacity and capacity constraints, ITA is the only carrier with a
         base1684 at LIN with 27 aircraft.1685 In addition, as described in section 11.4.1, due to
         the lack of available slots at LIN, the competitors of the merged entity would be
        prevented from expanding  their capacity or  starting operations  at LIN with a
         sufficient scale to operate efficiently and compete effectively with the merged
          entity.1686
(1698)  As a consequence, given the merged entity’s large passenger air transport capacity in
       LIN, it may be able to capture the part of the demand from foreclosed competitors,

(1699)  In  addition,  evidence  from  internal  documents  of  the  Parties,  reviewed  in
         section 11.4.1.6 above, shows that the Parties engaged successfully in the past in
         foreclosure strategies and indicates their intention to continue with such practices,
        including with respect to LIN. It can be concluded from these documents that the
       merged entity will have the incentive to engage in foreclosure strategy in LIN post-
         Transaction.
(1700)  In their Response to the SO the Parties did not challenge the finding above and
         limited  their  response  to  stating  that  “the Proposed Transaction… does  not
         materially change the Parties’ incentive to foreclose competitors in LIN.”1688 The
       Commission notes however  that the Transaction will bring about a significant
        increment of about 7% in terms of slots and number of passengers which the merged
         entity would have an interest to protect and therefore increase its the incentive to
         foreclose.
11.4.3.  Overall effect
(1701)  Effective competition would be significantly harmed if the foreclosed air carriers
        played a sufficiently important role in the competitive process on the passenger air
         transport markets from and to the overlap airport. The higher the proportion of
         carriers which would be foreclosed on these markets, the more likely it would be that
         the merger would result in a significant price increase in the passenger air transport
        markets and, therefore, to significantly impede effective competition therein.1689
(1702) On that basis, the Commission will assess whether the creation or strengthening of
         the merged entity’s dominant slot holding position at LIN post-Transaction would
          result in less effective competition for passenger air transport from or to LIN.
(1703)  As noted in section 11.4.1.1, ITA  is by far the largest slot holder in LIN and
        Lufthansa  is the second largest slot holder in LIN with a smaller slot holding
       compared to ITA. The slot holding of the merged entity post-Transaction will be
         significantly larger than those of its competitors in LIN, which hold a small and
        fragmented share of slots.
(1704)  The Commission notes that, when an air carrier holds a significant slot portfolio at a
        given airport while the remaining slot holding is very fragmented and slots are held
       by a large number of small air carriers, the latter are unable to translate these slots
         into a viable alternative to dominant air carriers.1690
(1705)  As indicated by the results of the market investigation reviewed in section 11.4.1.5
        above, the significant difference in slot holdings and deployed capacity (ITA is the
        only  carrier with a base  in LIN, with 27  aircraft) already means  that ITA’s
        competitors are not likely to have a sufficiently large portfolio of slots and capacity

         to react to any anti-competitive behaviour by ITA.1691 As explained by several
        competitors and LIN’s airport manager in section 11.4.1.5.2 above, the Transaction
           is likely to make the situation even we worse since the merged entity will have a
         materially stronger slot holding in LIN post-Transaction.
(1706)  Furthermore, this situation will not be likely to change. As noted in section 11.4.1.3
        above, LIN is highly congested. Competitors of the merged entity are therefore not
         likely to have access to additional slots that would allow viable entry or expansion of
          their activities in LIN.
(1707)  In light of the above, given that the Transaction may result in a disadvantage for their
          rivals by  further increasing  barriers  to  enter or expand  at LIN, and  that the
        competitors of the merged entity could be foreclosed. the Commission raises the
        concern that the dominant slot holding position of the merged entity would likely
        have a significant detrimental effect on competition in the markets for the provision
         of passenger air transport services at LIN.
11.5.   Conclusion
(1708)  The Commission finds that, as a result of its dominant slot holding position at LIN,
         the merged entity would have the ability and incentive post-Transaction to foreclose
        access of its competitors to the markets for the provision of passenger air transport
         services at LIN, leading to anti-competitive effects on the markets for the provision
         of passenger air transport services from and to LIN. On that basis, the Commission
        concludes that the Transaction is likely to significantly impede competition was a
          result of the creation or strengthening of a dominant position in the market for airport
         infrastructure services in LIN

                     12.1.1.3. The Commission’s assessment
(1718)  For a merger with a potential competitor to have significant anti-competitive effects,
       two basic conditions must be fulfilled. First, the potential competitor must already
         exert a significant constraining influence or there must be a significant likelihood
         that  it would grow into an effective competitive force. Evidence that a potential
        competitor has plans  to  enter a market  in a  significant way could help  the
       Commission to reach such a conclusion. Second, there must not be a sufficient
       number of other potential competitors, which could maintain sufficient competitive
        pressure after the merger.
(1719)  These conditions are not fulfilled in the present case.

(1720)  While on the one hand, the evidence shows that ITA has concrete plans to enter the

         sizeable market share on the Rome-Vienna route, the Commission considers that ITA
        does not already exert a significant constraining influence on Lufthansa and that
         there  is  not a  significant  likelihood  that ITA would grow  into an  effective
        competitive force on the route, for the following reasons.
(1721)   First, Lufthansa is currently facing competition from two competing airlines, Ryanair
       and Wizz Air. Assessing the market FCO-VIE, where the overlap between the
         Parties would be most pronounced, Ryanair held a market share of 40% in the Winter

        a market share of 28% in the Winter IATA Season 2023/2024 and 25% in the
      Summer IATA Season 2023.
(1722)  Second, while the two competitors are ULCCs, they operate from the same airports
          at both ends of the route as the Parties, namely VIE and FCO airports. This means
         that the offer in terms of airports served will be identical between the three remaining
        competitors (the merged entity, Ryanair, Wizz Air).
(1723)  Moreover, the Commission notes that, while the majority of competitors active on
         short-haul routes and expressing an opinion considered that the impact of the
        Transaction on potential competition or future competition on routes between Italy
       on the one hand and Germany, Austria, Belgium and/or Switzerland on the other
       hand would be negative, the views of customers on the impact of the Transaction on
         potential competition or future competition on routes between Italy on the one hand
       and Germany, Austria, Belgium and/or Switzerland on the other hand are overall
       mixed and inconclusive.
(1724)  In view of the significant presence of two competing carriers on this route, coupled
        with the inconclusive results of the market investigation, the Commission concludes
          that, all these elements considered, the Transaction would not significantly impede
         effective competition on the route Rome – Vienna by removing the potential
        competition exerted by ITA on the market.

(1738)  The Commission concludes that the Transaction does not lead to a significant
       impediment of effective competition on the routes sited in Table 86 above, for the
        following reasons.



                                    405

[PÁGINA PDF 408]
(1739)  First, in relation to route BLQ-NAP, ITA does not operate a direct connection.
         Instead,  it only operates an indirect flight of a minimum duration of 3 hours.
        Lufthansa does not operate a direct connection on this route either and there is no
        evidence on the Commission’s file indicating entry on the route by Lufthansa with a
         direct connection. Moreover, the Commission notes that the city pair is served by
         direct  train connection  offered by  Trenitalia,  of a  duration  of approximately
        3h30minutes – 4 hours.1703 The direct train connection offered by Trenitalia is falls
       below the 3 – 4 hours threshold  that the Commission’s market  investigation
        suggested as exercising competitive pressure on flights. Therefore, the Commission
        considers  that even post-Transaction, the combined  entity  will face  significant
        competitive pressure from these direct train connections.
(1740)  Therefore, in light of the existence of a convenient direct train connection, as well as
         the lack of evidence of entry by either of the Parties with a direct connection on the
         route, the Commission considers that the possibility for a significant impediment to
         effective competition on this route as a result of the Transaction is improbable and/or
         unlikely to occur.
(1741)  Second, as of Summer IATA 2024, Lufthansa will operate direct flights on the routes
      SUF-HAJ, NAP-STO, NCE-PRG, and PRG-VLC. However, ITA does  not
         currently offer any direct nor indirect flights connecting these city pairs, and, in any
         event, according to its business plan for the next 3 years, […].1704
(1742)  Therefore, the Commission considers that a significant impediment to effective
        competition on these routes as a result of the Transaction is improbable and/or
         unlikely to occur.
(1743)  Third, on the route ROM-PRN, neither Lufthansa nor ITA operates direct flights. In
          particular, ITA has no flight to PRN from either Rome or Milan, whereas […].1705
(1744)  Fourth, with regard to future direct-indirect overlaps, in its past decisional practice with
         regards to short-haul indirect flights, the Commission noted that “indirect flights do not
         generally  provide  a  competitive  constraint  to  direct  flights  absent  exceptional
         circumstances, for example, the direct connection does not allow for a one-day return
          trip or the share of indirect flights in the overall market is significant.”1706 In in the
         present case, and with regard to the routes listed in Table 86, in the absence of any
         specific plans to enter these routes, the Commission does not have any elements to assess
        whether the other party potentially  is in a position to operate one of these routes
          indirectly in the future.1707
(1745)  Therefore, the Commission considers that the possibility for a significant impediment
         to effective competition on these routes as a result of the Transaction is improbable
        and/or unlikely to occur.

(1747)  The Commission concludes that the Transaction does not lead to a significant
       impediment  of  effective  competition on  the above-mentioned  routes,  for  the
        following reasons.1708
(1748)   First, the Parties’ combined market shares on all of the above-mentioned routes are
         overall moderate between Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and Summer IATA
         2023.1709 In particular:
          (a)  On route BRI – ZRH, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          11%-14% over Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and between
          24%-28% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
         (b)  On route CAG-DUS, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          2%-43% over Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and between
          38%-44% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
          (c)  On route SUF-FRA, the  Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          8%-10% over Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and between
          26%-47% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
         (d)  On route MUC-TUN, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          23%-30%  over  Winter IATA  Seasons  2021/2022  and  2022/2023,  and
          24%-44% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
          (e)  On route NAP-BRU, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          20%-25%  over  Winter IATA  Seasons  2021/2022  and  2022/2023,  and
          36%-39% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
           (f)  On route NAP-ZRH, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between
          15%-44%  over  Winter IATA  Seasons  2021/2022  and  2022/2023,  and
          35%-39% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.




1708    The Commission notes that for its assessment it has considered the IATA Seasons for which complete
         data is available, which are the seasons from Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 until Summer IATA
       2023 (included). However, even if the Commission considered the data available for Winter IATA
        Season 2023/2024, the assessment would not change. In particular, for the routes Trieste – Munich and
         Cagliari – Düsseldorf, where the market shares of Lufthansa and ITA are above 50%, see footnote 1716
       and paragraph (1745)(b).
1709    The Commission notes that these market shares may be considered “overall moderate” only in the very
         specific circumstances of the present case, including particularly active competitors on the Italian
        market, the direct/indirect nature of the overlaps and the results of the market investigation in the
         present case.

         (g)  On route PMO-BRU, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between 6%-
         9% over Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and 15%-21% over
          Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023.
         (h)  On route FLR-BRU, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between 9%-

           (i)  On route TRS-MUC, the Parties’ combined market share ranges between 16%-

(1749)  Second, combined with the low combined market shares,1712 in many of the routes
         identified in Table 87 above, the increment brought by the Transaction is minimal,
       and ranging between 0%-3%. In particular:
          (a)  On route BRI – ZRH, the increment brought by the Transaction ranges
            between 2% and 3% except for one IATA season, namely Summer IATA
             2023, where the increment is significant, at 8%.
         (b)  On route CAG-DUS, the increment brought by the Transaction ranges between
         0% and 1% except for one IATA season, namely Winter IATA 2022/2023,
            where the increment is significant, at 9%.
          (c)  On route SUF-FRA, the increment brought by the Transaction over the winter
              seasons is 0%, whereas it is significant over the summer seasons, between 5-
           8%.
         (d)  On  route MUC-TUN,  the increment brought by  the  Transaction ranges
            between 0% and 2%.
          (e)  On route NAP-BRU the increment brought by the Transaction ranges between
         2% and 3% except for one IATA season, namely Summer IATA 2023, where
              the increment is significant, at 8%.
           (f)  On route NAP-ZRH, the increment brought by the Transaction ranges between
         0% and 1% with the exception of one IATA season, namely Winter IATA
             2022/2023, where the increment is higher, at 4%.
         (g)  On route PMO-BRU the increment brought by the Transaction over the winter
              seasons is 2%, whereas it is significant over the summer seasons, at 9%.
         (h)  On route FLR-BRU, the increment brought by the Transaction is negligible
             over both IATA seasons, namely between 0%-1%.

         Airlines had only one flight with a total capacity of 141 seats. (See response of Lufthansa and MEF to a
       Commission’s request for information (RFI 38), question 10). Therefore, the Commission notes that the
        Transaction does not give rise to a direct/indirect overlap over the Winter IATA Seasons, as Lufthansa
        only operates direct flights over summer. For more information on the assessment of indirect/indirect
         short-haul overlaps, see section 12.2.3.2 below.

(1750)  Third, there is at least one other active competitor offering direct connections (in
       most cases from an airport of proximity on at least one end of the route) and often
        holding a higher market share than that of the Parties combined in the widest
         plausible market.1713 In particular:
          (a)  On route BRI – ZRH, easyJet is active (operating from BSL on the Zurich end,
            and from the same airport as the Parties from the Bari end, i.e., BRI) with a
             market  share ranging between 86% – 88% over Winter IATA Seasons
            2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and between 36%-39%  over Summer IATA
             Seasons 2022 and 2023. The remaining market shares are captured by other
               indirect competitors.
         (b)  On route CAG-DUS, Neos was active during Winter IATA 2021/2022 with a
             market share of 98%. Moreover, Ryanair entered the route as of Summer IATA
            2022 (operating from NRN on the Dusseldorf end, and from the same airport as
              the Parties from the Cagliari end, i.e., CAG) with a market share of 56% over
             Winter IATA Season 2022/2023, and between 54%-61% over Summer IATA
             Seasons 2022 and 2023.
          (c)  On route SUF-FRA, Ryanair is active (operating from HHN on the Frankfurt
              end, and from the same airport as the Parties from the Lamezia Terme end, i.e.,
           SUF) with a market share ranging between 90% – 92% over Winter IATA
             Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and between 1%-2% over Summer IATA
             Seasons 2022 and 2023. However, another competitor is active on the route
              seasonally over the summer seasons, namely Condor, which operates from the
           same airport as the Parties on both ends (i.e., FRA and SUF), and obtained a
             market share of 52%-71% over the same period.
         (d)  On route MUC-TUN, Tunisair is active (operating from the same airports as
              the Parties on both ends) with a market share ranging between 64% – 71% over
             Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023, and 41%-50% over Summer
          IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023. Moreover, during Summer IATA 2023, there
           was entry by Nouvelair Tunisie, which managed to capture 26% of the market
               share, suggesting that barriers to entry and expand are low. Where applicable,
              the remaining market shares are captured by other indirect competitors (such as
             Air Europa through Madrid, Air France – KLM through Paris).
          (e)  On route NAP-BRU, currently Ryanair is active (operating from CLR on the
              Brussels end and from NAP on the Naples end) with a market share ranging
            between 73% – 74% over Winter IATA Seasons 2021/2022 and 2022/2023,
            and 56%-60% over Summer IATA Seasons 2022 and 2023. Over the summer
              season, another competitor, namely TUI Fly is active with direct flights from
              the same airports of operation as the Parties (i.e., BRU and NAP) with a market
              share between 4% and 5%.
           (f)  On route NAP-ZRH, easyJet is active (operating from BSL on the Zurich end,
            and from the same airport as the Parties from the Naples end, i.e., NAP) with a
             market  share ranging between 54% – 84% over Winter IATA Seasons

(1751)  Fourth, without prejudice to the Commission’s findings on closeness of competition
       between  airlines  operating each  short-haul  route from  the same  airports  (see
         section 9.1.2 above), the Commission considers that the direct flights offered by
        competitors even when from secondary airports of proximity, are likely to compete
         closely with the direct flights offered by Lufthansa, due to the views expressed by
        customers and confirmed by competitors during the market investigation as regards
         direct short-haul flights. In particular that (i) direct and indirect routes are generally
        not substitutable between Italy on the one hand and DACHB on the other, (ii) but
        passengers consider indirect flights as substitutable if there is only one company
         offering a direct flight.1714 Likewise, the similarity in the overall travel time between
       ITA’s indirect flight option (from the main airport serving each region, however
        including  additional layover  time) and  the  competitors’  direct  option from a
        secondary airport of proximity (only on one end of each route, if so) which requires
         additional travel time to reach the secondary airport from the city centre, also suggest
         that the direct flights offered by competitors from secondary airports of proximity on
         these routes are at least similarly competitive with Lufthansa’s direct flights as ITA’s
         indirect flights from the same airport. For example:
          (a)   According to the Parties’ submission, the minimum travel time from Zurich
                city  centre  to ZRH (based on  the most  efficient mean  of  transport)  is
            12 minutes, whereas to BSL is 1h 05 minutes.1715 The additional travel time to
          BSL is comparable to a layover of ITA on routes BRI – ZRH and NAP - ZRH
             which, according to ITA’s own website, last 0h 50 – 1h 05 minutes (ITA also
               offers additional indirect options with longer layovers of >3h) for both routes.

(1752)  As demonstrated above, the similarity between the travel time to the secondary
         airport (to fly directly) and the duration of ITA’s layovers renders the overall travel
        times of ITA’s indirect flights and the third-party competitors’ direct flights from
        proximity airports comparable. Thus, ITA’s indirect flights likely to compete closely
        with the direct flights offered by competitors from secondary airports of proximity
       on these routes and more closely than they compete with Lufthansa’s direct flights
       from the same airport (the latter of which is likely to offer the most attractive flight

(1753)  Moreover, where competitors operate from the same main airports as the Parties
       from both ends of the route (i.e., Tunisair on MUC-TUN, Tui Fly on NAP-BRU and
      PMO-BRU, Condor on SUF-FRA and the Tui Group on TRS-MUC),1721 the latter’s
        operations  are  likely  to compete more  closely with Lufthansa’s  direct  flights
       compared to the indirect flights of ITA, due to the preference expressed by customers
       and confirmed by competitors for direct short-haul flights.
(1754)  Fifth, as indicated above, for most city pairs, the other direct competitors operate
       from secondary airports of proximity on one end of each route (i.e., on all routes with
         the exception of Tunisair on MUC-TUN, Tui Fly on NAP-BRU and PMO-BRU, and
       Condor on SUF-FRA). Consequently, under the narrowest plausible product market
         definition (i.e., the one taking into account only the primary airports of each city, see
        Section 6.5 above), the direct activities of the Parties’ competitors (e.g., Ryanair,
         easyJet) do not belong in the same market as the activities of the Parties. Thus, under
         the narrowest plausible market definition, the transaction would result in higher
       combined market shares and/or (quasi-) monopolies of the Parties post-Transaction.
       However, the Commission considers that, in light of the findings that (i) there is a
        general preference by customers for direct short-haul flights, as well as (ii) it is likely
         that Lufthansa and ITA both compete more closely with the other direct operators
       compared to how closely they compete with each other on the routes indicated in this
         section, the out of market constraints exerted by the direct flights from secondary
         airports  will be  strong.  Therefore, even under  the narrowest  possible market
         definition, it is unlikely that the Transaction would result in significant impediment
        of effective competition, as the  latter will continue to exert significant (out-of-
        market) competitive  pressure over  the  Parties’  activities on  the  direct/indirect
        overlapping routes identified in this section.
12.2.2.5. Routes where an important competitor is offering direct flights
(1755)  Table 88 below  lists a number of routes where the Transaction gives  rise to
         horizontally affected markets, and where the combined market share of the Parties
         often exceeds 50%, but the Commission nonetheless concludes that the possibility
         for a significant impediment on effective competition as a result of the Transaction is
        improbable and/or unlikely to occur, due to the direct operations of a rival on the city
         pair (often from a regional airport of proximity).

(1756)  The Commission concludes that on most of the routes indicated in Table 88, the
        Transaction will not result in a significant impediment to effective competition due
         to the direct operations of a rival on the city pair (often from a regional airport of
         proximity).
(1757)  This  is supported by the  results of the Commission’s market investigation on
          substitutability between direct and indirect flights between Italy on the one hand,
        and, Germany, Austria, Belgium and/or Switzerland on the other hand. In particular,
        as already indicated  in section  6.6.3.1 above, the majority of customers who
        expressed an opinion in the market investigation were of the view that these flight
        operations are not substitutable, whereas only a large share of customers, about 40%,
        considered that convenient indirect flights are substitutable to direct flights when
         there is only one direct flight option.1722 Similarly, half of the carriers considered that
       when there is only one direct flight option, customers may consider the direct option
         substitutable with convenient indirect flights.1723 The views expressed during the
       Commission’s market investigation, are supported by factual evidence, suggesting
         that the more direct short-haul flights available, the less the attractiveness of the
         indirect alternatives, as customers tend to opt for the direct option (see Table 60
         above).1724
(1758)  Therefore, for the purposes of its assessment, the Commission only considered city
         pairs where no other direct competitor is active on the route. As indicated in Table 88
        above:
          (a)   Ryanair is active on the route BRI – FRA with a direct flight over the Summer
          IATA Seasons,1725 operating from HHN on the Frankfurt end, and from the
           same airport as the Parties from the Bari end (i.e., BRI);
         (b)   Ryanair is active on the route BDS – MUC with a direct flight, operating from
        FMM on the Munich end, and from the same airport as the Parties on the
               Brindisi end (i.e., BDS);
          (c)   easyJet is active on the route CAG – ZRH with a direct flight, operating from
          BSL on the Zurich end, and from the same airport as the Parties on the Cagliari
            end (i.e., CAG);
         (d)  on the route CTA – HAM, no third-party competitor was active and offering
                direct flights between Winter IATA 2021 and Summer IATA 2023. However,

1722     Responses to question C.C.1 of questionnaire 06 to customers of both short-haul and long-haul flights; and
         Responses to question C.C.2 of questionnaire 06 to customers of both short-haul and long-haul flights.
1723     Responses to question C.4 of questionnaire 03 to short-haul competitors and Responses to question C.5 of
          questionnaire 03 to short-haul competitors.
1724     As explained in section 6.6.3, the Commission considers that, in accordance to its prior practice, direct and indirect
           flights between the same short-haul route O&D make part of the same market when indirect flights represent at
           least 10% of passengers on the route. Nevertheless, as explained in this paragraph, the Commission’s market
          investigation suggests that the more direct short-haul flights available, the less the attractiveness of the indirect
           alternatives. In fact, if two direct alternatives compete on a route, the competitive pressure exerted by the indirect
          alternatives appear to be minimal. On this basis, while based on the market definition certain indirect flights may be
          part of the same market as two (or more) direct flights by other operators, the Commission considers that the
         Transaction will not result in a significant impediment to effective competition on such routes. This consideration
          also rests on the specific circumstances of this case, in particular the Italian market, where a number of competitors
          are active and constantly increasing their activities.
1725    On the contrary, the Commission concludes that the Transaction results in a significant impediment to effective
         competition on the route BRI – FRA over the Winter IATA Seasons, as Ryanair exited. According to Ryanair, its
           exit from these routes over the winter IATA seasons was linked to the “routes’ poor performance during the Winter
       IATA 2021/2022 season as a result of competition from larger flag-carrier competitors operating out of Frankfurt-
         Main”, the only ones being Lufthansa and ITA. Moreover, the Commission’s market investigation did not bring up
         evidence of market entry on route BRI – FRA over the Winter IATA Seasons, see section 9.4.6.2.3 above.

(1759)  Regarding the route FLR – ROM, the Commission notes that there are no direct
          flights competing on this route. However, Trenitalia and Italo Treno operate a
       number of daily direct connections on the route FLR – ROM, of 1h30 minutes to
       2h 35 minutes travel duration. These travel durations  fall within the time-range
       where based on the previous practice of the European Commission air and train
        passenger transport services may be substitutable with each other (see section 6.8
        above). Therefore, while the Commission cannot consider any direct air passenger
         transport competition on this route,  it considers that, also in light of the direct-
         indirect nature of the overlap, the relatively short and direct train connection exerts
         sufficient competitive pressure on this route.

(1760)  Moreover, the market share of the third party operating on the route is, in all cases
         significant, and often higher than the combined market share of the Parties:1729
           (a)  On the route BRI – FRA, even though Ryanair operates from HHN, its market
              share over the Summer IATA Seasons of 2022 and 2023 is significant, and
              ranges between 44% and 50% whereas the Parties’ combined market share
              ranges between 50% and 56% over the same time period;
         (b)  on the route BDS – MUC even though Ryanair operates from FMM, its market
              share from Winter IATA 2021/2022 to Summer 2023 ranges between 40% and
          82% whereas the Parties’ combined market share ranges between 18% and
          59% over the same time period;
          (c)   on the route CAG – ZRH even though easyJet operates from BSL, its market
              share from Winter IATA 2021/2022 to Summer 2023 is significant, and ranges
            between 20% and 62%;
         (d)  on CTA – HAM, Wizz Air operates (as of Summer IATA 2024) two weekly
               frequencies, compared  to Eurowings  that  operates  four  (direct) weekly
              frequencies over  the Summer IATA Seasons,  therefore  the Commission
              considers that it is likely to obtain significant market shares on this route. The
            Commission also notes that this route is also covered by the Commitments set
              out in section 14.5.1 below, as the Short-Haul Remedy Taker will be able to
              provide indirect connections between CTA and HAM;
          (e)   on the route CTA – FRA, even though Ryanair operates from HHN, its market
              share from Winter IATA 2021/2022 to Summer 2023 ranges between 29% and
          79% whereas the Parties’ combined market share ranges between 21% and
          71% over the same time period;
           (f)   on the route CTA – MUC, even though Wizz Air operates from FMM, its
             market share from Sumer IATA 2022 (when it entered the route) to Summer
          IATA 2023 ranges between 33% and 65% whereas the Parties’ combined
             market share ranges between 26% and 64% over the same time period;
         (g)  on the route SUF – DUS where Condor is active over the Summer IATA
              Seasons, its market share is significant over Summer IATA 2022 and Summer
          IATA 2023, and ranges between 27% and 29%. Over Summer IATA 2022,
           when Corendon Airlines was also active on the route, it managed to also obtain
             a significant market share of 14%;
         (h)  on the route SUF – ZRH, even though easyJet operates from BSL, its market
              share over the Summer IATA Seasons of 2022 and 2023 is significant, and
              ranges between 43% and 44%, whereas its market share over the Winter IATA
            2021/2022 and 2022/2023 Seasons  is  meaningfully  lower, between 3%
            and 4%; and,
           (i)   on the route PMO – FRA, where Ryanair operates from HHN, its market share
                  is significant from Winter IATA 2021/2022 to Summer 2023, and ranges
            between 20% and 70% whereas the Parties’ combined market share ranges
            between 60% and 68% over the same time period;

(1761) On the route FLR – ROM, the duration of both Trenitalia and Italo Treno’s direct

        connections.
(1762)  In  addition, without  prejudice  to  the Commission’s  findings on  closeness  of
        competition between airlines operating each short-haul route from the same airports
         (see section 9.1.2 above), the Commission considers that the direct flights offered by
        competitors even when from secondary airports of proximity, are likely to be
        competitive compared with the direct flights offered by Lufthansa, as expressed by
        customers and confirmed by competitors over direct short-haul flights.1730 Likewise,
         the similarity in the overall travel time between ITA’s indirect flight option (from the
       main airport serving each region, however including additional layover time) and the
        competitors’ direct option from a secondary airport of proximity (only on one end of
        each route, if so) which requires additional travel time to reach the secondary airport
       from the city centre, also suggest that ITA’s indirect flights are likely to compete
         closely with the direct flights offered by competitors from secondary airports of
        proximity on these routes and with Lufthansa’s direct flights from the same airport.
        For example:
          (a)   According to the Parties’ submission, the minimum travel time from Frankfurt
                city  centre  to FRA (based on  the most  efficient mean  of  transport)  is
            10 minutes, whereas to HHN is 1h 15 minutes.1731 The additional travel time to
        HHN is comparable to most of the layovers of ITA on routes BRI – FRA,
        CTA – FRA and PMO  - FRA which, according to ITA’s own booking
              platform (website), last: (a) on BRI – FRA, 0h 55 minutes (whereas ITA also
               offers additional indirect options with longer layovers of >2h); (b) on CTA –
         FRA between 1h 0 minutes to 1h 10 minutes (whereas ITA also offers
               additional indirect options with longer layovers, e.g., 1h 55 minutes, >3h etc.);

         airport (to fly directly) and the duration of ITA’s layovers renders the overall travel
        times of ITA’s indirect flights and the third-party competitors’ direct flights from
        proximity airports comparable.
(1764)  Furthermore, where competitors operate from the same main airports as the Parties
       from both ends of the route (i.e., Wizz Air on CTA – HAM, easyJet on PMO –
     GVA and Condor on SUF – DUS), the latter’s operations are likely to compete more
         closely with Lufthansa’s direct flights compared to the indirect flights of ITA, due to
         the preference expressed by customers and confirmed by competitors for direct short-
        haul flights.1735
(1765)  Finally, as indicated above, for most city pairs, the other direct competitors operate
       from secondary airports of proximity on one end of each route (i.e., on all routes
        except for Wizz Air on CTA – HAM, easyJet on PMO – GVA and Condor on SUF
       – DUS). Consequently, under the narrowest plausible product market definition (i.e.,
         the one taking into account only the primary airports of each city, see Section 6.5

        above), the direct activities of the Parties’ competitors (e.g., Ryanair) do not belong
         in the same market as the activities of the Parties. Thus, under the narrowest
         plausible market definition, the transaction would result in higher combined market
        shares and/or (quasi-) monopolies of the Parties post-Transaction. However, the
       Commission considers  that, in  light of the findings that  (i) there  is a general
        preference by customers for direct short-haul flights, as well as (ii) it is likely that
        Lufthansa and ITA both compete more closely with the other direct operators
       compared to how closely they compete with each other on the routes indicated in this
         section, the out of market constraints exerted by the direct flights from secondary
         airports will be strong and thus, even under the narrowest possible market definition,
         the latter will continue to exert significant (out-of-market) competitive pressure over
         the Parties’ activities on the direct/indirect overlapping routes identified in this
         section. Therefore,  it is unlikely that the Transaction would result in significant
       impediment of effective competition on these routes.

(1767)  Regarding NAP – DUS, the Commission concluded that the Transaction will result
         in a significant impediment to effective competition over the Winter IATA Season
         (see  section  9.4.6.4.3  above). However,  the Commission  concludes  that  the
        Transaction will not result in a significant impediment to effective competition over
         the Summer IATA Season, considering ITA’s negligible market share over Summer
      IATA 2022 and Summer IATA 2023 which was 0% and 1.5% respectively. Due to
         the negligible activity of ITA, the Commission concludes that the latter is unlikely to
         exercise a competitive constraint over Lufthansa’s activities on NAP - DUS over the
       summer season, and that post-Transaction the competitive dynamics will, in essence,
        remain unchanged.
(1768)  Similarly, on route BLQ – ZRH, the Commission concludes that the Transaction
         will not result in a significant impediment to effective competition, considering
       ITA’s negligible market share between Winter 2021/2022 and Summer 2023, which
       was consistently 1% (and exceptionally 3% over Summer IATA 2022). Due to the
         negligible activity of ITA, the Commission concludes that the latter is unlikely to
         exercise a competitive constraint over Lufthansa’s activities on BLQ - ZRH over the
       summer season, and that post-Transaction the competitive dynamics will, in essence,
        remain unchanged.
(1769)  Finally, the Commission reaches the same conclusion on route GOA – MUC, due to
       ITA’s de minimis market share between Winter 2021/2022 and Summer 2023, which
       was consistently between 1% and 2% (and exceptionally 21% over Winter IATA
        2021/2022).
(1770)  In this context, the Commission concludes that the 21% market share that ITA
        obtained over Winter IATA 2021/2022 is not representative of its actual competitive
         position on the route because: (i) over the remaining season’s ITA’s market share
       was significantly low, and in fact negligible, on a consistent basis; and (ii) the high
        market share during Winter IATA 2021/2022 is the result of an exceptionally low
       number of passengers (i.e., 375 passengers) during the Covid19 pandemic. Although
         the Commission did not apply a passenger  traffic  filter for  its assessment of
         direct/indirect overlaps in this present case, the inconsistency between the passenger
          traffic on this route during the remaining IATA seasons, compared to Winter IATA
       2021/2022 justifies the conclusion reached regarding the competitive landscape.
        Consequently, due to the negligible activity of ITA, the Commission concludes that
         the latter is unlikely to exercise a competitive constraint over Lufthansa’s activities
       on GOA - MUC over the summer season, and that post-Transaction the competitive
       dynamics will, in essence, remain unchanged.

      IATA Season, where the Transaction gives  rise to an indirect/indirect overlap,

         position on the route, as it held 87%-90% of the market over the same time period.

        over the summer seasons).
12.2.3.2. Indirect/indirect short-haul overlaps
(1777)  The Commission assessed the 1274 indirect/indirect short-haul overlaps that the
        Transaction gave rise to. As indicated above, in  its past decisional practice, the
       Commission applied filters to exclude likely unproblematic indirect/indirect short-
        haul routes from the scope of its investigation (the criterion must have been met in
         the four last completed IATA Seasons):
          (a)  The Parties’ combined market shares are below 25%; or,
         (b)  One of the Parties has a market share below 2%; or,
          (c)  The total annual traffic is below 15 000 passengers; or,
         (d)  The route was below the HHI thresholds of paragraph 20 of the Horizontal
            Merger Guidelines.1741
(1778)  After considering the filters indicated above in paragraph (1773), 38 potentially
        problematic  routes  remain.  For  these  routes  the Commission  conducted  an
         individual, route-by-route assessment, and although its assessment was not limited
          to, it focussed in particular on, those where:
          (a)  The Parties’ combined market share was equal to or above 40% in at least one
              of the four IATA Seasons between IATA Winter 2021/2022 and IATA
          Summer 2023; and,
         (b)  The increment brought by the Transaction was equal to or above 5% in at least
            one of the four IATA Seasons between IATA Winter 2021/2022 and IATA
          Summer 2023.
(1779)  The Commission assessed these overlaps and concluded that the Transaction does
        not result in significant impediment to effective competition on either of these routes,
       due  to  either the generally low passenger  traffic, or the  availability of  direct
        competition. The Commission notes that  it could not exclude on this basis the
        following routes: BRI-NCE (Summer 2022 IATA Season), PMO-AMS (Winter
       2022/2023 Season), ZRH-TUN (Summer 2022 IATA Season).

1741     Case M.9287 – Connect Airways / Flybe, decision dated 05 July 2019, footnote 341.

        following specific circumstances:
          (a)  On the route BRI-NCE, easyJet has entered to route as a direct competitor in

         (b)  On the route PMO-AMS, direct competitors were active on the route during all

          (c)  On the route ZRH-TUN a direct competitor has entered in the  last two

12.3.   Competitive assessment – horizontal overlaps on long-haul routes
12.3.1.  Assessment of non-problematic direct overlaps
(1782)  The Commission considers that on the long-haul overlap routes between Milan-
      New York, Rome-New York, and Rome-Chicago, where both Lufthansa’s  joint
        venture partner United Airlines and ITA currently (or very recently) offer direct
        connections, the Transaction would not significantly impede effective competition
         for the following reasons.
12.3.1.1. Milan-New York

         transported point-to-point (direct and indirect) under the widest plausible market
         definition is presented in Table 91 below.

       Milan Bergamo Airport (BGY) are the relevant airports near Milan. Newark Liberty
         International  Airport (EWR),  John  F. Kennedy  International  Airport  (JFK),
       LaGuardia Airport (LGA) and New York Stewart International Airport (SWF) are all
         located, even though to a different extent, near New York. Therefore, the assessment
         in this section includes the following airport pairs: MXP-EWR, MXP-JFK, MXP-
      LGA, MXP-SWF, LIN-EWR, LIN-JFK, LIN-LGA LIN-SWF, BGY-EWR, BGY-

        include both time-sensitive and non-time-sensitive passengers, as well as direct and
         indirect connections.

        (based on Winter 2023/24 and Summer 2024): American Airlines, Delta, Emirates,
      ITA (as explained below ITA exited this route in January 2024), La Compagnie,
       Neos and Lufthansa’s joint venture partner United Airlines. Other airline carriers
         active on this route operate via indirect flights only.

12.3.1.1.2.    Competitive assessment
(1787)  According to Lufthansa and MEF, ITA has ceased direct operations on this route
         since January 2024 in order for ITA to fully focus its long-haul operations on its hub
         in Rome-Fiumicino.1744 Lufthansa and MEF submit  that  therefore  the Milan-
      New York route should not be assessed as a direct overlap between the Parties.
(1788)  However, given that ITA’s business plan from March 2023, covering the period
        2023-2027, was already designed assuming that the Transaction will take place (see
         also section 7.2.3), the Commission considers that it cannot conclude with sufficient

         certainty that ITA would also exit this route in the relevant counterfactual where the

(1789)  Nevertheless, even assuming ITA would continue to operate a direct connection on
          this route absent the Transaction, for the reasons set out below, the Commission
        concludes that the Transaction would not significantly impede effective competition
       on the route Milan-New York under any plausible market definition during both
      IATA Winter and Summer season.
(1790)  First, the Parties’ combined share on this route is moderate at 30% or below in each
        of the last six IATA seasons.
(1791)  Second, the Parties will continue to face important competition on this route from
         several competitors with sizable market shares. Namely, as shown in Table 91, the
        Transaction would leave, in addition to Lufthansa and  its A++ JV partners, the
        following relevant competitors: The Blue Skies JV with markets shares between 14%
       and 24%, the AA-IAG JV with market shares between 10% and 19%, Emirates with
        market shares between 21% and 40%, and Neos with market shares between 6%
       and 13% during the  last six IATA seasons. In addition, the above competitors,
         together with La Compagnie, will continue to offer direct connections on this route.
        For the reasons outlined in section 10.1.4, airline passengers prefer direct flights over
         indirect  flights and therefore these  five competitors  will continue  to be close
        competitors to the Parties on this route.
(1792)  Third, while  the views  of  competitors and customers on  the impact  of  the

(1793)  Fourth, the Commission has taken into consideration multiple exceptional factors of
          this case, namely that ITA’s long-term competitiveness as a standalone carrier is
        highly uncertain (see section 7.2.2) and that, following the Transaction, ITA will
         retain some ability and incentive to compete against Lufthansa’s A++ joint venture
         partners, in particular due to the presence of MEF as a controlling shareholder (see
         section 10.1.1).
(1794)  In conclusion, the Transaction would not significantly impede effective competition
        with respect to the Milan-New York route during both IATA Winter and Summer
        season.

1746     At the time of writing this Decision, passenger data for the Winter 2023/2024 season was only available
       up until January 2024. This table therefore does not include two months of passenger data for Winter

(1800)  First, despite the Parties’ high combined market shares, they will continue to face
        competition from both the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV on this route. While
         the Parties, following the Transaction, will have an airport hub on both ends of the
         route, both Delta, a member of the Blue Skies JV, and American Airlines, a member
        of the AA-IAG JV, have an airports hub at New York-JFK airport.1748 Therefore, in
          this particular case, these airlines have access to feeder traffic from their short-haul
       and domestic operations at JFK airport which strengthens their profitability on this
         route. In addition, the fact that these JVs have an airport hub on one end of this route
        could mean that these airlines can flexibly adapt capacity in order to respond to
        changes in demand on this route. Furthermore, given the importance of economies of
         scale, the fact that both the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV have airport hubs at
      JFK airport might enable these airlines to operate direct and indirect operations on
          this route at a relatively low cost-base and therefore act as a significant competitor to
         the  Parties. Therefore, the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV are significant
        competitors to the Parties on this route (albeit the Parties will have some advantages
        as a result of having an airport hub on both ends of the route).
(1801)  Second, during the last summer season (Summer 2023), which is the first season
         since Norse’s direct entry on this route, the Parties’ combined market share was
       below 50%,  i.e., below the dominance threshold as  set out  in the Horizontal
        Guidelines.
(1802)  Third, during the summer seasons, the Parties will continue to face important
        competition on this route from three competitors with sizable market shares. Namely,
        as shown in Table 92, the Transaction would leave, in addition to Lufthansa and its
      A++ JV partners, the following relevant competitors: the Blue Skies JV with markets
        shares between 21% and 25%, the AA-IAG JV with market shares between 15%
       and 16%, and Norse with a market share equal to 12% in the first season that it had
        entered this route.1749 The above competitors will continue to offer direct connections
       on this route during the summer season. For the reasons outlined in section 10.1.4,
          airline passengers prefer direct flights over indirect flights and therefore these three
        competitors will continue to be close competitors to the Parties on this route.
(1803)  Fourth, during the winter seasons, the Parties, despite their high combined market
         shares, will continue to face competition on this route from a strong competitor, the
       Blue Skies JV, with market shares ranging from 26% to 31%, as shown in Table 92.
       The Blue Skies JV will continue to offer direct connections on this route during the
        winter seasons. As the AA-IAG JV does not have any direct connection on this route
         in the winter season, its market share is relatively modest during the winter seasons,
        ranging from 3% to 6%. However, given that JFK airport is an airport hub for
       American Airlines, a member of the AA-IAG JV, as described at paragraph (1796)
        above, it therefore is a relevant potential direct competitor on this route during the
        winter season. Norse is not active during the winter season.

        not significantly impede effective competition on the route Rome-Chicago under any
         plausible market definition during both IATA Winter and Summer season.
(1813)  First, despite the Parties’ high combined market share, they will continue to face
        competition from the AA-IAG JV on this route. While the Parties, following the
         Transaction, will have an airport hub on both ends of the route, American Airlines, a
      member of  the AA-IAG JV, has an  airport hub  at Chicago-ORD  airport.1754
        Therefore, in this particular case, the AA-IAG JV has access to significant feeder
          traffic from American Airlines’ short-haul and domestic operations at ORD airport
       which strengthens its profitability on the route. In addition, the fact that the AA-IAG
      JV has an airport hub on one end of the route could mean that it can flexibly adapt
        capacity in order to respond to changes in demand on this route. Furthermore, given

12.3.2.  Assessment of non-problematic direct-indirect overlaps
(1819)  Consistent with its practice,1756 the Commission has applied the following filters to
        exclude likely unproblematic direct / indirectly overlapping routes from the scope of
           its investigation. For a route to be excluded, at least one of the filters must have been
       met in all the 4 last completed IATA seasons and for all passenger segmentations:1757
          (a)   The Parties' combined market share was below 25%, or
         (b)   one of the Parties had a market share below 2%, or
          (c)   the total annual traffic was below 30 000 passengers,1758 or
         (d)   the route was below the HHI thresholds of paragraphs 19 and 20 of the
              Horizontal Merger Guidelines.1759
(1820)  Routes where one of the Parties offers a direct flight and the other offers an indirect
          flight only and that are excluded based on the above filters are not further discussed
         in this Decision.
(1821)  In relation to the remaining overlapping routes where one of the Parties offers a
         direct flight and the other offers an indirect flight, the Commission has identified the
        following relevant 12 overlapping O&Ds with origin/destination in the EEA or
         Switzerland1760 for which it has found that, even though the conditions for applying
         the above  filters are not met, the Transaction would not  significantly impede
         effective competition:1761 Athens-Washington (ATH-WAS), Brussel-Tokyo (BRU-
       TYO),  Naples-New York  (NAP-NYC),  Rome-Boston  (ROM-BOS),  Rome-
       Buenos Aires (ROM-BUE), Rome-Delhi (ROM-DEL), Rome-Los Angeles (ROM-
       LAX), Rome-Miami (ROM-MIA), Rome-Sao Paulo (ROM-SAO), Rome-Tokyo
      (ROM-TYO), Venice-New York (VCE-NYC), and Zurich-Cairo (ZRH-CAI).

12.3.2.2. Competitive assessment
(1824)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
        not significantly impede effective competition on these routes under any plausible
        market definition during both IATA Winter and Summer season:
(1825)  First,  the  Parties’ combined share  is moderate  or  relatively moderate (below
        40%)1763 or below the dominance threshold (below 50%)1764 over each of the last
        four complete IATA seasons for 6 out of 12 routes. As of the remaining 6 routes
       where the Parties’ combined markets shares are higher than 50% in some of the last
        four complete IATA seasons, on three of these routes  (i.e., Athens-Washington,
        Brussel-Tokyo,  and  Zurich-Cairo),  the  increment  arising  as  a  result  of  the
        Transaction is small (between 1% and 6%). On the other three routes (i.e., Rome-
       Miami, Rome-Los Angeles and Naples-New York), the Parties will continue to face
         significant competition from both the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV. Notably:
          (a)  On the Rome-Miami route, while the A++ JV does not have an airport hub in
            Miami, American Airlines (which is part of the AA-IAG JV) does have an
               airport hub in Miami.1765 Therefore, as further illustrated in section 10.1.2 of
                this Decision, the AA-IAG JV has access to significant feeder traffic in Miami.
              In addition, the fact that this JV has an airport hub on one end of this route
             could mean that it can flexibly adapt capacity in order to respond to changes in
           demand on this route. Furthermore, given economies of scale, the fact that the
          AA-IAG JV has an airport hub in Miami means that this airline can operate on
                this route at relatively low cost. Therefore, the AA-IAG JV is a significant
                (potential) competitor to the Parties on the Rome-Miami route. This is also
              exemplified by its sizeable market shares on this route, equal to between 11%
            and 32% over the last six seasons.1766 Other relevant competitors on this route
              include the Blue Skies JV (with market shares ranging from 6% to 21%), TAP
             Air Portugal (with market shares ranging from 4% to 13%) and Air Europa
              (with market shares ranging from 2% to 15%).1767
         (b)  On the Rome-Los Angeles route, both the AA-IAG JV and the Blue Skies JV
              are competitors to the Parties. In particular, in addition to United Airlines (A++
              JV), both American Airlines (AA-IAG JV) and Delta (Blue Skies JV) have an
               airport hub at LAX airport in Los Angeles.1768 Therefore, as further illustrated
               in section 10.1.2 of this Decision, both the AA-IAG JV and the Blue Skies JV
             have access to significant feeder traffic in Los Angeles. In addition, the fact
                that these JVs have an airport hub on one end of this route could mean that
              these airlines can flexibly adapt capacity in order to respond to changes in
           demand on these routes. Furthermore, given economies of scale, the fact that
             both the Blue Skies JV and the AA-IAG JV have airport hub at LAX airport
            means that these airlines can operate on these routes at relatively low cost. This
                  is also exemplified by their market shares on this route, with the AA-IAG JV



1763     This applies to Rome-Delhi (except in Summer 2023) and Rome-Sao Paulo (except in Winter 2022/23).
1764     This applies to Rome-Boston (except in Winter 2022/23), Rome-Buenos Aires, Rome-Tokyo (except
      Summer 2023), and Venice-New York.
1765    RFI 23, Annex Q7.
1766    IATA passenger data, RFI 36 Annex 100.
1767    IATA passenger data, RFI 36 Annex 100.
1768    RFI 23, Annex Q7.


                                    442

[PÁGINA PDF 445]
             having a market share equal to between 14% and 27% over the last six seasons
            and the Blue Skies JV having a market share equal to 10% to 35%.1769
          (c)  On the Naples-New York route (summer only),1770 Delta of the Blue Skies JV
               started a direct operation with five weekly frequencies in Summer 2024. While
                this direct entry is not reflected in the historical market share data, it is likely
                 that, given that passengers prefer direct flights over indirect flights, Delta will
            compete closely with United Airlines’ direct connection on this route, whereas
            ITA, which only operates  indirectly on  this  route,  will be a  less close
              competitor to United Airlines on this route.
(1826)  Second, the increment arising as a result of the Transaction is low (below 5%) to
        moderate (between 5% and 10%) on 6 out of 12 of these routes. Notably, based on
         the last four seasons, the increment is low on Athens-Washington (except in Summer
       2023 where it was 6%), Brussel-Tokyo, and Zurich-Cairo and moderate on Rome-
       Buenos Aires, Rome-Delhi, and Rome-Sao Paulo. In addition, on the Venice-New
       York the increment was slightly above 10% only in Winter 2022/23.
(1827)  Third, in addition to the route Naples-New York, the Parties face competition from
        competitors with a direct connection on the following routes. During both summer
       and winter seasons, Delta (from the Blue Skies JV) operates direct connections on
         the Rome-Boston and Venice-New York routes, Aerolíneas Argentinas on the Rome-
       Buenos Aires route, and LATAM Airlines on the Rome-Sao Paulo route.1771 For the
        reasons outlined in section 10.1.4, passengers prefer direct connections over indirect
        connections, and therefore these competitors are particularly strong competitors to
         the Parties on these routes.
(1828)  Fourth, while  the views of competitors and customers on  the impact of  the
        Transaction on  these  routes  are  overall mixed and  inconclusive,  the market
         investigation  did  not  reveal any  substantiated  competition concerns  for  these
          routes.1772
(1829)  Fifth, the Commission has taken into consideration multiple exceptional factors of
          this case, namely that ITA’s long-term competitiveness as a standalone carrier is
        highly uncertain (see section 7.2.2) and that, following the Transaction, ITA will
         retain some ability and incentive to compete against Lufthansa’s A++ joint venture
         partners, in particular due to the presence of MEF as a controlling shareholder (see
         section 10.1.1).
(1830)  In conclusion, the Transaction would not significantly impede effective competition
        with respect to the 12 direct / indirect overlapping routes identified above.

                     12.3.3.2. Competitive assessment
(1836)  For the reasons set out below, the Commission concludes that the Transaction would
        not significantly impede effective competition on these routes under any plausible
        market definition during both IATA Winter and Summer season:
(1837)  First, the Parties’ combined share is only moderately high (below 40%)1779 or below
         the dominance threshold (below 50%)1780 on 28 out of 38 of these routes in each of
         the  last  four complete IATA  seasons. On two  additional  routes,  the  Parties’

       combined share  is below or only slightly above 50% in most of the  last four
         seasons.1781
(1838)  Second, the increment arising as a result of the Transaction is low (below 5%)1782 to
        moderate (between 5% and 10%)1783 on 25 out of 38 of these routes.
(1839)  Third, on most of these routes (except those discussed in more detail below, see sixth
         point), the Parties’ combined market shares are below the dominance threshold with
          at most moderate increments (up to 10%) or the increment from the Transaction is
       low (<5%).
(1840)  Fourth, on most of these routes, the Parties will continue to face competition from
         several competitors with sizable market shares and, on many routes, the Parties will
        continue to face competition from at least one competitor with a market share that is
        higher or of similar magnitude to the Parties’ combined market share.
(1841)  Fifth, on some routes, the Parties face competition from competitors with a direct
        connection on the route. During the summer season only, American Airlines (from
         the AA-IAG JV) operates a direct connection on the Rome-Charlotte route, whereas
        Delta (from the Blue Skies JV) operates direct connections on the Athens-Boston and
        Rome-Dallas/Fort Worth routes. In addition, American Airlines operates a direct
        connection on the Rome-Dallas/Fort Worth route during both summer and winter
         seasons.1784 For the reasons outlined in section 10.1.4, passengers prefer direct
        connections  over  indirect  connections,  and  therefore  these  competitors  are
         particularly strong competitors to the Parties’ indirect connections on these routes.
(1842)  Sixth, the only indirect-indirect overlapping long-haul routes on which the Parties’
       combined market shares are very high (above 50%) in more than one of the last four
        complete seasons and where the increment from the Transaction is significant (over
       10%) are Palermo-New York, Catania-New York, and Naples-New York (winter
         only).
(1843)  In the first place, on the Palermo-New York route, where the Parties’ combined
        market share is high and the increment arising from the Transaction significant, the
        following countervailing factor applies. Neos has entered with a direct connection,
         starting with two weekly connections since Summer 2024 onwards.1785 For the
        reasons outlined in section 10.1.4,  airline passengers prefer  direct  flights over
         indirect flights and therefore Neos is likely to be a particularly strong competitor to
         the Parties’ indirect connections on this route.
(1844)  In the second place, on the route Catania-New York, where the Parties’ combined
        market share is high and the increment arising from the Transaction significant, the
        following countervailing factors apply. First, demand on this route during the winter
        seasons is particularly low (<8 000 in Winter 2022/23). Second, during the summer

         seasons, the other two joint ventures have a sizeable number of connections from
        Catania to their long-haul hubs in Europe. In particular, based on Summer 2024,
        Air France-KLM  (of  the Blue  Skies JV) has 13 average weekly  frequencies
        connecting Catania with its hubs in Amsterdam and Paris, whereas IAG (of the AA-
      IAG JV) has 16 average weekly frequencies connecting Catania with its hubs in
        Dublin, London and Madrid.1786 These short-haul connections can be used by
